listenings.title: Track 07. Magazine interview
intro: Bridget kollej jurnali uchun Eddiega intervyu topshirig'ini bermoqda; Eddie qaydlar yozadi. Avval qaydlarni o'qing va har bo'sh joy turini ayting (familiya, kasb, son, sana, telefon, manzil). Keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
transcript: BRIDGET: Hello, Eddie? It's Bridget.
EDDIE: Oh hi, Bridget.
BRIDGET: Listen, Eddie, are you still free to do an article for the college magazine?
EDDIE: Sure, is there anything in particular you'd like me to write about?

BRIDGET: Well, the next issue is about people's lives, you know, people who have done something interesting or exciting. Anyway, I've got someone lined up, and I was wondering if you could interview them and then write the article.
EDDIE: All right, that's fine with me.
BRIDGET: Great. Have you got a pen?
EDDIE: Yes.
BRIDGET: OK, take this down. His name is Tom Coogan.
EDDIE: Tom ...?
BRIDGET: Coogan. That's C-O-O-G-A-N. Got that?
EDDIE: Sure, and what does he do?
BRIDGET: He's a travel writer.
EDDIE: I don't think I've heard of him. What else can you tell me about him? How old is he? What's he written? That sort of thing.
BRIDGET: OK, he's 42 years old, er, and he's written ten or twelve books. Let me just check that. Uh huh, twelve books, including his latest. Oh, and he also presents a travel programme on TV.
EDDIE: All right.

BRIDGET: Now, his latest book is about a journey he made across the Gobi desert on horseback. It took him six months, apparently. Anyway, I think he'd like to talk about that, so make sure you ask lots of questions.
EDDIE: Fine, I'd better look at a copy. What's it called?
BRIDGET: It's called Has Anyone Seen My Horse? I've got a copy here which I can lend you.
EDDIE: OK, and why does he want to talk about that book in particular?
BRIDGET: It's just won him an award.
EDDIE: Really? What kind?
BRIDGET: Travel Book of the Year.
EDDIE: Oh, wow, that's pretty impressive.
BRIDGET: Exactly, so like I say, ask lots of questions about it. Now, I've arranged for you to meet him on 21st October. That's two weeks on Friday, is that OK?
EDDIE: It should be. Have you got a time for that?
BRIDGET: Not yet, he wants you to call him beforehand to arrange that. I'll give you his contact number. It's 0722, no, hang on, it's 0772 9214490.
EDDIE: 0772 9214490. And where am I supposed to meet him?
BRIDGET: He's suggested his place, which is good as it's not far from the college. It's 138 Lonsdale Avenue, Summertown. Lonsdale is L-O-N-S-D-A-L-E.
EDDIE: Yeah, I think I know where Lonsdale Avenue is. You did say 138, didn't you?

BRIDGET: Right. Oh, and I suggest that you take a look at his website as well. It's got loads of information, so you might want to ask him about some of his other trips. It's at www.tomcooganbooks.com.
EDDIE: All right. Thanks for that. I'll let you know how I get on.
BRIDGET: Great. Thanks, Eddie. Good luck.

tasks.title: Magazine interview — complete the notes (1–10)
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER
why: Harflab aytilgan: C-O-O-G-A-N. Ikki "O" ga e'tibor.
"He's a travel writer". Tuzoq: "presents a travel programme on TV" — qo'shimcha ish, asosiy kasb emas.
Avval "ten or twelve" — keyin tekshirib aniqlaydi: "Uh huh, twelve books". Tuzatishdan keyingi javob yoziladi.
"It took him six months". Tuzoq: "on horseback" — qanday usulda, vaqt emas.
Kitob nomi: "Has Anyone Seen My Horse?" — ikki so'z, bosh harflar bilan.
"Travel Book of the Year". Formada "Travel Book of" bor — qolgan qismi "the Year".
"I've arranged for you to meet him on 21st October". Tuzoq: "two weeks on Friday" — "Friday" formada bor, sana so'ralgan.
Tuzatish tuzog'i: "It's 0722, no, hang on, it's 0772 9214490". Oxirgi raqam yoziladi.
"138 Lonsdale Avenue ... L-O-N-S-D-A-L-E". Raqam + ikki so'z — chegara ichida (TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER). "Summertown" formada bor.
"I suggest that you take a look at his website". Tuzoq: www.tomcooganbooks.com — manzilni yozish shart emas; forma "his ___" deydi.
tasks.note: Tekshirishda: 3 va 8-savollarda so'zlovchi o'zini tuzatadi — oxirgi variant yoziladi; 7-savolda "Friday" qaydda bor, faqat sana yoziladi.

listenings.title: Language school enrolment
intro: Til kursiga yozilish. BIR MARTA tinglang; qaydlarni to'ldiring.
Ko'rsatma: ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
transcript: ADVISER: Good morning, Oakfield Language School. I'm Martin, the course adviser.
CALLER: Hello. I'd like some information about your English courses.
ADVISER: Of course. Are you interested in general English or exam preparation?
CALLER: Exam preparation — IELTS, if possible.
ADVISER: We run IELTS courses three times a year. The next one starts on the 4th of February.
CALLER: How long does it last?
ADVISER: Ten weeks. Classes are on Mondays and Wednesdays, from six to eight in the evening.
CALLER: And the price?
ADVISER: The full course is 340 pounds. There's a discount for anyone who pays before the 20th of January — 290.
CALLER: That's useful. How many students are in a class?
ADVISER: Never more than twelve. The average is about nine.
CALLER: Do I need a test before I join?
ADVISER: Yes, a short placement test online — it takes forty minutes. You need a score of at least 40 out of 60 for the IELTS group.
CALLER: What about materials?
ADVISER: The book is included, but you should bring a notebook and a dictionary. Paper dictionaries only in class, I'm afraid — no phones.
CALLER: Where exactly is the school?
ADVISER: We're at 14 Beaumont Road. That's B-E-A-U-M-O-N-T. The nearest station is Hollow Park, about six minutes on foot.
CALLER: And can I visit before I decide?
ADVISER: Certainly. We have open evenings every Thursday at seven. Just bring some identification — a passport is best.

listenings.title: Museum tour booking
intro: Muzeyga guruh ekskursiyasi buyurtmasi. BIR MARTA tinglang.
transcript: STAFF: City Museum, bookings department. How can I help?
TEACHER: Hello, I'm calling from Green Lane School. I'd like to book a tour for a group of students.
STAFF: Certainly. How many students, and what age?
TEACHER: Thirty-two students, all aged fourteen.
STAFF: And how many adults will come with them?
TEACHER: Four teachers. We also have one parent helper, so five adults in total.
STAFF: Fine. Which tour are you interested in? We offer the Ancient Egypt tour, the Science Gallery tour, and a mixed one called Highlights.
TEACHER: The Science Gallery, please. It fits our topic this term.
STAFF: Good choice. That tour lasts ninety minutes. Which date?
TEACHER: The 14th of March, if it's free. In the morning if possible.
STAFF: Let me see... the 14th is fully booked in the morning. I could offer you the afternoon, at two o'clock, or the morning of the 15th at ten.
TEACHER: The 15th at ten is better for us.
STAFF: The 15th at ten it is. The price is 6 pounds per student; teachers go free.
TEACHER: Is there a lunch area?
STAFF: Yes, groups can use the education room, but you have to book it separately. It's free, but only until one o'clock.
TEACHER: We'll take it. Anything we should tell the students?
STAFF: No large bags in the galleries — there are lockers by the entrance, and they need a one-pound coin. Photography is allowed except in the temporary exhibition.
TEACHER: Understood. Do we need to pay in advance?
STAFF: A deposit of 50 pounds within two weeks; the rest on the day.
TEACHER: Perfect. My name is Rachel Whitford, W-H-I-T-F-O-R-D, and my email is r.whitford@greenlane.ac.uk.

listenings.title: Cycling club information
intro: Velosiped klubi haqida ma'lumot. Uyda bir marta tinglang, keyin transkriptga qarang.
transcript: WOMAN: Riverside Cycling Club, Helen speaking.
MAN: Hi. A colleague told me about the club and I'd like to join.
WOMAN: Great. We have three groups: beginners, intermediate and racing. Which suits you?
MAN: I ride to work most days, but I've never done a long ride. Intermediate, maybe?
WOMAN: If you can do 40 kilometres without stopping, intermediate is fine. Beginners do 20.
MAN: I've done 45, so yes, intermediate.
WOMAN: The intermediate group meets on Saturdays at seven thirty, and on Wednesday evenings in summer only.
MAN: Where do you start from?
WOMAN: The car park behind the swimming pool, on Mill Street. Not the sports centre — people often go there by mistake.
MAN: Noted. What does membership cost?
WOMAN: It's 45 pounds a year, or 30 if you're a student or over sixty-five. That includes insurance.
MAN: Do I need special equipment?
WOMAN: A helmet is compulsory — we won't let you ride without one. Lights are essential in winter, and we recommend gloves. You don't need an expensive bike; most members ride ordinary ones.
MAN: Is there a trial ride before I pay?
WOMAN: Yes, your first two rides are free. After that we ask you to join.
MAN: And how many members are there?
WOMAN: Around 180 now. It was only 60 five years ago.
MAN: Right. How do I sign up?
WOMAN: Fill in the form on our website, riverside-cc dot org. Or come on Saturday and talk to me — I'm usually the one with the yellow jacket.

homework_intro: Bugun to'rtta qaydni birga to'ldirdik, endi beshinchisini — "Cycling club information" ni — uyda yolg'iz o'zingiz bajarasiz: audioni BIR MARTA qo'ying, to'xtatmang va 11 ta qaydni oxirigacha to'ldiring, bu 10–12 daqiqa vaqt oladi.
Javoblarni yozib bo'lgandan keyingina varaqning orqasidagi transkriptni oching va xatolaringizni qizil qalam bilan tuzating; oldin qarasangiz, mashqning ma'nosi qolmaydi.

Ikkinchi vazifa — "Chalg'ituvchi daftari": bugungi uchta skriptdan 10 ta noto'g'ri javobni ko'chirib yozasiz va har bir qatorda uni ochib bergan signal so'zni ko'rsatasiz — but, though, sorry, average kabi.
Eng ko'p xato shu yerda: ko'pchilik faqat "noto'g'ri" deb yozadi-yu, signal so'zni yozmaydi — signal so'zsiz qator hisobga olinmaydi.

Uchinchi vazifa — raqam va vaqt diktanti: men 15 ta narx, vaqt va masofani o'qiyman, siz faqat raqamni yozasiz; 13/30 va 15/50 juftliklarida urg'uni diqqat bilan tinglang: thirTEEN — urg'u oxirida, THIRty — boshida.
Uchala vazifani bitta daftarda bajaring va keyingi darsning boshida daftarni menga topshiring; men tekshirib, coinni o'sha kuni yozaman.

The lesson costs thirty pounds.

homework.note: 15 dan 13 tasi to'g'ri bo'lsa — bajarilgan. Gaplarni tabiiy tezlikda o'qing; -teen sonlarda uzun "ii" va oxiridagi "n" aniq eshitilsin (ot oldida urg'u siljishi mumkin: "thirteen POUNDS"). O'quvchi varag'ida faqat 1–15 raqamlari bo'ladi.

kahoot.q: Notes: 'Bus leaves from the ___ at 8.15'. What kind of word is missing?
kahoot.explain: "the ... at" orasida ot turadi va "leaves from" joyni so'raydi — demak joy nomi kerak.

kahoot.q: The instruction says ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER. Which answer breaks the rule?
kahoot.explain: "city centre" — ikki so'z; uzun bo'lsa ham bitta so'z (accommodation) yoki raqam (350) chegarani buzmaydi.

kahoot.q: You hear: 'It's usually £20, but for students it's £12.' Notes: 'Student price: £___'. Answer?
kahoot.explain: "But" dan keyingi son talabalar uchun aytilgan; 20 — odatdagi narx, ya'ni chalg'ituvchi.

kahoot.q: You hear: 'Meet at the bank — no, sorry, at the post office.' Where do they meet?
kahoot.explain: "No, sorry" — tuzatish signali: oxirgi, tuzatilgan variant yoziladi.

kahoot.q: Which phrase usually signals that a speaker is correcting information?
kahoot.explain: "Sorry, I mean..." dan keyin to'g'ri ma'lumot keladi; qolganlari tuzatish emas.

kahoot.q: The notes say 'Cost: £___'. Which phrase might you hear instead of 'cost'?
kahoot.explain: Audio ko'pincha qaydlardagi so'zni boshqacha aytadi: cost = price = charge.

kahoot.q: You hear: 'Please bring two towels.' Notes: 'Bring two ___'. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: Ko'plik "s" javobning bir qismi; "two" qaydda bor, uni takrorlamang.

kahoot.q: A surname is spelled out for you, but you write one letter wrong. What do you get?
kahoot.explain: IELTS da yarim ball yo'q: bitta harf xato bo'lsa ham javob noto'g'ri hisoblanadi.

kahoot.q: You hear 'a quarter past nine'. The limit is ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: Vaqtni raqam bilan yozing: "quarter past nine" — 3 so'z, chegaradan oshadi; 9.45 esa "quarter to ten".

kahoot.q: While listening, you miss the answer to one gap. What should you do?
options: Leave it and move on to the next gap
Stop and try to remember it
Ask for the audio to be repeated
kahoot.explain: Audio to'xtamaydi: o'tkazib yuborilgan katakda qolsangiz, keyingi javob ham o'tib ketadi.

kahoot.q: When you transfer or check your answers at the end, what should you do with an empty gap?
kahoot.explain: Ko'chirish (kompyuterda — oxirgi tekshirish) vaqtida bo'sh katak qoldirmang: noto'g'ri javob uchun ball ayirilmaydi, taxmin esa to'g'ri chiqishi mumkin.

kahoot.q: In IELTS Listening, do you need to calculate an answer, e.g. 40 - 8?
kahoot.explain: Javob audioda aniq aytiladi; hisoblash kerak bo'lib tuyulsa, son keyinroq aytilishini kuting.

kahoot.q: An 'expedition' is...
options: a short walk in a park
kahoot.explain: Expedition — ekspeditsiya: maqsadli, oldindan tashkil etilgan uzoq safar.

kahoot.q: A 'remote' village is...
kahoot.explain: Remote — chekka, shahar va yo'llardan uzoq.

kahoot.q: If you are 'fluent' in Spanish, you...
kahoot.explain: Fluent — tilda erkin, qiynalmasdan gapiradigan.

kahoot.q: 'I can get by in French' means...
options: I can manage in simple situations
I speak it perfectly, like a native
I don't speak French at all
I teach French at a school
kahoot.explain: Get by — eplab ketmoq: oddiy vaziyatlarda tushuntira olish, mukammal emas.

kahoot.q: A 'discount' is...
kahoot.explain: Discount — chegirma, narxning kamaytirilgani.

kahoot.q: When you pay a 'deposit', you pay...
kahoot.explain: Deposit — oldindan to'lov: narxning bir qismi hozir, qolgani keyin to'lanadi.

kahoot.q: If a hotel is 'fully booked', ...
kahoot.explain: Fully booked — barcha joylar band, bo'sh xona qolmagan.

kahoot.q: If a uniform is 'compulsory' at a school, it is...
kahoot.explain: Compulsory — majburiy, qoida talab qiladi; "recommended" esa faqat tavsiya.

lessons.title: Reading: True / False / Not Given
lessons.grammar_topic: True / False / Not Given (fakt savollari)
lessons.book_ref: Jony Academy materiali — mualliflik matnlari, skriptlar va mashqlar.
objectives: TRUE, FALSE va NOT GIVEN orasidagi farqni aniq ajratish.
FALSE (matn boshqacha aytadi) va NOT GIVEN (matn umuman aytmaydi) farqini isbot bilan ko'rsatish.
Savoldagi cheklovchi so'zlarni (all, only, never, most, always) topish — bu diqqat signali, javob emas: matnda aynan shu ma'no bormi, tekshiriladi.
Javobni faqat matndan olish: dunyo haqidagi bilim yoki mantiq bilan javob berilmaydi.
3 ta Band 4–5 matnda ishlab, har javob uchun matndagi gapni ko'rsatish.
materials: Reading #6 "Mau Piailug, ocean navigator" matni savollari bilan (3 + 7 savol) — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa, savollar matn bilan bir varaqda.
Reading #9 "Sylvia Earle, underwater hero" matni short answer va T/F/NG savollari bilan — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa.
"The accident that gave us the microwave" va "The woman who mapped the ocean floor" matnlari, glossary qatori matn ostida chop etilsin — har juftlikka bittadan nusxa, ular juftlikda ishlanadi.
"The first photograph" matni va 8 ta savoli — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa; dars oxirida uyga vazifa uchun tarqatiladi, sinfda ochilmaydi.

Uchta kartochka — TRUE, FALSE, NOT GIVEN — qalin qog'ozga yozib qirqing, har juftlikka bitta to'plam: "Uch ustun mashqi"da o'quvchi javobni kartochka ko'tarib beradi. Shu mashqning 6 ta matn-savol juftligi ustoz varag'ida chop etilgan bo'lsin.

Doskada dars boshlanishidan oldin uchta ustun yozib qo'yilsin: TRUE — "bir xil", FALSE — "qarshi", NOT GIVEN — "yo'q"; yoniga to'rtinchi ustun — "isbot: qaysi xatboshi, qaysi gap". Vaqtni o'lchash uchun telefonda sekundomer (7 savolga 10 daqiqa).
timeline: Salomlashish, o'tgan darsdagi savol turini 3 savolda eslatish
Ustoz doskada: TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN qoidasi, uch ustun + isbot ustuni, cheklovchi so'zlar (diqqat signali), tipik xatolar
Uch ustun mashqi (6 juftlik, kartochkalar bilan): o'quvchi javob va sababini aytadi
Matndagi va savoldagi so'zlar jadvali; o'quvchilar ovoz chiqarib topadi
1–3-savollar birga, so'ng 7 savol mustaqil (10 daqiqa), isbot bilan tekshiriladi; paraphrase juftlari
Short answer (4) + T/F/NG (5) mustaqil, so'ng tekshirish: 2 va 5-savol tuzoqlari
Juftlikda, vaqt bilan (har matnga 8 savol), so'ng "Xato turini ayting" va "Isbot qatori" tahlili
Xatolar daftari: har xato javob sababi bilan yoziladi
"The first photograph" matni uyga tarqatiladi; FALSE/NOT GIVEN ro'yxati va cheklovchi so'zlar vazifasi tushuntiriladi; xatolar daftari to'ldiriladi

intro: TRUE — matn savol bilan BIR XIL ma'noni aytadi (boshqa so'z bilan bo'lsa ham).
FALSE — matn savolga QARSHI ma'noni aytadi: son boshqa, vaqt boshqa, inkor bor.
NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqida ma'lumot YO'Q. Ehtimol to'g'ridir, lekin matn aytmagan.
Eng ko'p xato: o'quvchi o'zidan bilgan narsani qo'shadi. IELTSda faqat matn hakam.

Cheklovchi so'zlar: all, every, only, never, always, the first, the most. Savolda shu so'zlar bo'lsa, matnni juda diqqat bilan tekshiring. Bu — diqqat signali, javob emas: matn ham shuni aytsa — TRUE, boshqacha aytsa — FALSE, umuman aytmasa — NOT GIVEN.
Solishtirish savollari ("X is bigger than Y") uchun ikkala raqamni ham toping. Faqat bittasi berilgan bo'lsa — NOT GIVEN.
Fikr (opinion) savollarida "the writer believes..." bo'lsa, matndan muallif fikri aytilgan joyni qidiring; faqat fakt bo'lsa — NOT GIVEN.
Javoblar matn tartibida keladi, shuning uchun 3-savolni 2 va 4 oralig'idan qidiring.
formulas: Savolni o'qing va kalit so'zni belgilang
presentation: Matnda "about 40", savolda "more than 50" — javob?
FALSE. Raqamlar bir-biriga qarshi.
Matnda "she studied in Paris", savolda "she studied in Paris for five years" — javob?
NOT GIVEN. Muddat aytilmagan.
Savolda "the only country" so'zi bor, matnda "one of the countries" — javob?
FALSE. "Only" va "one of" bir xil emas.
Men bilaman, bu to'g'ri. NOT GIVEN deb yozaymi?
Ha, agar matnda bu haqida hech narsa bo'lmasa. Matn aytgan bo'lsa — TRUE yoki FALSE; o'z bilimingiz hisobga olinmaydi.
"The writer thinks..." savoliga qanday qaraymiz?
Matnda muallif bahosi bormi? Bo'lmasa — NOT GIVEN.
YES/NO/NOT GIVEN bilan farqi bormi?
Bor: TRUE/FALSE — faktlar, YES/NO — muallif fikri. Ishlash usuli bir xil.
notes: Doskada uchta ustun: TRUE — "bir xil", FALSE — "qarshi", NOT GIVEN — "yo'q". Har javobda o'quvchi ustunni ko'rsatadi.
Har javob uchun matndagi qatorni ko'rsatish majburiy: "3-xatboshi, 2-gap".
NOT GIVEN javoblarini alohida yig'ing: o'quvchilar ularni eng ko'p xato qiladi.
Vaqt: 13 savolga 20 daqiqa — bu darsda 6–8 savolga 10 daqiqa.
mistakes: FALSE va NOT GIVEN ni almashtirish
Bu so'z ma'noni o'zgartirishi mumkin — matn bilan solishtiring
Faqat bitta so'zga qarab javob berish

class_ex.instr: Ustoz gap o'qiydi, o'quvchi TRUE/FALSE/NOT GIVEN deb javob beradi va sababini aytadi.
items: Matn: "The factory opened in 1998." Savol: "The factory opened before 2000."
Matn: "The factory opened in 1998." Savol: "The factory opened in 1989."
Matn: "The factory opened in 1998." Savol: "The factory cost 3 million dollars."
Matn: "Most students walk to school." Savol: "All students walk to school."
Matn: "The museum is open at weekends." Savol: "The museum is busiest on Sundays."

why: 1998 < 2000 — bir xil ma'no.
Raqamlar qarshi.
Narx haqida hech narsa yo'q.
"Most" va "all" bir xil emas.
Matnda faqat ochiq kunlar aytilgan; qaysi kuni eng ko'p odam bo'lishi haqida ma'lumot yo'q. Diqqat: savol "open on Sundays" bo'lsa — TRUE bo'lardi (weekends = shanba + yakshanba).
"First" shu ma'noni beradi.

readings.title: Reading #6. Mau Piailug, ocean navigator
text: Mau sailed from Hawaii to Tahiti using traditional methods.

In early 1976, Mau Piailug, a fisherman, led an expedition in which he sailed a traditional Polynesian boat across 2,500 miles of ocean from Hawaii to Tahiti. The Polynesian Voyaging Society had organised the expedition. Its purpose was to find out if seafarers in the distant past could have _found their way_ from _one island to the other_ without navigational instruments, or whether the islands had been populated by accident. At the time, Mau was _the only man alive who knew how to navigate_ just by observing the stars, the wind and the sea.

He had never before sailed to Tahiti, which was a long way to the south. However, he understood how the wind and the sea behave around islands, so he was confident he could find his way. The voyage took him and his crew a month to complete and he did it without a compass or charts.

His grandfather began the task of teaching him how to navigate when he was still a baby. He showed him pools of water on the beach to teach him how the behaviour of the waves and wind changed in different places. Later, Mau used a circle of stones to _memorise_ _the positions of the stars_. Each stone was laid out in the sand to represent a star.

The voyage proved that Hawaii's first inhabitants came in small boats and navigated by reading the sea and the stars. Mau himself became a keen teacher, passing on his traditional secrets to people of other cultures so that his knowledge would not be lost. He explained the positions of the stars to his students, but he allowed them to write things down because he knew they would never be able to remember everything as he had done.
paraphrases: from one island to the other
the only man alive who knew how to navigate

tasks.instr: TRUE — matn bilan bir xil; FALSE — matnga qarshi; NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqida ma'lumot yo'q.
items: The purpose of Mau's voyage was to find the quickest route between Hawaii and Tahiti.
The purpose of Mau's voyage was to find out if navigating between islands had been possible in the past.
Mau's boat belonged to the Polynesian Voyaging Society.
why: Maqsad boshqa: "to find out if seafarers in the distant past could have found their way ... without navigational instruments". Eng tez yo'l haqida emas.
"Navigate" = "found their way", "between islands" = "from one island to the other", "in the past" = "in the distant past".
Matnda Jamiyat ekspeditsiyani TASHKIL QILGANI aytilgan ("had organised the expedition"). Qayiq kimniki ekani aytilmagan.

readings.title: Reading #9. Sylvia Earle, underwater hero
readings.qtype: Short answer + True / False / Not Given
text: She has spent her working life studying the world's oceans. Sylvia Earle is an underwater explorer and marine biologist who was born in the USA in 1935. She became interested in the world's oceans from an early age. As a child, she liked to stand on the beach for hours and look at the sea, wondering what it must be like under the surface.

When she was 16, she finally got a chance to make her first dive. It was this dive that inspired her to become an underwater explorer. Since then, she has spent more than 6,500 hours under water, and has led more than seventy expeditions worldwide. She has also walked on the sea floor in a special diving suit, reaching a record-breaking depth of 381 metres.

In 1970, she became famous around the world when she became the captain of the first all-female team to live under water. The team spent two weeks in an underwater 'house'. The research they carried out showed the damage that pollution was causing to marine life, and especially to coral reefs. Her team also studied the problem of over-fishing. Fishing methods meant that people were catching too many fish, Earle warned, and many species were in danger of becoming extinct.

Since then she has written several books and magazine articles in which she suggests ways of reducing the damage that is being done to the world's oceans. One way, she believes, is to rely on fish farms for seafood, and reduce the amount of fishing that is done out at sea. Although she no longer eats seafood herself, she realises the importance it plays in our diets. It would be wrong to tell people they should stop eating fish from the sea, she says. However, they need to reduce the impact they are having on the ocean's supplies.

tasks.title: Short answer questions (1–4)
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the passage
items: What career did Sylvia decide to follow after her first dive?
How far under water did she go in order to break a world record?
What was causing harm to everything living in the sea?
Where does Sylvia think we should get our fish from?
why: "It was this dive that inspired her to become an underwater explorer". "Decide to follow a career" = "inspired her to become".

"She has also walked on the sea floor ..., reaching a record-breaking depth of 381 metres". Raqam + o'lchov birligi — chegara ichida (TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER); birlikni matndagidek ko'plikda yozing: "metres".
"The damage that pollution was causing to marine life". "Harm" = "damage", "everything living in the sea" = "marine life".
"One way, she believes, is to rely on fish farms for seafood". "Think" = "believes".

tasks.title: TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN (1–5)
tasks.instr: Har javob uchun matndagi gapni ko'rsating.
items: Sylvia Earle lives in the USA.
Until 1970, nobody had lived underwater before.
Sylvia Earle was worried about the amount of fish that were being caught.
Her books offer some solutions to marine problems.
She thinks people should avoid eating seafood.
why: Matnda u AQShda TUG'ILGANI aytilgan ("born in the USA"), hozir qayerda yashashi aytilmagan. Tug'ilgan joy ≠ yashash joyi.
Matnda "the first ALL-FEMALE team to live under water" deyilgan — birinchi ayollar jamoasi. Undan oldin erkaklar yashaganmi-yo'qmi, aytilmagan. Cheklovchi so'zga e'tibor bering.
"People were catching too many fish, Earle warned". "Worried" = "warned", "amount" = "too many".
"Books ... in which she suggests ways of reducing the damage". "Offer solutions" = "suggests ways".
"It would be wrong to tell people they should stop eating fish from the sea". O'zi dengiz mahsuloti yemaydi, lekin boshqalarga buni tavsiya qilmaydi — tuzoq.
tasks.note: 2 va 5-savollar eng yaxshi tuzoq misoli. 2-savolda "all-female" so'zi, 5-savolda uning o'zi va boshqalar farqi javobni belgilaydi.

readings.title: The accident that gave us the microwave
text: In 1945 an American engineer called Percy Spencer was testing a magnetron, a device used in radar equipment during the Second World War. While he stood in front of the machine, he noticed that a chocolate bar in his pocket had melted. Spencer had left school at twelve and had no university degree, but he had already registered dozens of patents.

Curious, he sent for a bag of popcorn kernels and held them near the magnetron. They popped. The next morning he tried an egg, which exploded in the face of a colleague who leaned over it. Spencer understood that the waves were heating the water inside the food, and that the heat came from the inside out.

The first commercial microwave oven went on sale in 1947. It was nearly two metres tall, weighed 340 kilograms and cost about 5,000 dollars — as much as a house in some parts of the country. Restaurants and ships bought a few, but ordinary families did not.

Everything changed in 1967, when a smaller model appeared for less than 500 dollars. By 1975 microwaves were selling faster than gas cookers in the United States, and today they are found in more than 90 per cent of American homes. Spencer himself received no extra payment for the invention beyond the company's standard bonus of two dollars.

tasks.title: True / False / Not Given
items: Spencer was working on radar equipment when he made his discovery.
Spencer had a university degree in engineering.
The egg experiment injured Spencer's colleague.
The first microwave oven was cheaper than a house everywhere in the country.
The first microwave oven was sold to restaurants.
Microwaves outsold gas cookers in the US by 1975.
More than 90 per cent of homes worldwide have a microwave today.
Spencer later became rich from the invention.
why: "Testing a magnetron, a device used in radar equipment".
"Had left school at twelve and had no university degree".
Tuxum portlagani aytilgan, lekin jarohat haqida hech narsa yo'q.
"As much as a house in some parts of the country" — ba'zi joylarda uyga teng.
"Restaurants and ships bought a few".
"By 1975 microwaves were selling faster than gas cookers".

Matnda faqat "more than 90 per cent of American homes" deyilgan; dunyo bo'yicha raqam umuman yo'q — qamrov o'zgargan, ma'lumot yo'q. FALSE bo'lishi uchun matn dunyo haqida boshqa raqam aytishi kerak edi.
"Received no extra payment ... beyond the company's standard bonus of two dollars".

"90 per cent worldwide" savolida xato turi

NOT GIVEN.

American homes ≠ worldwide; matn dunyo haqida hech narsa demaydi — NOT GIVEN.

readings.title: The woman who mapped the ocean floor
text: When Marie Tharp finished her geology degree in 1944, American universities were short of male students because of the war, and for the first time women were accepted onto the course. After graduating she moved to New York and found work at Columbia University, where she was given a desk but not a place on the research ships: women were not allowed on board until 1965.

Her colleague Bruce Heezen collected measurements of ocean depth from the Atlantic; Tharp turned thousands of numbers into pictures. Working by hand, she drew the shape of the sea floor, line by line, on long sheets of paper. In 1952 she noticed something nobody expected: a deep valley running along the middle of the underwater mountain chain.

Heezen called her idea "girl talk", because it supported the theory of continental drift, which most scientists then rejected. For almost a year he refused to publish it. Only after the same valley appeared in recordings of underwater earthquakes did he agree that she was right. The discovery became one of the main pieces of evidence for plate tectonics, the idea that the Earth's surface is made of moving plates.

When the discovery was first announced in 1956, Tharp's name did not appear, although it was based on her drawings. Her work later led to a famous painted map of the whole ocean floor, published in 1977. Recognition came late: in 1997, when she was in her seventies, the Library of Congress named her one of the four greatest cartographers of the twentieth century.

tasks.title: True / False / Not Given
items: Women were admitted to the geology course because of a shortage of men.
Tharp worked on research ships from the beginning of her career.
Tharp and Heezen were married.
Tharp used a computer to draw the sea floor.
Heezen accepted her discovery immediately.
Earthquake recordings supported Tharp's discovery.
The 1977 map sold more copies than any other scientific map.
Tharp received an important honour when she was in her seventies.
why: "Universities were short of male students because of the war, and for the first time women were accepted".
"Women were not allowed on board until 1965".
Faqat hamkasb ekani aytilgan; oilaviy holat haqida hech narsa yo'q.
"Working by hand, she drew the shape of the sea floor".
"For almost a year he refused to publish it".
"Only after the same valley appeared in recordings of underwater earthquakes".
Sotuv haqida ma'lumot yo'q.
"In 1997, when she was in her seventies, the Library of Congress named her one of the four greatest cartographers" — "important honour" = shu e'tirof.

readings.title: The first photograph
text: The oldest surviving photograph was taken in 1826 or 1827 by a French inventor, Joseph Nicéphore Niépce, from an upstairs window of his house in Burgundy. The picture shows the roofs of farm buildings and a tree. To make it, Niépce covered a metal plate with a kind of natural tar which hardens in light, and left the plate inside a wooden box with a lens for at least eight hours — some experts believe several days.

Niépce called the process heliography, from the Greek words for "sun" and "writing". He was not trying to make art: his first aim had been to copy printed pictures cheaply. He worked alone for years, spending much of his small income on materials, and received no public attention during his life.

In 1829 he agreed to work with Louis Daguerre, a painter from Paris. Niépce died four years later, and in 1839 Daguerre announced a faster process, the daguerreotype, which needed only a few minutes. The French government bought the invention and gave it to the world; Daguerre became famous, while Niépce's name was almost forgotten for a century.

The original plate was lost for many years and rediscovered in a London storeroom in 1952. It is now kept in Texas in a sealed case filled with a gas that protects it from air. Visitors often say it is difficult to see anything at all: the image is pale, and the light in the photograph comes from both sides, because the sun moved across the sky while the picture was being made.

"From an upstairs window".
"At least eight hours — some experts believe several days" — kelishmovchilik bor.
"He was not trying to make art".
Daromadini sarflagani aytilgan; uy sotilgani haqida hech narsa yo'q.
"A faster process ... which needed only a few minutes".
"Rediscovered in a London storeroom in 1952".
"It is now kept in Texas".

Eng ko'p uchraydigan xato shu: "men bilaman, bu to'g'ri" deb TRUE yozish — matn aytmagan bo'lsa, javob NOT GIVEN. Daftarni keyingi darsga to'liq yozilgan holda olib keling, dars boshida har javobingizdan matndagi qatorni so'rayman.

kahoot.q: In TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN, a statement is TRUE when...
options: the text says the same thing
you know it is true in real life
the text does not mention it
it uses exactly the same words
kahoot.explain: TRUE — matn xuddi shu ma'noni aytadi (ko'pincha boshqa so'zlar bilan); o'z bilimingiz hisobga olinmaydi.

kahoot.q: When is the answer NOT GIVEN?
kahoot.explain: NOT GIVEN — matnda bu haqida ma'lumot yo'q; qarama-qarshi gap bo'lsa — FALSE.

kahoot.q: Text: 'The bridge took about four years to build.' Statement: 'The bridge was built in less than two years.'
options: FALSE – four years, not under two
NOT GIVEN – 'about' is not an exact number
NOT GIVEN – no dates are given
kahoot.explain: "About four years" taxminiy bo'lsa ham, "less than two years" ga aniq qarshi — FALSE.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Ali studied medicine in London.' Statement: 'Ali studied medicine in London for six years.'
options: NOT GIVEN – no length is stated
kahoot.explain: Matnda muddat aytilmagan: savoldagi qo'shimcha tafsilot (six years) tekshirib bo'lmaydi — NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Some visitors arrive by train; the rest come by bus.' Statement: 'All visitors arrive by train.'
options: NOT GIVEN – no numbers are given
kahoot.explain: Matn "some" deydi va qolganlari avtobusda kelishini aytadi; savoldagi "all" matnga qarshi — FALSE.

kahoot.q: A statement contains 'only', 'all' or 'never'. What should you do?
options: Ignore it – it is not important
kahoot.explain: Cheklovchi so'z — diqqat signali, javob emas: matn ham shuni aytsa TRUE, boshqacha aytsa FALSE, aytmasa NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Only members can use the pool.' Statement: 'The pool is open to members only.'
options: TRUE – the text says the same
NOT GIVEN – no times are given
kahoot.explain: "Only" har doim FALSE emas: bu yerda matn ham aynan shuni aytadi — TRUE.

kahoot.q: Text: 'The festival takes place every July.' Statement: 'The festival is popular with tourists.' You know it is popular. Answer?
options: NOT GIVEN – the text says nothing
FALSE – the text is about July
kahoot.explain: IELTS da faqat matn hakam: matn mashhurlik haqida gapirmagan — NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: You found the answers to Q2 and Q4. Where should you look for the answer to Q3?
options: At the start of the text
kahoot.explain: T/F/NG savollari matn tartibida keladi: 3-savol 2 va 4-javoblar oralig'ida.

kahoot.q: Text: 'The new hall seats 500 people.' Statement: 'The new hall is bigger than the old one.'
options: NOT GIVEN – no size for the old hall
TRUE – 500 is a lot of seats
FALSE – the old hall was bigger
TRUE – new halls are always the biggest
kahoot.explain: Solishtirish uchun ikkala son kerak; eski zal haqida ma'lumot yo'q — NOT GIVEN.

kahoot.q: YES / NO / NOT GIVEN questions test the writer's views. What do TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN questions test?
kahoot.explain: TRUE/FALSE/NOT GIVEN — matndagi faktlar, YES/NO/NOT GIVEN — muallif fikri; ishlash usuli bir xil.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Tom never misses a chance to play football.' Statement: 'Tom never plays football.'
options: FALSE – he plays whenever he can
NOT GIVEN – no days are given
kahoot.explain: Ikkala gapda "never" bor, lekin ma'no teskari: u o'ynash imkonini qo'ldan bermaydi — FALSE.

kahoot.q: To 'navigate' means to...
options: build a boat out of wood
kahoot.explain: Navigate — yo'nalishni aniqlab, kerakli joyga yetib bormoq.

kahoot.q: The 'inhabitants' of an island are the people who...
kahoot.explain: Inhabitant — o'sha joyda yashovchi, aholi.

kahoot.q: An 'extinct' animal...
kahoot.explain: Extinct — qirilib ketgan: bu turdan birorta ham tirik qolmagan.

kahoot.q: A 'curious' child wants to...
kahoot.explain: Curious — qiziquvchan, yangi narsalarni bilishni istaydigan.

kahoot.q: An inventor gets a 'patent' to...
kahoot.explain: Patent — ixtironi boshqalar ruxsatsiz ishlatmasligi uchun beriladigan hujjat.

kahoot.q: When a new product 'goes on sale', it...
kahoot.explain: Go on sale — sotuvga chiqmoq, sotib olish mumkin bo'ladi.

kahoot.q: 'Evidence' is information that...
kahoot.explain: Evidence — dalil: biror narsa to'g'riligini ko'rsatadigan ma'lumot.

kahoot.q: If scientists 'reject' a theory, they...
kahoot.explain: Reject — rad etmoq, qabul qilmaslik (= did not accept).

lessons.title: Reading: Diagram Labelling
lessons.grammar_topic: Diagram labelling — chizma va rasmni belgilash
lessons.vocab_topic: Texnologiya va qurilmalar: qismlar va joylashuv
lessons.book_ref: Jony Academy mualliflik matnlari ("Inside a wind turbine", "How a vacuum flask keeps drinks hot", "The parts of a traditional water mill") va mashqlar; Reading #10 "The electric revolution" — Complete IELTS Bands 4–5 (Cambridge), Unit 3 "Getting from A to B", 29-bet; Reading #11 "The Boeing 787" — Complete IELTS Bands 4–5 Workbook (Cambridge), Unit 3, 18-bet (qo'shimcha mashq, chizmasi bilan).
objectives: Chizmadagi belgini matndagi tavsif bilan bog'lash: qism nomi, joylashuvi, vazifasi.
Joy va yo'nalish predloglarini o'qish: above, below, beneath, at the top, on either side, through, into.
Diagram labelling javoblari odatda (USUALLY) matn tartibida kelishini bilish va shundan foydalanish.
Chizma turini farqlash: qurilma sxemasi, jarayon sxemasi, joy rejasi.
3 ta Band 4–5 matnda mustaqil ishlash va har javobni izohlash.
materials: Doskaga dars boshlanishidan oldin oddiy elektr velosiped chizmasi: rom, o'rindiq, o'rindiq ostidagi kichik motor, zanjir, ikki g'ildirak (shinada kichik havo klapani — valve), rul, rulga mahkamlangan chiroq va rulning ikki yonidagi ikkita ko'zgu — belgilarsiz, faqat chiziqlar; "Predlog mashqi" shu chizma ustida og'zaki bajariladi (mashqdagi 6 gapning har biri chizmadagi qismga tayanadi).

Doska chetiga predloglar ro'yxati: above, below/beneath, inside, through, between, on either side, at the top of, at the base of — dars oxirigacha o'chirilmaydi, uchala matnda ham shu ro'yxatga qaytiladi.
Reading #10 "The electric revolution" matni va elektromobil chizmasi (ielts5_07_electric_car.jpg) — har juftlikka bitta nusxa; chizmadagi 1–6 belgilar bo'sh holda chop etilsin.

"Inside a wind turbine" (9 belgi) va "How a vacuum flask keeps drinks hot" (7 belgi) matnlari — har o'quvchiga bittadan nusxa; glossary qatori (nacelle, hub, blade / stopper, pad, case) matn ostida ko'rinib tursin, bu so'zlar o'quvchiga mutlaqo yangi.
Reading #11 "The Boeing 787" matni va samolyot chizmasi (ielts5_07_boeing_787.jpg) — har juftlikka bitta nusxa; eng qiyin mashq, faqat dastlabki uch matn tugagach tarqatiladi.

Uyga vazifa to'plami, dars oxirida tarqatiladi: "The parts of a traditional water mill" matni (9 belgi) va 15 gapli predlog testi — har o'quvchiga bittadan, ustiga "O'z chizmangiz" uchun bo'sh A4 varaq; har o'quvchida oddiy qalam va o'chirg'ich bo'lsin (chizmaga belgi qalam bilan qo'yiladi).

Grammatika bo'limi: qoida, 6 bosqich, savol-javob, tipik xatolar
Sinf mashqi: doskadagi velosiped chizmasida 6 gap og'zaki; o'quvchi har predlogni chizmada ko'rsatadi

How a vacuum flask keeps drinks hot
Vaqt bilan (8 daqiqa, IELTS tezligi): 7 belgi + "Uch yo'l" tahlili
Eng qiyin mashq (1–7), faqat dastlabki uch matndan keyin; vaqt yetmasa — uyga qo'shimcha

Uyga: water mill matni (9 belgi), "O'z chizmangiz", 15 gapli predlog testi — vazifa tushuntiriladi

intro: Diagram labelling — matndagi tavsifni rasmga ko'chirish. Javob deyarli har doim OT (qism nomi) bo'ladi.
Avval chizmaga qarang: nima tasvirlangan, qaysi qismlar allaqachon nomlangan? Nomlangan qismlar — langar.
Keyin matndan o'sha nomlangan qismni toping. Javob shu jumlaning yonida turadi.
Joy predloglari eng muhim: above (ustida), below/beneath (ostida), inside (ichida), on either side (ikki yonida), at the base (tagida), through (orqali).
Yo'nalish so'zlari jarayon sxemasida keladi: enters, passes, flows into, is carried to, comes out of.
Javob so'z chegarasidan oshmasin: "ONE WORD ONLY" bo'lsa, "metal ring" emas, "ring".
Diagram labelling savollari odatda (USUALLY) matn tartibida joylashadi: topilgan javobdan keyin qidiring, topilmasa nomlangan qismlarga qayting.
presentation: Javob qanday so'z turkumi bo'ladi?

readings.title: Reading #10. The electric revolution
readings.source: Complete IELTS Bands 4–5 (Cambridge), Unit 3 "Getting from A to B", 29-bet (Reading 1)
text: Your next car may be electric. We look at the technologies that will bring the revolution.

The main reasons why electric cars are not more popular at present are their price and their relatively small range. Existing battery systems only allow electric cars to travel a distance of between 100 and 160 km. However, this distance may not be a problem for urban drivers. A recent Sydney study reported that 70 percent of journeys were 30 km or less, and recent data from the US suggests that 77 percent of trips taken there are 48 km or less.

An innovative company called Better Place is aiming to make electric cars an option for all drivers. It wants to see existing vehicles replaced by electric vehicles which, it says, offer a number of benefits. Firstly, they can be powered by renewable energy which produces zero emissions. What is more, electric motors are more efficient and can convert more than 90 percent of power into movement, whereas the efficiency of diesel or petrol engines is less than 20 percent. To achieve its aim, Better Place plans to use technology which is already available.

The plan is simple but revolutionary. It starts with the installation of a home charge point, and through this, the vehicle will be plugged into the electricity grid whenever it is in the garage, typically at night. In the morning, with a fully charged battery, the car is capable of as much as 160 km in urban motoring conditions. In addition to the home charge point, the battery can be topped up by charge points at work and at supermarkets.

The battery is linked to a control centre by smart technology inside the vehicle. Better Place can then ensure that the car is charged with electricity from renewable sources at the cheapest price. For longer trips, a navigation system directs the driver to the nearest switch station, where the depleted battery can be replaced with a charged one by a robot within a couple of minutes.

the depleted battery can be replaced

readings.title: Inside a wind turbine
text: A modern wind turbine looks simple from a distance, but it contains more than eight thousand parts. The structure stands on a concrete base, sometimes twenty metres across, which is buried under the ground. Above this rises the tower, a hollow steel tube with a ladder and, in larger machines, a small lift inside.

At the top of the tower sits a box about the size of a bus. This box is called the nacelle, and it holds the working parts of the machine. Attached to the front of the nacelle is the hub, and three blades are fixed to the hub. Each blade is made of glass fibre and can be longer than eighty metres — longer than the wing of a large aircraft.

Inside the nacelle, the slow turning of the blades, about fifteen times a minute, is passed to a gearbox, which increases the speed to around 1,500 turns a minute. The fast shaft then drives the generator, where movement becomes electricity. Behind the generator, at the back of the nacelle, a small weather station measures wind speed and direction; a motor called the yaw drive turns the whole nacelle so that the blades always face the wind.

The electricity travels down cables inside the tower to a transformer at the base, which raises the voltage so that the power can be carried along the grid. A single large turbine produces enough electricity for about two thousand homes, and modern machines start working in a wind of only three metres a second.

readings.title: How a vacuum flask keeps drinks hot
text: The vacuum flask was invented in 1892 by the Scottish scientist James Dewar, who needed to store extremely cold gases in his laboratory. He never patented it; a German company began selling flasks for tea and coffee twelve years later.

The flask works by stopping the three ways in which heat moves. Its heart is a glass or steel bottle with double walls. The air between the two walls is removed, leaving a vacuum. Because heat cannot travel through empty space by conduction, very little warmth escapes through the sides.

The inner surface of both walls is covered with a thin layer of silver, which acts like a mirror and reflects heat back into the liquid. This stops radiation. At the bottom of the inner bottle there is a small glass point, sealed after the air was taken out; this is the weakest part, so the bottle sits on a soft pad of rubber or foam inside the outer case.

The outer case, usually plastic or metal, protects the fragile bottle and stays cool to touch. At the top, a tight stopper made of plastic or cork closes the neck; this prevents convection, the movement of warm air upwards and out. Many modern flasks add a cup, which screws over the stopper and serves as a lid. Together these parts can keep a drink hot for up to twenty-four hours, though every time the flask is opened it loses several degrees.

readings.title: The parts of a traditional water mill
text: Water mills have ground grain into flour for more than two thousand years, and a few still work in Central Asia and Europe today. The building is usually placed beside a fast stream. Water is taken from the stream further upriver and carried along a narrow channel, called the leat, which runs almost level so that the water arrives above the height of the wheel.

At the end of the leat the water passes through a wooden gate, the sluice, which the miller opens and closes to control the flow. From there it falls onto the wheel. In an overshot mill the water lands in buckets at the top of the wheel and turns it by weight; in an undershot mill the water pushes the bottom of the wheel instead, and less power is produced.

The wheel turns a horizontal beam, the axle, which passes through the wall into the building. Inside, a large wooden gearwheel, the pit wheel, changes the direction of the movement from horizontal to vertical. A vertical shaft then carries the movement upwards to the millstones on the floor above.

There are always two millstones. The lower one, the bed stone, never moves. The upper one, the runner stone, turns just above it, leaving a gap thinner than a sheet of paper. Grain falls into the centre of the runner stone from a wooden box called the hopper, moves outwards between the stones, and leaves the edge as flour, which slides down a wooden chute into sacks on the floor below.

readings.title: Reading #11. The Boeing 787
readings.source: Complete IELTS Bands 4–5 Workbook (Cambridge), Unit 3 "Getting from A to B", 18-bet (Reading 1)
text: The Boeing 787 'Dreamliner' has been described as the airliner of the future. We look at the technology that makes it different.

Until now, airliner fuselages have been made of aluminium sheets. Large aircraft can have 1,500 of these sheets with between 40,000 and 50,000 metal fasteners. The 787 is the first airliner to be built with a one-piece fuselage made from a special material called 'composite'. Not only does this make the airliner quicker and easier to build, but it also makes it a lot lighter.

The advantage of this weight reduction is that the 787 uses 20 percent less fuel than other airliners of a similar size, which makes it much more environmentally friendly. The reduced weight also means that the Boeing 787 can fly further than many other airliners of a similar size, carrying 210 passengers or more up to 15,200 kilometres before refuelling.

Sometimes an airliner needs to change from one type of engine to another. This is a difficult and time-consuming process. The 787 has a revolutionary engine attachment on the wing which means that the engines can be changed in a much shorter time. The case containing the engine is also different from those on other airliners. It has been designed to cut down the noise from the engine, making it less noisy for passengers in the cabin as well as for people on the ground.

In addition to a quieter cabin, passengers will also benefit from windows which are 65 percent larger than those on other airliners, giving them a much better view of the world passing by below them. The windows also have a unique facility which allows passengers or cabin crew to control the amount of light that enters them. This is thanks to a liquid in the window which reacts to an electric current. When a passenger or cabin crew member presses a button, the current causes a chemical reaction in the window which darkens the liquid.

tasks.title: Complete labels (1–7) on the diagram
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the passage
tasks.instr: Eng qiyin mashq: belgilar uzun, paraphrase ko'p. Har belgida kalit so'zni tagiga chizing.

Airliner can accommodate at least ___.
Engineers can fit a new engine in a ___ than it takes on other airliners.
A special engine case reduces ___.
The size of the windows has increased by ___.

why: "It also makes it a lot lighter". "Much" = "a lot"; "than" dan oldin qiyosiy daraja keladi.
"The 787 uses 20 percent less fuel". "Reduces the amount" = "uses less".
"Carrying 210 passengers or more". "At least" = "or more", "accommodate" = "carrying".
"The engines can be changed in a much shorter time". "Fit a new engine" = "engines can be changed".
"Designed to cut down the noise from the engine". "Reduces" = "cut down". "Noise" yoki "engine noise" — ikkalasi to'g'ri.
"Windows which are 65 percent larger". "Increased by" = "larger".
"A liquid in the window which reacts to an electric current ... darkens the liquid". FAROSAT: "an" artikli unli tovush bilan boshlanadigan so'zni ko'rsatadi.
tasks.note: Matnda ikkita foiz bor: 20 percent (yoqilg'i) va 65 percent (derazalar). 6-belgi derazalar haqida — shuning uchun 65.

homework_intro: Bugun chizmadagi belgini matndan topishni birga mashq qildik — uyga vazifada xuddi shu ishni endi yolg'iz o'zingiz, ustozsiz bajarasiz.
Birinchi vazifa — "The parts of a traditional water mill" matni: soatga qarab 10 daqiqa vaqt oling va 9 ta belgini to'ldiring, javob ONE WORD ONLY, ya'ni faqat bitta so'z.

Ikkinchisi — "O'z chizmangiz": uyingizdagi bitta qurilmani (choynak, velosiped, fen) chizib, 8 qismini inglizcha belgilaysiz va har biriga kamida 6 ta predlog ishlatib joylashuv gapini yozasiz, bu 20 daqiqacha vaqt oladi; uchinchisi — 15 gapli predlog testi, doskadagi ro'yxatdan foydalanasiz va 15 tadan 13 tasi to'g'ri bo'lsa bajarilgan hisoblanadi.

Eng ko'p qilinadigan xato shu yerda: chizmada allaqachon yozilgan so'z bo'sh joyga yana ko'chiriladi — "thin metal ___" belgisiga "metal ring" deb ikki so'z yoziladi, to'g'risi esa faqat "ring"; va javob har doim ot bo'lsin, fe'l emas.
Uchala vazifa ham bitta daftarda bo'ladi, chizmangizni daftarga yopishtirasiz va keyingi darsga olib kelasiz: birinchi 10 daqiqada javoblarni juftlikda solishtiramiz, keyin daftarlarni yig'ib olaman.

Ildiz yer ostida (under ham to'g'ri).
"Under a small cover" — batareyalar pult ichida.

kahoot.q: In a diagram labelling task, what type of word is the answer usually?
kahoot.explain: Chizmadagi belgilar qism nomlari, shuning uchun javob deyarli har doim ot bo'ladi.

kahoot.q: ONE WORD ONLY. The text says 'a thin metal ring'. The label is 'thin metal ___'. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: Chizmada bor so'zlar (thin metal) qayta yozilmaydi; ONE WORD ONLY — faqat "ring".

kahoot.q: Why are the words already written on a diagram useful?
options: They show where to look in the text
They are usually the answers to the gaps
They tell you the word limit for each gap
They show which paragraphs you can skip
kahoot.explain: Nomlangan qismlar — langar: ularni matndan topsangiz, javob shu atrofda bo'ladi.

kahoot.q: In a reading diagram labelling task, where do the answers usually come from?
kahoot.explain: Chizma odatda matnning bitta qismida tasvirlanadi, javoblar ham shu qismdan olinadi; ular ko'pincha matn tartibida keladi, lekin IELTS buni kafolatlamaydi.

kahoot.q: You cannot find the answer to label 3. What is the best thing to do?
options: Go on to label 4 and come back later
Write the longest word in the paragraph
Stop and read the whole text again
Copy the answer to label 2 again
kahoot.explain: Bitta belgiga vaqt yo'qotmang: keyingisini toping, 3-belgining javobi odatda ikkalasi oralig'idagi gaplarda bo'ladi.

kahoot.q: The text says: 'The fuel tank is fixed below the engine.' Where is the tank on the diagram?
kahoot.explain: "Below" = ostida (under); joy predlogi javobning chizmadagi o'rnini ko'rsatadi.

kahoot.q: Which phrase means 'on both the left and the right'?
kahoot.explain: "On either side" — ikki yonida, ya'ni chapda ham, o'ngda ham.

kahoot.q: In a process diagram, which verb phrase shows movement from one part to another?
kahoot.explain: Jarayon sxemasida harakat fe'llari keladi: flows into, passes through, is carried to.

kahoot.q: The instructions say NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER. Which answer is NOT allowed?
kahoot.explain: "The old stone bridge" — 4 so'z, chegaradan oshadi va 0 ball oladi.

kahoot.q: A label says 'takes water to the tank'. Which phrase from a text is a paraphrase of it?
kahoot.explain: "Takes to" = "carries to"; "from the tank" esa teskari yo'nalish, shuning uchun mos emas.

kahoot.q: What should you do first in a diagram labelling task?
options: Study the diagram and its title
Read the whole text very slowly
Write any words you already know
Check the answers of your partner
kahoot.explain: Avval chizma va sarlavhani o'qing: nima tasvirlangan, qaysi qismlar nomlangan, qaysilari bo'sh.

kahoot.q: You copy the answer from the text but spell it wrongly. What happens in IELTS?
kahoot.explain: Imlo xatosi bo'lgan javob noto'g'ri hisoblanadi, shuning uchun so'zni matndan harfma-harf ko'chiring.

kahoot.q: Something that is 'hollow' is ...
kahoot.explain: "Hollow" — ichi bo'sh, kovak.

kahoot.q: Choose the best synonym for 'fragile'.
kahoot.explain: "Fragile" — mo'rt, tez sinadigan (easily broken).

kahoot.q: 'Can I top up my bus card here?' Here 'top up' means ...
kahoot.explain: "Top up" — to'ldirmoq: kartaga pul yoki batareyaga quvvat qo'shmoq.

kahoot.q: Which word means 'producing good results without wasting energy'?
kahoot.explain: "Efficient" — samarali: kam energiya sarflab ko'p ish bajaradi.

kahoot.q: Renewable energy comes from sources that ...
kahoot.explain: "Renewable" — qayta tiklanadigan: shamol, quyosh, suv kabi manbalar tugamaydi.

kahoot.q: Car 'emissions' are ...
kahoot.explain: "Emissions" — chiqindi gazlar, ya'ni zararli gazlarning havoga chiqarilishi (emissiya).

kahoot.q: A light is 'attached to' the bicycle. This means it is ...
kahoot.explain: "Attached to" — biriktirilgan, mahkamlangan (fixed to).

kahoot.q: Choose the correct collocation: a thin ___ of paint.
kahoot.explain: "A thin layer of paint / ice / dust" — yupqa qatlam; "slice" non yoki go'sht bo'lagi uchun ishlatiladi.

listenings.audios: Complete IELTS Bands 4–5 (Cambridge), Unit 3, 30-bet — Track 17 (ustoz bergan audio)
intro: Kemadagi yo'lovchilar uchun e'lon. Avval chizmani 1 daqiqa o'rganing: "Reception: you are here" — boshlanish nuqtasi. A, B, C Deck qayerda ekanini toping va har bo'sh joy turini ayting.
Ko'rsatma: Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Diagramma javoblari USUALLY tartibda keladi — e'lon sizni kema bo'ylab "yurgizadi".
transcript: Good evening and welcome aboard the Pride of Poole. In this recorded announcement, we'll give you details of some of the facilities available on board this ship.

You're currently standing in the reception area in the centre of B Deck. If you're feeling hungry after a long day's travelling, go up the stairs to A Deck, where you'll find the restaurant. The restaurant caters for all appetites, with anything from a light snack to a full three-course meal. The restaurant will be open from the moment the ship leaves port to half an hour before arrival.

Next to the restaurant on A Deck in the lounge, there are reclining seats with music headphones if you want to relax. The headphones are free, but people using this area are encouraged to keep noise to a minimum so that other passengers can enjoy themselves and sleep or read if they wish.

For those of you who'd like some entertainment, just next door to us on this deck is a 40-seat cinema showing the latest full-length feature films. The cinema programme is available here at reception, but you'll have to buy the tickets themselves at the cinema entrance just before you go in.
Just next to the cinema is the staircase leading down to the cabins on C Deck. To access your cabin, just show your boarding pass to a steward, who will give you the key.
On this deck, that is B Deck, you'll also find an area where you can either play games in our special electronic games arcade or do your shopping.

Just beyond that on the same level, people who want a bit of fresh air or just want to see the sea can go out onto the viewing deck, which is in the open air. Make sure you wear a jacket or coat, as it can be quite cold and windy.

listenings.title: Guided tour of a small factory
intro: Kichik shokolad fabrikasi bo'ylab ekskursiya. Chizmada zal rejasi bor. BIR MARTA tinglang.
transcript: GUIDE: Welcome to Brookfield Chocolate. Before we go in, let me show you the plan of the building, so you know where everything is.

GUIDE: We're standing at the main entrance, at the bottom of the plan. As you come in, on your left there's the reception desk, and behind that a small shop where you can buy our products at the end of the tour.
GUIDE: Directly opposite the entrance, at the far end of the corridor, is the tasting room. That's where we finish, so remember the way.

GUIDE: Now, the working area. On the right of the corridor, the first door leads to the store room, where the cocoa beans arrive in large sacks. Next to the store room, going up the plan, is the roasting area — you'll smell it before you see it.
GUIDE: Above the roasting area, in the top right corner, is the grinding room. The nibs are ground there into a thick liquid. Please don't touch the machines; they are hot.

GUIDE: In the middle of the building, between the grinding room and the tasting room, you'll find the mixing hall. Sugar and milk powder are added there. The large silver tanks you can see through the window are in that hall.

GUIDE: The last production area, in the top left corner, is the moulding section, where liquid chocolate is poured into shapes and cooled. It's kept at eighteen degrees, so take a jacket if you feel the cold.
GUIDE: Finally, next to the shop, there's the packing area. It used to be upstairs, but we moved it down last year so that visitors can watch through the glass. Any questions before we start?

listenings.title: How a rainwater system works
intro: Uy uchun yomg'ir suvini yig'ish tizimi haqida ma'ruza. Chizmada tizim kesimi. BIR MARTA tinglang.
transcript: SPEAKER: Right, let's look at how a domestic rainwater system actually works. I'll follow the water from the roof down to the tap.
SPEAKER: Rain falls on the roof and runs into the gutter along the edge. Nothing unusual so far. The gutter takes the water to a vertical pipe at the corner of the house — that's the downpipe.
SPEAKER: At the bottom of the downpipe, before anything else, there's a leaf filter. It's a simple mesh basket. Most people forget to clean it, and that's the commonest cause of problems.

SPEAKER: After the filter the water reaches the first flush device. The idea is simple: the first few litres carry dust and bird droppings, so they are sent away and not stored. Once that small chamber is full, the clean water passes on.
SPEAKER: The water then enters the tank, which is usually underground, where the temperature stays low and the water keeps better. A typical family tank holds five thousand litres.
SPEAKER: Inside the tank, notice that the inlet pipe has a smooth curve at the end, called a calmed inlet. It slows the water so that the dirt at the bottom is not stirred up.
SPEAKER: The pump sits either in the tank or beside it; in our diagram it's outside, in the small chamber on the right. It sends water to the house through the supply line.

SPEAKER: Near the top of the tank there's an overflow, which takes extra water away in heavy rain. And finally, at the house end, there's a backflow valve, which makes sure rainwater can never enter the drinking water pipes.

intro: Yangi kutubxona binosining rejasi tanishtiriladi. Uyda bir marta tinglang.
transcript: LIBRARIAN: Good afternoon, everyone. I'd like to explain the layout of the new building, because it's quite different from the old one.
LIBRARIAN: You come in from Park Street, through the main doors at the bottom of the plan. Straight in front of you is the help desk; if you're lost, that's where to go.

LIBRARIAN: To the right of the help desk is the self-service area, with four machines for borrowing and returning books. To the left, behind the glass wall, is the children's section. It has its own small entrance from the garden, so families don't have to walk through the quiet areas.

LIBRARIAN: Now, the ground floor. Along the whole of the left-hand wall are the study rooms — six of them, bookable online for up to two hours. Opposite them, on the right-hand side, you'll find the newspaper corner and, beyond it, the café. The café has a separate door to the street, so it stays open after the library closes.
LIBRARIAN: At the back, in the middle, is the lift, with the stairs immediately to its left.

LIBRARIAN: Upstairs, the plan is simpler. The whole front half is the reading hall, with sixty desks. Behind it, on the right, is the computer room — twenty machines, no food or drink. And in the far left corner, next to the window, is the local history collection. That used to be in the basement, but the damp damaged some books, so we moved it up.
LIBRARIAN: Finally, the toilets are on both floors, next to the lift.

listenings.title: Track 08. The Sunshine Express — train facilities
listenings.qtype: Diagram labelling (1–5) — eng qiyin, oxirgi mashq
listenings.audios: Complete IELTS Bands 4–5 Workbook (Cambridge), Unit 3, 20-bet — Track 08 (ustoz bergan audio)
intro: Poyezd menejeri Jane Sharpe yo'lovchilarga e'lon qilmoqda. Chizmada "Observation deck: you are here" — boshlanish nuqtasi. Avval har vagon qaysi tomonda ekanini (oldinda — lokomotiv, orqada — oxirgi vagon) aniqlang.
Ko'rsatma: Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Bu mashq qiyinroq: yo'nalish so'zlari (below us, at the front, behind, at the back) tez-tez almashadi.
transcript: Hello, everyone, and welcome aboard the Sunshine Express on our journey from London to Naples. I'm Jane Sharpe, the train manager, and I hope you'll all enjoy the trip.

Before we depart, I'd like to tell you a bit about the train and its facilities. Now, we're here on the observation deck, which is where you'll probably spend most of your trip, as it offers the best views, and directly below us is a, well, we call it our leisure centre. There are some games machines, a television, a small library and so on. If you've brought a laptop or computer with you, you can also get onto the Internet here, as it has full wi-fi capability. There's also a small bar where you can get tea, coffee and light meals. For lunch and dinner, you'll use the restaurant car, which is at the front of the train. You'll have breakfast in your cabins, by the way, which will be brought to you by your steward.

The two cars behind the restaurant are where you'll find the second-class cabins. Each cabin has seats which are changed into beds at night. You'll also find a simple basin for washing, and a small fold-down table. First-class passengers, your cabins are at the back of the train. To get to them, you'll need to pass through the lounge. This can be used by everyone during the day, but is exclusive to first-class passengers after 6 p.m.

Right at the back of the train, basically as far as you can go, is my office. If anyone needs to see me, though, please use the phone in your cabin rather than coming to the office. Just press one and you'll get me. If I'm not there, tell your steward you need to see the manager, and he or she will look for me.

"For lunch and dinner, you'll use the restaurant car, which is at the front of the train". Midday and evening meals = lunch and dinner. Tuzoq: breakfast — kabinada.
"A simple basin for washing". Basic = simple. Tuzoq: "beds" va "fold-down table" — ular ham kabinada, lekin "___ facilities" = washing.
"Pass through the lounge ... exclusive to first-class passengers after 6 p.m." Only = exclusive; in the evening = after 6 p.m.
"Use the phone in your cabin ... you'll get me" — "me" = Jane Sharpe, the train manager. "Her" — ayol. Tuzoq: "steward" — menejer bo'lmasa stewardga aytiladi; lekin chizma "her"ni so'raydi.
