kahoot.q: 'The shop is directly opposite the bank.' This means the shop is ...
kahoot.explain: "Opposite" — ro'parasida, qarama-qarshi tomonda (facing).

kahoot.q: 'The toilets are at the far end of the hall.' Where are they?
options: in the middle of the long hall
kahoot.explain: "At the far end" — siz turgan joydan eng narigi uchida.

kahoot.q: ONE WORD ONLY. You hear 'the staff meeting room'. The label is 'the staff ___ room'. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: Chizmada bor so'zlar (staff, room) qayta yozilmaydi; bo'sh joyga faqat "meeting".

kahoot.q: You miss the answer to question 3. What should you do?
options: Mark it and listen for question 4
Stop and wait for the recording to repeat
Ask the examiner to play it again
Write the answer to question 4 in 3
kahoot.explain: Audio to'xtamaydi: belgi qo'yib keyingi savolga o'ting, oxirida mantiqiy taxmin yozasiz.

kahoot.q: How does a speaker usually describe a plan or a diagram?
options: step by step in a clear order
from the smallest room to the largest
kahoot.explain: So'zlovchi chizma bo'ylab tartib bilan yuradi: kirishdan ichkariga, chapdan o'ngga yoki yuqoridan pastga.

kahoot.q: Why is the 'You are here' point on a plan important?
options: It is where the speaker starts
It shows where the toilets are
It is always the answer to question 1
It marks the emergency exit of the building
kahoot.explain: "You are here" — boshlanish nuqtasi: so'zlovchi yo'nalishlarni shu joydan hisoblaydi.

kahoot.q: In IELTS Listening, what happens to an answer with a spelling mistake?
kahoot.explain: Imlo xatosi bo'lgan javob 0 ball oladi, shuning uchun oddiy so'zlarning imlosini mashq qiling.

kahoot.q: 'The café is on your left as you come in.' The direction is given from ...
kahoot.explain: "As you come in" — yo'nalish kirish eshigidan, ichkariga qarab turgan odam nuqtai nazaridan hisoblanadi.

kahoot.q: Why should you write short notes like 'gen.' on the diagram while listening?
options: to keep up with the speaker
to show the examiner your work
to make the answer look longer
kahoot.explain: Qisqa belgi vaqtni tejaydi: audio davom etadi, to'liq so'zni keyin yozasiz.

kahoot.q: 'The ship has excellent facilities.' Facilities are ...
options: places and services you can use
people who work on the ship
kahoot.explain: "Facilities" — xizmat joylari va qulayliklar (restoran, kinoteatr, do'kon).

kahoot.q: 'The hotel caters for families with small children.' This means the hotel ...
kahoot.explain: "Cater for" — kimningdir ehtiyojini qondirmoq, unga mos xizmat ko'rsatmoq.

kahoot.q: 'The swimming pool is exclusive to hotel guests.' This means ...
options: only hotel guests can use it
hotel guests pay extra for it
everyone can use it for free
kahoot.explain: "Exclusive to" — faqat ... uchun, boshqalarga ruxsat yo'q.

kahoot.q: 'The tennis courts are bookable online.' This means you can ...
options: read about them in a book
kahoot.explain: "Bookable" — oldindan band qilsa bo'ladigan (book = band qilmoq).

kahoot.q: 'Please stay on board until the train stops.' 'On board' means ...
kahoot.explain: "On board" — kema, poyezd yoki samolyot ichida (bortida).

kahoot.q: The 'layout' of a building is ...
options: the money spent on building it
the hours when it is open
kahoot.explain: "Layout" — joylashuv rejasi: xonalar va qismlar qanday joylashgani.

kahoot.q: 'The walls of the old house were damp.' 'Damp' means ...
kahoot.explain: "Damp" — nam, rutubatli; namlik kitob va devorlarni buzadi.

kahoot.q: 'Our train departs from platform 4.' 'Departs' means ...
kahoot.explain: "Depart" — jo'nab ketmoq (leave); teskarisi "arrive".

lessons.title: Listening: Multiple Choice
lessons.grammar_topic: Multiple choice — uch variantdan bittasini tanlash
lessons.vocab_topic: Sayohat e'lonlari, yarim kunlik ish va shahar xizmatlari
lessons.book_ref: Jony Academy materiali — ustoz bergan audiolar (Track 18 Ferry — further details; Track 09 Sunshine Express) va 3 ta mualliflik skripti.
objectives: Savol va uchta variantni audio boshlanishidan oldin o'qib ulgurish.
Ko'pincha aksariyat variantlar audioda tilga olinishini, ba'zilari esa umuman aytilmasligini bilish: eshitilgani emas, savolga MOS kelgani tanlanadi.
Chalg'ituvchi turlarini tanish: eski ma'lumot, boshqa odamning fikri, qisman to'g'ri variant, rad etilgan variant (not …, it's …).
Variantni o'chirib borish usuli bilan ishlash (elimination).
Javobni belgilab, keyingi savolga o'tishda kechikmaslik.
materials: Audio: ielts5_09_ferry_details.mp3 (Track 18, Ferry) va ielts5_09_train_trip.mp3 (Track 09, Sunshine Express) — dars boshlanishidan oldin telefon yoki kolonkaga yuklab, orqa partadan eshitiladigan qilib sinab qo'ying; ikkalasi ham faqat BIR MARTA qo'yiladi.

"Choosing a part-time job" va "A talk about the city bike scheme" skriptlari — bu ikkisining audiosi yo'q, ustoz o'zi ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi: skriptni chop etib, MAYA va TOM repliklarini ikki xil belgilab chiqing.
Savol varag'i: Ferry 6–10, Sunshine Express 1–5, part-time job 1–5 va city bike 1–6 savollari A/B/C variantlari bilan — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa, audio boshlanishidan OLDIN tarqatiladi.
Sekundomer yoki telefon taymeri — har mashq oldidan savollarni o'qishga 45 soniya berasiz; shu bilan uyga vazifadagi "Tez o'qish mashqi" ham tekshiriladi.

Transkript nusxalari (Ferry va Sunshine Express) — har juftlikka bitta, faqat tekshirish bosqichida tarqatiladi; har o'quvchida ikki xil rangli qalam bo'lsin: javob joyi bir rang, chalg'ituvchi joyi boshqa rang.

[class] "Chalg'ituvchi turlari" uchun 6 ta gap alohida qog'ozchalarga yozib, kesib qo'yiladi (o'quvchi kartochkani tortib oladi va turini aytadi); doskaga esa dars boshlanishidan oldin uch tur — ESKI ma'lumot / BOSHQA odamning fikri / QISMAN to'g'ri — va signal so'zlar yozib qo'yiladi: but, however, actually, though, in the end, only. Yonida to'rtinchi ustun uchun joy qoldiring — RAD ETILGAN (not …, it's …): u 5-kartochkadan keyin yoziladi.
Uy vazifasi "Tez o'qish mashqi" varag'i — homework bo'limidagi 10 ta savol (javobsiz), har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa; dars oxirida vazifa tushuntirilganda tarqatiladi.
timeline: Salomlashish, o'tgan darsdagi savol turini 3 savolda eslatish
Ustoz doskada: qoida, bosqichlar, tipik xatolar
"Chalg'ituvchi turlari": 6 ta kartochka — o'quvchi turini va signal so'zni aytadi, har javob izohlanadi

Ustoz savoldagi so'zni aytadi, o'quvchilar audioda qanday eshitilishi mumkinligini topadi (ustozning o'z misollari: cheaper = costs less, not allowed = you mustn't, on foot = walk, the main reason = what really matters, nearly = almost); bugungi audiolarning javoblari ochilmaydi
45 soniya savollarni o'qish, BIR MARTA tinglash, keyin javoblar va "Nega boshqa variantlar emas?" tahlili
45 soniya o'qish, bir marta tinglash, transkript bilan tekshirish va tuzoq turlari
Jony skriptlari: part-time job va city bike
Ustoz har skriptni bir marta ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi (dialogda MAYA va TOM ovozini farqlab), keyin chalg'ituvchi izohi
Xatolar daftari: har xato javob sababi bilan yoziladi
Tutorial skripti uyga; chalg'ituvchi daftari va tez o'qish mashqi tushuntiriladi

intro: Multiple choice — eng ko'p vaqt oladigan tur, chunki o'qish kerak: savol + 3 variant.
Oltin qoida: ko'pincha aksariyat variantlar tilga olinadi, lekin ba'zilari umuman aytilmaydi — ularni tez o'chiring. Eshitilgan variant emas, savolga to'liq mos kelgani javob bo'ladi.
Chalg'ituvchi 1 — ESKI ma'lumot: "It used to be on Mondays, but now it's on Thursdays."
Chalg'ituvchi 2 — BOSHQA odamning fikri: "My friend liked the food, but I thought the service was better."
Chalg'ituvchi 3 — QISMAN to'g'ri: variantda ikkita narsa aytiladi, audio faqat bittasini tasdiqlaydi.
Savolni o'qiyotganda kalit so'zni belgilang; variantlarni qisqa belgilab qo'ying (masalan: A = tez, B = arzon, C = yaqin).
Javob topilgach darhol belgilang va keyingi savolga qarang: audio to'xtamaydi.
Ishonchingiz komil bo'lmasa, eng ehtimolli variantni belgilang — bo'sh javob har doim 0.
formulas: A tez / B arzon / C yaqin
Ko'z bilan tez qamrab olish uchun
presentation: Uchala variant ham eshitildi. Qaysi biri javob?
Savolga TO'LIQ mos kelgani. Qolganlari chalg'ituvchi.
"It used to be..." degan gap eshitildi. Bu javobmi?
Yo'q, bu eski ma'lumot. Hozirgi holatni kuting.
Do'stining fikri aytildi, javob shumi?
Savol kimning fikrini so'rayotganiga qarang.
Savolni o'qishga ulgurmadim.
Variantlarning faqat farqli so'zini o'qing: tez / arzon / yaqin.
Ikkita variant to'g'ridek.
Savolning aniq so'ziga qayting: "main reason", "most", "first".
Javobni o'zgartirsam bo'ladimi?
Ha, lekin faqat aniq yangi ma'lumot eshitilsa.
notes: Ustoz skriptni o'qishdan oldin 45 soniya beradi: savol va variantlarni o'qish uchun.
Tekshirishda har chalg'ituvchi uchun "nega noto'g'ri" izohi aytilsin — bu darsning asosiy ishi.
Transkriptda javob joyini va chalg'ituvchi joyini ikki xil rangda belgilang.
Kuchsiz o'quvchilarga: avval faqat 3 savol, keyin 6 savol.

core: Our voyage across the sea took all night, so we slept in a cabin.
Dengiz bo'ylab sayohatimiz tun bo'yi davom etdi, shuning uchun kabinada uxladik.
We reached our destination early in the morning, just in time for breakfast.
Manzilimizga erta tongda, nonushtaga ulgurib yetib keldik.
She bought a small souvenir for her brother at the airport.
U aeroportda akasi uchun kichik esdalik sovg'a sotib oldi.
He upgraded his old laptop so that it would run faster.
U eski noutbukini tezroq ishlashi uchun yangiladi.
If you buy your ticket online, you won't have to queue at the station.
Chiptani internetda sotib olsangiz, vokzalda navbatda turishingiz shart bo'lmaydi.
The crew changed at the border, and a new driver took over.
Chegarada ekipaj almashdi va boshqaruvni yangi mashinist oldi.
Many students have a part-time job to pay for their books.
Ko'p talabalar kitoblari uchun pul topish maqsadida yarim kunlik ishda ishlaydi.
Her wages are paid every Friday.
Uning ish haqi har juma kuni to'lanadi.
If I have an exam, I can swap shifts with a colleague.
Imtihonim bo'lsa, hamkasbim bilan smenani almashtira olaman.
With her staff discount, she pays much less for clothes.
Xodimlar chegirmasi tufayli u kiyim uchun ancha kam to'laydi.
An annual membership at the gym is cheaper than paying for each visit.
Sport zaliga yillik a'zolik har bir tashrif uchun alohida to'lashdan arzonroq.
Good hygiene, such as washing your hands, stops illness from spreading.
Qo'l yuvish kabi yaxshi gigiyena kasallik tarqalishining oldini oladi.
Local residents complained about the noise from the new car park.
Mahalliy aholi yangi avtoturargohdan keladigan shovqindan shikoyat qildi.
Attending the first lecture is compulsory for all new students.
Birinchi ma'ruzaga qatnashish barcha yangi talabalar uchun majburiy.
The deadline for the essay is next Monday, so don't leave it until Sunday night.
Insho topshirishning oxirgi muddati kelasi dushanba, shuning uchun uni yakshanba kechasiga qoldirmang.

class_ex.title: Chalg'ituvchi turlari
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gap o'qiydi, o'quvchi chalg'ituvchi turini aytadi.
items: "The course was on Mondays last year, but now it's on Thursdays."
"My sister found it easy; I struggled with the writing."
"The hotel was clean and quiet, though the food was poor."
"We wanted to go by train, but in the end we drove."
"It's not the price that matters, it's the time."
"Almost everyone said yes — only two people disagreed."
why: Javob — Thursdays.
Savol kim haqida ekanini tekshiring.
Variantda "clean and good food" bo'lsa — noto'g'ri.
Javob — mashina.
Javob — vaqt.
Variantda "everyone agreed" bo'lsa — noto'g'ri: ikki kishi rozi bo'lmagan, variant faqat qisman to'g'ri.
class_ex.note: Har misolda "signal so'z" ni ayting: but, though, in the end, only, not ... it's. 4 va 6-gaplar doskadagi turlarning ko'rinishi (4 — eski ma'lumot: reja o'zgargan; 6 — qisman to'g'ri: "almost everyone" ≠ "everyone"). 5-gap — tez-tez uchraydigan to'rtinchi holat: variant aytiladi, lekin darhol rad etiladi — doskaga to'rtinchi ustun qilib yozing: RAD ETILGAN (not …, it's …).

listenings.title: Track 18. Ferry — further details
intro: 8-darsdagi "Pride of Poole" kemasi e'lonining davomi. Avval savollarni o'qing va har savolda kalit so'zni belgilang (what time, children, reduced price, lounge, special event). Keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. MCQ da ko'pincha bir nechta (ba'zan uchala) variant tilga olinadi, lekin faqat bittasi savolga aniq javob; umuman aytilmagan variantni tez o'chiring.
transcript: Now for some further details. This voyage is an overnight trip. The ship leaves port at 7 p.m. and the journey takes just over 12 hours and 45 minutes, reaching our destination at about eight tomorrow morning. This is for the convenience of those wishing to catch the nine o'clock train, which leaves from the ferry terminal.

Passengers with children in their party are informed that there is a special section in the restaurant with kids' food and a play area. People with children are encouraged to turn up early to get a place, as the section is very popular.

Make this a trip to remember. Here at the information desk, you can obtain a souvenir ship's key ring for four euros fifty; you can upgrade from a tourist-class cabin to a first-class cabin; and you can get your train tickets here, which will save you time queuing in the station tomorrow morning. If you buy them on the ship, you can get them for 20 percent off.

For those using the lounge and wishing to check their email, there's a wireless connection, but you'll have to bring your own laptop. You can also watch the latest TV programmes there or in the coffee bar next to the restaurant.

Finally, a unique feature on this crossing only: anyone who buys a fashion item from our wonderful range of men's and women's clothes in the shopping area has the chance to win a free holiday. All you have to do is complete a sentence starting 'I like Sealand Ferries because ...' and the best sentence wins the prize of a holiday in Switzerland with tickets to a three-day music festival included. Talk to any member of staff for more details.

tasks.title: Questions 6–10: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Savollar audio tartibida (ALWAYS). Bu yozuvda har variantga aloqador so'z eshitiladi — "qaysi biri SAVOLGA javob?" deb so'rang.
items: 6 At approximately what time will the ship arrive? A) at 7 a.m. B) at 8 a.m. C) at 9 a.m.
7 Which of these can children have in the restaurant? A) a children's menu B) earlier mealtimes C) a children's party
8 What is available at a reduced price? A) souvenirs of the ship B) first-class cabins C) train tickets
9 Which of these is situated in the lounge? A) a computer B) a coffee machine C) a television
10 What special event will happen during the voyage? A) a fashion show B) a concert C) a competition
why: "Reaching our destination at about eight tomorrow morning". A tuzoq: "7 p.m." — jo'nash vaqti (kechqurun). C tuzoq: "the nine o'clock train" — poyezd vaqti, kema emas.

"A special section in the restaurant with kids' food". Kids' food = children's menu. B tuzoq: "turn up early to get a place" — joy olish uchun erta kelish, ovqat vaqti erta emas. C tuzoq: "passengers with children in their party" — party bu yerda "birga sayohat qilayotgan guruh" ma'nosida, bayram emas; "play area" — o'yin joyi.

"If you buy them on the ship, you can get them for 20 percent off" — them = train tickets. Reduced price = 20 percent off. A tuzoq: key ring narxi aytilgan (4.50), lekin chegirma yo'q. B — upgrade qilish mumkin, arzonroq emas.

"You can also watch the latest TV programmes there" — there = the lounge. A tuzoq: wireless bor, lekin "bring your own laptop" — kompyuter yo'q. B tuzoq: "coffee bar next to the restaurant" — boshqa joy.

"Complete a sentence ... the best sentence wins the prize" — bu tanlov (competition). A tuzoq: "fashion item" — kiyim sotib olish sharti, ko'rgazma emas. B tuzoq: "a three-day music festival" — sovrin ichida, kemada emas.
tasks.note: Bu yozuvda har savoldagi uchala variantga aloqador so'z eshitiladi — 7 p.m./8/9 o'clock; kids' food/early/party, play area; souvenir/first-class/tickets; laptop/coffee bar/TV; fashion/festival/sentence. Bu tez-tez uchraydi, lekin qonun emas: boshqa yozuvlarda ba'zi variantlar umuman aytilmaydi, shuning uchun eshitilgan so'zga emas, savolga mos ma'noga qarang.

tasks.title: Nega boshqa variantlar emas?
tasks.instr: Har tuzoq variant audioda qanday eshitildi?
items: 6-savol A (7 a.m.)
8-savol A (souvenirs)
9-savol B (coffee machine)
10-savol B (concert)
why: Soat to'g'ri, lekin p.m. va jo'nash — savol kelish vaqtini so'raydi.
Narx aytildi, chegirma emas.
Joy boshqa.
Sovrin — kemadagi voqea emas.

listenings.title: Track 09. The Sunshine Express — trip information
intro: London — Neapol poyezdi haqida e'lonning davomi (8-darsdagi Track 08 dan keyin). Avval savollarni o'qing va kalit so'zlarni tagiga chizing: how long, passports, dinner, Italian border, NOT do.
Ko'rsatma: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C. 5-savolda "NOT" bor — nima QILMASLIK kerakligini qidiring.
transcript: Right, let me give you a bit more information about the trip. The first part of our journey is from London to Paris, going through the Channel Tunnel. It will take us just over an hour to get to the Tunnel, including a short stop before we get there to pick up some more passengers. From there, it'll be another three hours to Paris, so we're looking at four hours altogether, give or take a few minutes.

A quick bit of advice about passports. You won't need these until we get to the Italian border, so I suggest you keep them in the safe which you'll find in your cabin. Ask your steward – that's the person in charge of your carriage – for a key. That way, you won't need to carry them with you all the time.

Now, meals. As I said earlier, breakfast tomorrow morning will be in your cabins, and this will be served at about 7.30, 7.45, so you'll be able to enjoy it as we travel along the southern French coast. Lunch is at 1 o'clock in the restaurant car, and dinner is at 8 o'clock, although we'd like you all to be at your table about fifteen minutes earlier, at a quarter to, if you could.

When we get to the Italian border tomorrow morning, our train will change engines, and we'll also be getting a new crew. We'll be taking advantage of the stop to have a look around. I've arranged a visit to the local market, a museum and a castle. This will take about four hours, with a break for coffee in a local café, and we'll be back on the train in time for lunch.

A few quick rules. Some of you might have brought your own food or drink on board. That's fine, but could we ask that you consume it in your cabins and not in the restaurant or lounge? Could we also ask you to make sure your cabin windows are closed when you're not in your cabin? And whatever you do, don't get off the train until we reach the Italian border. Apart from the border and one or two other places, which I'll tell you about, any stops we make will only be for a few minutes. I'd hate to leave anyone behind.
All right, so, moving on from the Italian border, we'll be heading ... [fade]

tasks.title: Questions 1–5: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C
tasks.instr: Savollar audio tartibida. Ko'p variantlar audioda tilga olinadi, lekin hammasi emas — aytilmagan variantni tez o'chiring.
items: 1 How long will it take to get to Paris? A) about one hour B) about three hours C) about four hours
2 What should passengers do with their passports? A) leave them with their steward B) lock them away C) carry them at all times
3 When should passengers be in the restaurant car for dinner? A) 7.45 p.m. B) 8.00 p.m. C) 8.15 p.m.
4 What will the passengers do when the train gets to the Italian border? A) change trains B) go on a tour C) have lunch in a local café
5 What should passengers NOT do? A) eat their own food on the train B) open their cabin window C) leave the train before it gets to Italy
why: "We're looking at four hours altogether". A tuzoq: "just over an hour to get to the Tunnel" — birinchi qism. B tuzoq: "another three hours to Paris" — ikkinchi qism. Jami: 1 + 3 = 4.
"Keep them in the safe which you'll find in your cabin" — safe = qulflanadi. A tuzoq: stewarddan faqat KALIT so'raladi. C teskari: "you won't need to carry them with you all the time".

"Dinner is at 8 o'clock, although we'd like you all to be at your table about fifteen minutes earlier, at a quarter to" — 7.45. B tuzoq: rasmiy vaqt. 7.45 nonushta vaqti sifatida ham eshitiladi (7.30, 7.45) — ehtiyot bo'ling.
"I've arranged a visit to the local market, a museum and a castle" — bu tur (tour). A tuzoq: poyezd emas, "change ENGINES". C tuzoq: kafeda QAHVA, tushlik esa poyezdda.

"Whatever you do, don't get off the train until we reach the Italian border". A tuzoq: o'z ovqatini yeyish mumkin — faqat kabinada. B tuzoq: oyna kabinada YO'Q bo'lganda yopiq bo'lsin — ochish umuman taqiqlanmagan.
tasks.note: 1 va 3-savollar — raqam tuzog'i: avval qismlar aytiladi (1 soat + 3 soat; rasmiy vaqt 8), javob keyin keladi ("four hours altogether"; "at a quarter to" = 7.45). Birinchi eshitilgan raqamni belgilashga shoshilmang.

tasks.title: Tuzoq turlari
items: 1-savol A/B
3-savol B
4-savol A
5-savol A, B
why: Yo'lning bir qismi vaqti.
"Be at your table ... at a quarter to".
change engines ≠ change trains.
"fine, but in your cabins"; "closed when you're not in your cabin".

listenings.title: Choosing a part-time job
intro: Ikki talaba yarim kunlik ish haqida gaplashmoqda. BIR MARTA tinglang, har savolda A, B yoki C ni tanlang.
transcript: MAYA: Have you found a job yet, Tom?
TOM: I've got two offers, actually. One is in the café at the station, on the other side of town, and the other is at the bookshop in the centre.
MAYA: The café pays well, doesn't it?
TOM: It's nine pounds an hour, and the bookshop is eight fifty. But the café shifts start at seven in the morning, and I have lectures at nine, so I'd be running across town every day.
MAYA: So you'll take the bookshop?
TOM: I think so. It's not the money — half an hour of sleep matters more to me right now.
MAYA: Fair enough. How many hours a week?
TOM: The bookshop wants twelve, but they said ten is possible during exams. The café wanted sixteen, which is too many.
MAYA: My job is only eight hours, but I work every Saturday, and I hate that.
TOM: Yes, weekends are the problem. The bookshop is closed on Sundays, and they rotate Saturdays, so I'd work two Saturdays a month.
MAYA: That's better than mine. What about the people?
TOM: I met the manager. She seemed strict — she talked a lot about being on time — but the other staff said she's fair, and she lets people swap shifts.
MAYA: My manager is friendly but hopeless at organising. Last week nobody knew who was working.
TOM: That sounds worse. Oh, and the bookshop gives a staff discount — thirty per cent on books.
MAYA: Thirty? That's dangerous for you.
TOM: I know. I'll probably spend my wages there.

tasks.title: Multiple choice
items: 1 Why does Tom prefer the bookshop? A) It pays more B) The hours suit him better C) It is nearer his home
2 How many hours a week will Tom probably work? A) eight B) ten C) twelve
3 What does Tom say about Saturdays? A) He will work every Saturday B) He will work two a month C) He will never work Saturdays

listenings.title: A talk about the city bike scheme
intro: Shahar velosiped tizimi haqida qisqa ma'ruza. BIR MARTA tinglang.
transcript: SPEAKER: Good evening. I'm here to explain how the city bike scheme works, and to answer the question everyone asks: is it actually cheaper than the bus?
SPEAKER: The scheme opened three years ago with 200 bikes at 20 stations. Today there are 1,400 bikes at 130 stations, and we add about thirty-five stations a year.

SPEAKER: Now, prices. A single ride of up to thirty minutes costs one pound fifty. A day pass is five pounds, and an annual membership is sixty. For most people the annual pass pays for itself after about six weeks of daily use.

SPEAKER: The most common complaint is not price, though — it's finding an empty space to leave the bike. In the morning everybody cycles towards the centre, so the central stations fill up. We move bikes back out by van at night, but the vans themselves are unpopular with residents.

SPEAKER: We are testing a solution: users who return a bike to an empty station in the centre get a free ride credit. In the trial, this cut the number of full stations by about a third, which is better than we expected.

SPEAKER: Safety. Helmets are not provided — we know some cities do this, but hygiene rules make it difficult. Instead we spend the money on lights, which are now fitted to every bike and switch on automatically.

SPEAKER: Finally, who uses the bikes? You might expect students, but our data shows that the largest group is people aged between thirty and forty-five, travelling to work. Students actually prefer walking, because the campus is close to the centre.

5 Why are helmets not provided? A) they are too expensive B) for hygiene reasons C) they are not needed

listenings.title: Tutorial: choosing a project topic
intro: Talaba va ustoz loyiha mavzusi haqida gaplashmoqda. Uyda bir marta tinglang.
transcript: TUTOR: So, Leyla, you wanted to talk about your project topic.
LEYLA: Yes. I had three ideas: school uniforms, screen time in children, and food waste in supermarkets.
TUTOR: Which one attracts you most?
LEYLA: Screen time, I think. But I'm worried there's too much written about it already.

TUTOR: That's a real risk. The uniform topic is narrower, but honestly, students write about it every year and the tutors get tired of it. Food waste is the one I'd choose in your place — you can collect your own data locally.
LEYLA: Collect it how?
TUTOR: Two supermarkets near campus have agreed to talk to students this term. You could interview a manager and count what goes into the bins for a week.
LEYLA: That sounds like a lot of work.
TUTOR: It is, but it's original. And your mark comes mostly from method, not from the amount of reading.
LEYLA: How long should the project be?
TUTOR: Four thousand words. Some students hand in six and lose marks for going over.
LEYLA: And the deadline is in May?
TUTOR: The 12th of May for the written part. But there's an outline due much earlier — the 3rd of March. That's only two pages, but it's compulsory; without it we can't approve your topic.
LEYLA: Should I start with the reading or the interviews?
TUTOR: The interviews, definitely. Managers change jobs, and if you wait until April they may say no. Do the reading while you wait for their replies.
LEYLA: All right. One more thing — can I work with Dmitri? He's doing something similar.
TUTOR: You can share the data collection, but the writing must be completely separate. Two identical projects fail, even if the data is the same.

kahoot.q: In IELTS Listening multiple choice, when should you read the questions and options?
options: Only while the speaker is talking
When the answer sheets are collected
kahoot.explain: Audio boshlanishidan oldin berilgan vaqtda savol va variantlarni o'qib, kalit so'zni belgilang.

kahoot.q: You hear: 'The swimming club used to meet on Tuesdays, but now it meets on Saturdays.' When does the club meet?
kahoot.explain: "used to" — eski ma'lumot; javob "but now" dan keyin aytilgan hozirgi holat.

kahoot.q: Which group of words often signals that the speaker is correcting or changing information?
kahoot.explain: but, actually, in the end kabi so'zlardan keyin ko'pincha yangi, to'g'ri ma'lumot keladi.

kahoot.q: You hear words connected to all three options. How do you choose the answer?
options: Pick the option that answers the question
Pick the option you heard first
Pick the option you heard last
Pick the option repeated most often
kahoot.explain: Eshitilgan so'z emas, savolga aniq javob beradigan variant tanlanadi.

kahoot.q: Does the recording always mention all three options?
options: No — some options may not be said at all
Yes — all three are always mentioned in full
Yes — but only in the last part of the test
No — only the correct option is ever mentioned
kahoot.explain: Ko'pincha aksariyat variantlar tilga olinadi, lekin ba'zilari umuman aytilmaydi — ularni tez o'chiring.

kahoot.q: Anna says: 'My brother loved the course, but I found it too long.' What does Anna think of the course?
kahoot.explain: "My brother loved it" — boshqa odamning fikri; savol Annaning o'z fikrini so'raydi.

kahoot.q: Option C: 'The café is cheap and quiet.' You hear: 'It's cheap, but the music is always really loud.' Option C is...
options: true, but only about the past
kahoot.explain: Variantning bir qismi to'g'ri (cheap), ikkinchisi teskari (loud) — qisman to'g'ri variant noto'g'ri javob.

kahoot.q: Why is it useful to shorten each option to one key word (A = fast, B = cheap, C = near)?
options: You can follow all three quickly
It helps you write longer answers
kahoot.explain: Qisqa belgi uchala variantni ko'z bilan tez kuzatishga yordam beradi, audio esa to'xtamaydi.

kahoot.q: The question asks for the MAIN reason, and two reasons are mentioned. What should you do?
options: Choose the one the speaker says matters most
Choose the reason you hear first
Choose the reason with the longest explanation
kahoot.explain: "main" — asosiy sabab: spiker "more importantly", "what really matters" kabi iboralar bilan ajratadi.

kahoot.q: You missed the answer to question 3 and the speaker is already talking about question 4. What should you do?
options: Wait for the speaker to repeat 3
Leave 3 blank and never go back
kahoot.explain: Audio qaytarilmaydi: 3 ga eng ehtimolli variantni belgilab, 4-savolga o'ting; bo'sh javob — 0 ball.

kahoot.q: The question is: 'Which activity is NOT allowed?' What are you listening for?
options: Something that is free of charge
Something the speaker did last year
kahoot.explain: NOT — nima QILMASLIK kerakligi: "don't", "you mustn't", "not allowed" kabi taqiqni qidiring.

kahoot.q: Option A says 'on foot'. Which phrase in the recording has the same meaning?
kahoot.explain: on foot = walking: variantdagi so'z audioda ko'pincha boshqa so'z bilan (paraphrase) aytiladi.

kahoot.q: What is a 'voyage'?
options: A long journey, especially by sea
A short walk around the centre of a town
A seat on a crowded train
A ticket for a music festival
kahoot.explain: Voyage — uzoq sayohat, ayniqsa dengizda (kemada).

kahoot.q: If a team 'rotates' the night shift, its members...
kahoot.explain: Rotate — navbatma-navbat bajarish: har safar boshqa odam ishlaydi.

kahoot.q: Choose the best synonym for 'compulsory'.
kahoot.explain: Compulsory = required (majburiy); optional esa uning teskarisi.

kahoot.q: What is a 'souvenir'?
options: Something you buy to remember a place
A document you need to cross a border
A person who works on a ship
kahoot.explain: Souvenir — biror joyni eslab yurish uchun olingan esdalik buyum.

kahoot.q: 'Wages' are...
kahoot.explain: Wages — ish uchun (odatda haftalik yoki soatbay) to'lanadigan haq.

kahoot.q: Which word means the LAST date by which something must be done?
kahoot.explain: Deadline — oxirgi muddat; outline esa reja yoki qisqa konspekt.

kahoot.q: The new night buses are 'unpopular with local residents'. This means that the people who...
options: live in the area dislike them
live in the area use them a lot
visit the city want more of them
kahoot.explain: Residents — shu hududda doimiy yashovchilar; unpopular with — ularga yoqmaydi.

kahoot.q: If you 'upgrade' your phone, you...
options: pay less for the same model
kahoot.explain: Upgrade — yaxshiroq yoki yangiroq darajaga o'tish.

intro: Matching headings — matnning har xatboshisiga ro'yxatdan sarlavha tanlanadi. Sarlavhalar soni xatboshidan ko'p bo'ladi: ortiqchalari ishlatilmaydi.
Bu tur TARTIBSIZ: i, ii, iii raqamlari matn tartibida kelmaydi. Shuning uchun har xatboshi alohida o'qiladi.
Ishlash yo'li: avval xatboshini o'qing, asosiy g'oyani O'Z so'zingiz bilan bir gapda ayting, keyingina sarlavhalar ro'yxatiga qarang.
Aksincha qilsangiz (avval sarlavhalarni o'qisangiz), ko'zingiz matndan o'sha so'zni qidiradi va tuzoqqa tushasiz.
Asosiy g'oya odatda birinchi yoki oxirgi gapda bo'ladi, lekin har doim emas: butun xatboshini qamrab oluvchi fikrni qidiring.
Tafsilot tuzog'i: sarlavha faqat bitta gapga mos kelsa — noto'g'ri. Sarlavha butun xatboshiga mos kelishi kerak.
O'xshash sarlavhalarni yonma-yon qo'ying va FARQLI so'zini belgilang: "problems of X" va "solutions to X".
Oson xatboshilardan boshlang, qiyinlarini oxiriga qoldiring va ishlatilgan sarlavhani o'chirib boring.
presentation: Qaysi tartibda ishlayman?
Xatboshi → o'z gapingiz → sarlavhalar ro'yxati.
Sarlavhalar tartibdami?
Yo'q, bu turda tartib yo'q.
Sarlavha faqat birinchi gapga mos keladi. Olamanmi?
Yo'q, bu tafsilot tuzog'i. Sarlavha butun xatboshiga mos bo'lsin.
Ikkita sarlavha o'xshash. Nima qilaman?
Farqli so'zini belgilang va xatboshidan shu so'zni qidiring.
Ortiqcha sarlavhalar nega beriladi?
Tuzoq uchun. Hamma sarlavha ishlatilmaydi.
Vaqtim kam. Nimadan boshlayman?
Eng oson va aniq xatboshidan; qiyinlari oxirida qoladi.
notes: Bu tur o'quvchilarni eng ko'p qiynaydi: ustoz har xatboshi uchun "bir gapda nima haqida?" savolini majburiy qilsin.
Doskada ikki ustun: "asosiy g'oya" va "tafsilot" — o'quvchilar gaplarni ajratadi.
Vaqt: har xatboshiga 1.5 daqiqa; 6 xatboshi — 9 daqiqa.

readings.title: Reading #12. Traffic Jams — No End in Sight
text: A. There are no easy answers to the problems of traffic congestion. Traffic congestion affects people throughout the world. Traffic jams cause smog in dozens of cities across both the developed and developing world. In the U.S., commuters spend an average of a full work week each year sitting in traffic, according to the Texas Transportation Institute. While alternative ways of getting around are available, most people still choose their cars because they are looking for convenience, comfort and privacy.

B. The most promising technique for reducing city traffic is called congestion pricing, whereby cities charge a toll to enter certain parts of town at certain times of day. In theory, if the toll is high enough, some drivers will cancel their trips or go by bus or train. And in practice it seems to work: Singapore, London and Stockholm have reduced traffic and pollution in city centers thanks to congestion pricing.

C. Another way to reduce rush hour traffic is for employers to implement flexitime, which lets employees travel to and from work at off-peak traffic times to avoid the rush hour. Those who have to travel during busy times can do their part by sharing cars. Employers can also allow more staff to telecommute (work from home) so as to keep more cars off the road altogether.

D. Some urban planners still believe that the best way to ease traffic congestion is to build more roads, especially roads that can take drivers around or over crowded city streets. But such techniques do not really keep cars off the road; they only accommodate more of them.

E. Other, more forward-thinking, planners know that more and more drivers and cars are taking to the roads every day, and they are unwilling to encourage more private automobiles when public transport is so much better both for people and the environment. For this reason, the American government has decided to spend some $7 billion on helping to increase capacity on public transport systems and upgrade them with more efficient technologies. But environmentalists complain that such funding is tiny compared with the $50 billion being spent on roads and bridges.

readings.title: Reading #13. Pedestrians only
text: How traffic-free shopping streets developed

A. The concept of traffic-free shopping areas goes back a long time. During the Middle Ages, traffic-free shopping areas known as souks were built in Middle Eastern countries to allow people to shop in comfort and, more importantly, safety. As far back as 2,000 years ago, road traffic was banned from central Rome during the day to allow for the free movement of pedestrians, and was only allowed in at night when shops and markets had closed for the day. In most other cities, however, pedestrians were forced to share the streets with horses, coaches and, later, with cars and other motorised vehicles.

B. The modern, traffic-free shopping street was born in Europe in the 1960s, when both city populations and car ownership increased rapidly. Dirty exhaust fumes from cars and the risks involved in crossing the road were beginning to make shopping an unpleasant and dangerous experience. Many believed the time was right for experimenting with car-free streets, and shopping areas seemed the best place to start.

C. At first, there was resistance from shopkeepers. They believed that such a move would be bad for business. They argued that people would avoid streets if they were unable to get to them in their cars. When the first streets in Europe were closed to traffic, there were even noisy demonstrations, as many shopkeepers predicted they would lose customers.

D. However, research carried out afterwards in several European cities revealed some unexpected statistics. In Munich, Cologne and Hamburg, visitors to shopping areas increased by 50 percent. On Copenhagen's main shopping street, shopkeepers reported sales increases of 25-40 percent. Shopkeepers in Minneapolis, USA, were so impressed when they learnt this that they even offered to pay for the construction and maintenance costs of their own traffic-free streets.

E. With the arrival of the traffic-free shopping street, many shops, especially those selling things like clothes, food and smaller luxury items, prospered. Unfortunately, it wasn't good news for everyone, as shops selling furniture and larger electrical appliances actually saw their sales drop. Many of these were forced to move elsewhere, away from the city centre. Today they are a common feature on the outskirts of towns and cities, often situated in out-of-town retail zones with their own car parks and other local facilities.
paraphrases: goes back a long time / 2,000 years ago
the time was right for experimenting

readings.title: Reading #14. Future of money: a currency that helps people make friends
text: A. In one of America's poorest cities, a new use of technology has been attracting attention. The 92,000 people who live in Macon, Georgia, USA know each other a little better than they did, thanks to an online computer game. Since October, the locals - college students and elderly people alike - have been playing Macon Money, a 'social impact game' that uses 'virtual money' to bring people from different economic backgrounds closer together by encouraging them to meet.

B. In the game, winning players receive 'bonds', which they can then exchange for bank notes of Macon Money. These notes can be spent at local shops and businesses. But the game is not as simple as it sounds. Each person receives just half a bond and must find the person with the other half so that they can spend it. People often find their other half by searching for them on the social networking sites Facebook and Twitter. Matching players then meet in person to redeem the bond and get their Macon Money. The bonds range in value from $10 to $100.

C. Pairs might spend their money separately, or do something together like share a meal or give the money to someone who needs it more, says Beverly Blake of the John S. and James L. Knight Foundation, the non-profit group based in Miami, Florida, that funded the game. 'These are meetings and conversations that might not happen naturally at all,' she said. The game's designers are hoping Macon Money will bring members of the community together who wouldn't normally meet each other.

D. Although Macon Money is quite a new innovation, early signs are positive. The first round of the game has seen $65,000-worth of bonds given out and 2,688 participants so far spending $48,000 in Macon Money. Recently, Macon Money's Executive Producer Kati London accepted the 2011 FutureEverything Award for outstanding innovation in art, society and technology in Manchester, UK. 'It isn't just technology for technology's sake,' London said in an interview with FutureEverything after receiving the award. 'It's about putting those tools, that craft, to work in the community.'

E. Whether such a game can bring lasting economic growth remains to be seen, however. An independent research firm will now evaluate how much economic activity the game has caused, with results due later this year.
paraphrases: new game with a social purpose
a 'social impact game' ... to bring people closer together
winning players receive 'bonds' ... must find the person with the other half
members of the community who wouldn't normally meet each other
quite a new innovation, early signs are positive

readings.title: Why city birds sing differently
text: A. Anyone who has walked in a park at dawn knows that birds are noisy in the morning. What fewer people notice is that the same species sounds different in the city and in the countryside. Over the last twenty years biologists in Europe, Asia and North America have recorded thousands of hours of birdsong and found the same pattern almost everywhere.

B. The pattern is simple: city birds sing higher and louder. Traffic produces a deep, low noise, and a low song disappears inside it, like a voice in a busy room. By raising the pitch, a bird lifts its song above the traffic. Great tits in Amsterdam, for example, sing about two hundred hertz higher than great tits in nearby woods.

C. Singing higher solves one problem and creates another. Female birds usually prefer deep songs, which show that a male is large and strong. A male who sings high may be heard, but he may also be judged as weak. Researchers in Germany found that city females took longer to choose a partner, and some pairs produced fewer eggs.

D. Time of day matters as well. In quiet villages, birds begin singing at first light. In cities they often start up to two hours earlier, using the only period when the streets are silent. Street lighting adds to this: under bright lamps, robins sometimes sing through the night, which is exhausting for them.

E. Not every bird can adapt. Species that sing naturally low, such as pigeons, cannot raise their pitch, and they are disappearing from the noisiest districts. Species with flexible voices, like blackbirds and sparrows, are doing well. Over time this changes which birds live around us — noise acts like a filter.

F. Some cities are now responding. Planting trees along busy roads reduces noise by several decibels, and quiet surfaces on roads help too. In one Dutch experiment, after a road was resurfaced, the local great tits lowered their songs again within two years — proof that the change is behaviour, not evolution.
glossary: pitch — tovush tonining balandligi (ingichka yoki yo'g'on ovoz); "louder" (qattiqroq) bilan adashtirmang

readings.title: The return of the wolf
text: A. A hundred years ago wolves had disappeared from most of Western Europe. Farmers had hunted them, governments had paid rewards for dead animals, and the forests they needed had been cut down. By 1970 only a few hundred survived, mainly in Italy, Spain and Poland.

B. Then the law changed. In 1979 European countries signed an agreement that made killing wolves illegal, and at the same time millions of people were leaving the countryside for the cities. Fields returned to forest, deer and wild boar multiplied, and the wolves followed the food. Today there are more than twenty thousand wolves in Europe, and packs have been photographed within fifty kilometres of Paris and Berlin.

C. Scientists were especially interested in what happened in one American park, where wolves were reintroduced in 1995. Deer had eaten so many young trees that the riverbanks were bare. With wolves present, the deer moved more often and stopped feeding in open valleys; trees grew back, birds returned, and even the rivers changed shape because the banks became stronger.

D. Farmers see the story from another side. A single wolf pack can kill sheep, and in some mountain regions attacks have risen sharply. Governments pay compensation, but the money arrives late and does not cover the fear of losing animals that a family has raised for years. In several countries this has become a political question, not a scientific one.

E. Protection that works is usually old-fashioned. Electric fences help, but the most effective tool is a large guard dog that lives with the flock from birth. In Portugal, farms with such dogs report up to 90 per cent fewer attacks. The problem is cost: a trained dog is expensive, and small farms cannot always afford one.

F. The debate is likely to continue, because both sides are partly right. Wolves make forests healthier, and they are protected by law; but the people who lose animals are real, and telling them that a predator is "good for the ecosystem" solves nothing. Most experts now argue for money and training rather than for new laws.

readings.title: Sleep and the teenage brain
text: A. Parents often complain that teenagers cannot get up in the morning and will not go to bed at night. For a long time this was treated as laziness. Sleep research over the past thirty years suggests something different: the teenage body clock really does move.

B. The clock is controlled by a hormone called melatonin, which tells the body that it is time to sleep. In children, melatonin is released at about nine in the evening. In teenagers it appears one to three hours later, and it also disappears later in the morning. A fifteen-year-old asked to sleep at ten is being asked to sleep while their body is still in "day" mode.

C. The effects of missing sleep are easy to measure. Teenagers who sleep fewer than seven hours make more mistakes in tests of attention, remember less of what they studied, and report more arguments at home. Some studies also link short sleep to weight gain, because tiredness changes the hormones that control hunger.

D. Screens make the situation worse, though perhaps not for the reason most people think. The blue light of a phone does delay melatonin a little, but the bigger problem is what the phone contains: messages that demand an answer and videos designed never to end. A book in bed rarely keeps a teenager awake until two in the morning.

E. Some schools have tried the obvious experiment. In one English town, lessons began at ten instead of nine for two years. Attendance improved, and the number of top grades rose by about twelve per cent. However, parents who started work at eight found the new times difficult, and after the study ended the school returned to the old timetable.

F. Researchers suggest small changes that families can make: the same bedtime every day, including weekends; no screens for an hour before sleep; bright light in the morning to reset the clock. These are less dramatic than changing the school day, but they are free, and every family can try them tonight.

readings.title: Reading #15. Air conditioning
text: The history of an invention that makes life more pleasant
Willis Carrier designed the first air-conditioning unit in 1902, just a year after graduating from Cornell University with a Masters in Engineering.

At a Brooklyn printing plant, _fluctuations in heat and moisture_ were causing the size of the printing paper to keep changing slightly, making it hard to align different colours. Carrier's invention made it possible to control temperature and humidity levels and so align the colours. The invention also allowed industries such as film, processed food, textiles and pharmaceuticals to improve the quality of their products.

In 1914, the first air-conditioning device was installed in a private house. However, its size, similar to that of an early computer, meant it _took up too much space_ to come into widespread use, and later models, such as the Weathermaker, which Carrier brought out in the 1920s, _cost too much_ for most people. Cooling for human comfort, rather than industrial need, really took off when three air conditioners were installed in the J.L. Hudson Department Store in Detroit, Michigan. People crowded into the shop to experience the new invention. The fashion spread from department stores to cinemas, whose income rose steeply as a result of the comfort they provided.

To start with, money-conscious employers regarded air conditioning as a luxury. They considered that if they were paying people to work, they should not be paying for them to be comfortable as well. So in the 1940s and '50s, the industry started _putting out a different message_ about its product: according to their research, installing air conditioning _increased productivity_ amongst employees. They found that typists increased their output by 24% when transferred from a regular office to a cooled one. Another study into office working conditions, which was carried out in the late '50s, showed that the majority of companies cited air conditioning as the single most important contributor to efficiency in offices.

However, air conditioning has its critics. Jed Brown, an environmentalist, complains that air conditioning is _a factor in global warming_. Unfortunately, he adds, because air conditioning leads to higher temperatures, people have to use it even more. However, he admits that it provides _a healthier environment_ for many people in the heat of summer.

readings.title: Reading #16. The ballpoint pen
text: Most of us have at least one, but how did this popular item evolve?

One morning in 1945, a crowd of 5,000 people jammed the entrance of Gimbels Department Store in New York. The day before, Gimbels had placed _a full-page advertisement_ in the New York Times for a wonderful new invention, the ballpoint pen. The advertisement described the pen as _'fantastic' and 'miraculous'_. Although they were expensive, $12.50 each, all 10,000 pens in stock were sold on the first day.

In fact, this 'new' pen was not new at all. In 1888, John Loud, a leather manufacturer, had invented a pen with a reservoir of ink and a rolling ball. However, his pen was _never produced_, and efforts by other people to produce a commercially successful one failed too. The main problem was with the ink. If it was too thin, the ink _leaked out_ of the pen. If it was too thick, it _didn't come out of the pen at all_.

Almost fifty years later, in 1935, a newspaper editor in Hungary thought he spent too much time filling his pens with ink. He decided to invent a better kind of pen. With the help of his brother, who was a chemist, he produced a ballpoint pen that _didn't leak when the pen wasn't being used_. The editor was called Ladislas Biro, and it was his name that people would associate more than any other with the ballpoint pen.

By chance, Biro met Augustine Justo, the Argentinian president. Justo was so impressed with Biro's invention that he invited him to set up a factory in Argentina. In 1943, the first Biro pens were produced.

Unfortunately, they were not popular, since the pen _needed to be held in a vertical position_ for the ink to come out. Biro redesigned the pen with a better ball, and in 1944 the new product was on sale throughout Argentina.

It was a North American, Milton Reynolds, who introduced the ballpoint pen to the USA. Copying Biro's design, he produced the version that sold so well at Gimbels. Another American, Patrick Frawley, _improved the design_ and in 1950 began producing a pen he called the Papermate. It was _an immediate success_, and within a few years, Papermates were selling in their millions _around the world_.

readings.title: Why we believe things that are not true
text: Most people think of memory as a recording: something happens, the brain stores it, and later we play it back. Psychologists have shown that this picture is wrong. Memory is closer to a story that we rebuild each time we tell it, and small changes appear at every telling.

In a famous series of experiments in the 1970s, Elizabeth Loftus showed volunteers a short film of a car accident and then asked them questions about it. One group was asked how fast the cars were going when they "hit" each other; another group heard the word "smashed". A week later, those who had heard "smashed" were more than twice as likely to say they had seen broken glass, although there was no broken glass in the film at all.

This does not mean that people were lying. The brain fills gaps automatically, using what seems reasonable. If a word suggests a violent crash, broken glass becomes part of the reasonable picture, and the memory is updated without our permission. Later, the false detail feels exactly like a true one; confidence is no guide to accuracy.

The effect matters outside the laboratory. Courts have relied for centuries on witnesses who say they are certain, and studies of prisoners later cleared by DNA evidence found that mistaken identification played a part in about seventy per cent of the cases. Police forces in several countries now show photographs one at a time rather than together, because comparing faces encourages the brain to choose the "best match" rather than the right one.

None of this makes memory useless. For the general shape of events — who was there, what happened first — it is usually reliable. The danger lies in small, confident details, and the solution is not to trust less but to check more: write things down, keep records, and treat a vivid memory as a good story rather than as evidence.

readings.title: The four-day week experiment
readings.qtype: Multiple choice — IELTS tezligida (vaqt yetmasa zaxira)
text: Between June and December 2022, sixty-one British companies took part in the largest trial of a four-day working week ever organised. About 2,900 employees worked one day less each week for the same pay, on the condition that they maintained their previous level of output.

The companies were of many kinds: software firms, a fish-and-chip shop, a charity, a bank, a small brewery. Researchers from three universities collected data before, during and after the trial. When it ended, fifty-six of the sixty-one companies decided to continue, and eighteen made the change permanent immediately.

The results that attracted most attention were about health. Employees reported that anxiety and tiredness fell, and the number of sick days dropped by about two thirds. The number of staff leaving their jobs fell by more than half compared with the same period a year earlier — a figure that matters to employers, because replacing a trained worker is expensive.

Output did not fall. Company revenue stayed broadly the same during the trial, rising slightly on average, although researchers warned that six months is too short a period to be certain, and that companies willing to join such a trial may be unusual. Some firms achieved the change by shortening meetings; one limited meetings to fifteen minutes unless a longer time was agreed in advance.

Not everything worked smoothly. Businesses that deal with the public, such as shops and clinics, found it harder, because somebody must be present every day; they used staggered days off rather than closing. A few employees said that four longer days left them more tired, and preferred the old pattern. The researchers' conclusion was careful: the model suits many offices, but it is not a rule that fits every workplace.

readings.title: The language that has no numbers
text: In the Amazon rainforest lives a small community, the Pirahã, whose language has fascinated linguists for fifty years. Its most famous feature is what it lacks: there are no words for exact numbers. Speakers use three quantity words, usually translated as "few", "some" and "many", and the same word can mean one or two depending on the situation.

The psychologist Peter Gordon tested this with a simple task. He put out a line of batteries and asked speakers to copy it. With two or three objects they were accurate; with eight or ten, performance fell sharply, even though they clearly understood the task and wanted to succeed. Later researchers, however, found that speakers could copy a line while it stayed in front of them, but the same problems appeared when they had to remember how many objects they had seen.

For some scientists this supports a strong claim: that the words a language gives us shape what we can think. Others reject that conclusion. They point out that exact numbers play almost no part in Pirahã daily life. When some adults asked for evening lessons so that traders could not cheat them, they made little progress, and the classes ended after eight months — but, these researchers say, a few months of lessons cannot replace years of everyday practice. Not having a tool, they argue, is different from being unable to use one.

What is clear is that exact counting is not automatic in humans. Archaeologists find counting marks on bones from at least 20,000 years ago, but writing systems for numbers are much younger, and several languages around the world stop at "three" before moving to "many". Children everywhere learn number words slowly, one at a time, and can take several months to move from "two" to "three" — which suggests that counting is invented and taught, not born with us.

The Pirahã themselves are not troubled by the debate. When a visitor asked why they did not want to count, one man answered that they had everything they needed and did not wish to store things — a reply that says as much about economics as about language.

5 What happened to the counting lessons? A) they continued for years B) they ended after eight months C) children taught the adults D) the traders ran them
6 What does evidence from archaeology suggest? A) numbers are very recent B) counting marks are older than number writing C) all languages count to ten D) children learn numbers quickly
7 How does the writer describe the man's answer? A) angry B) confused C) revealing about economics D) typical of linguists
why: "There are no words for exact numbers".
"With two or three objects they were accurate".
"The same problems appeared when they had to remember how many objects they had seen". A teskari: "could copy a line while it stayed in front of them".
"Not having a tool ... is different from being unable to use one".
"They made little progress, and the classes ended after eight months".
"Counting marks on bones from at least 20,000 years ago, but writing systems for numbers are much younger".
"A reply that says as much about economics as about language".

tasks.title: Tuzoq turlari
items: 1-savol C varianti
4-savol A varianti
5-savol A varianti
6-savol A varianti
why: Uchta miqdor so'zi bor, lekin til uch so'zdan iborat emas.
Bu birinchi olimlar qarashi.
Darslar yillab emas, sakkiz oydan keyin tugagan.
Belgilar qadimiy, yozuv keyinroq.

homework_intro: Bugun biz variantlar orasidagi farqli so'zni topib, uni matndan tekshirishni o'rgandik; uyda endi xuddi shuni yolg'iz o'zingiz bajarasiz.

Birinchi vazifa — "The language that has no numbers" matni: taymerni 12 daqiqaga qo'ying, 7 ta savolni tartib bilan ishlang va har bir javobingiz yoniga matndagi tasdiqlovchi joyni belgilab qo'ying; javoblarga faqat vaqt tugagach qarang.

Ikkinchisi — "Farqli so'z mashqi": 10 juft A/B variantda farqli so'zni belgilaysiz va yonidagi "qanday tekshiraman" ustuniga bir gap yozasiz; uchinchisi — "Tuzoq daftari": bugungi sinf matnlaridan 12 ta noto'g'ri variantni ko'chirib, har biriga turini qo'yasiz — matn qarshi, aytilmagan, qisman to'g'ri yoki juda kuchli so'z.

Eng ko'p qilinadigan xato shu: variantdagi so'z matnda uchragani uchun uni to'g'ri deb belgilash — so'z bor bo'lishi mumkin, lekin savolga javob bermasligi mumkin, shuning uchun har rad etishga sabab yozing; tuzoq daftarida turi ko'rsatilmagan qator qabul qilinmaydi.
Uchalasi qo'shib taxminan yarim soat oladi; keyingi darsning boshida daftaringiz bilan topshirasiz, men esa har savolda "nega qolgan uchtasi noto'g'ri?" deb so'rayman.

homework.title: Uyga matn: "The language that has no numbers"
homework.instr: 12 daqiqada bajaring; javoblar va izohlar Reading bo'limida.
homework.answers: Ustoz rad etish sabablarini so'raydi.

homework.title: Farqli so'z mashqi
homework.instr: 10 juft variant: har juftda farqli so'zni belgilang va matnda uni qanday tekshirishingizni bir gapda yozing.
items: A) The museum is open every day. B) The museum is open most days.
A) Prices rose in 2020. B) Prices fell in 2020.
A) The scientist discovered the drug. B) The scientist tested the drug.
A) The plan was cheap but slow. B) The plan was cheap and fast.
A) Some experts support the idea. B) Most experts support the idea.
A) The writer criticises the report. B) The writer summarises the report.
A) The bridge will be finished next year. B) The bridge was finished last year.
A) Children may benefit from the change. B) Children will definitely benefit from the change.
A) The company moved to a bigger office. B) The company moved to a cheaper office.
A) Only teachers can use the library. B) Teachers can also use the library.
why: Miqdor: matnda muzey yopiladigan kun bormi — tekshiring.
Teskari yo'nalish: narx oshganmi yoki tushganmi.
Boshqa harakat: olim dorini kashf qilganmi yoki faqat sinab ko'rganmi.
Ikkinchi qism farq qiladi: "but slow" va "and fast".
Miqdor: "some" (ba'zilar) va "most" (ko'pchilik).
Muallif hisobotni tanqid qilyaptimi yoki shunchaki qisqacha bayon qilyaptimi.
Zamon va sana: ish tugaganmi yoki hali tugamaganmi.
Ishonch darajasi: "may" — ehtimol, "will definitely" — juda kuchli.
Ko'chish sababi: kattaroq joymi yoki arzonroq joymi.
"Only" — cheklov, "also" — qo'shimcha imkoniyat.

homework.title: Tuzoq daftari
homework.instr: Bugungi sinf matnlaridan 12 ta noto'g'ri variantni yozing va turini belgilang: matn qarshi / aytilmagan / qisman to'g'ri / juda kuchli.
homework.answers: Tur ko'rsatilmagan qator qabul qilinmaydi.

kahoot.q: In IELTS Reading multiple choice, in what order do the answers usually come?
options: In the same order as the text
kahoot.explain: Reading MCQ javoblari matn tartibida keladi: keyingi javob odatda oldingisidan keyin turadi.

kahoot.q: Two options look almost the same. What should you do first?
options: Find the one word that is different
Choose the one with more words from the text
Pick the longer of the two options
Skip both and guess at the end
kahoot.explain: Ikki variant farqi ko'pincha bitta so'zda bo'ladi — o'sha so'zni topib, faqat uni matndan tekshirasiz.

kahoot.q: An option contains a word that also appears in the text. What does this prove?
options: Nothing until you check the meaning
It is certainly the correct answer
The other three options are wrong
It is always a trap option
kahoot.explain: Matndagi so'z tuzoq variantda ham bo'ladi; faqat ma'no mos kelsa, variant to'g'ri.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Most visitors came by bus.' Option: 'All visitors came by bus.' The option is…
options: right: the verb and the place match
impossible to check in the text
kahoot.explain: "All" (hammasi) "most" (ko'pchilik) dan kuchliroq — variant matndan ko'proq narsani da'vo qiladi.

kahoot.q: Which word in an option is often a warning sign?
kahoot.explain: "Only", "always", "never", "all" kabi mutlaq so'zlar ko'pincha variantni noto'g'ri qiladi — matn kamdan-kam mutlaq gapiradi.

kahoot.q: An option has two parts. The first part is true, but the second is false. The option is…
options: wrong, because it is only partly true
correct, because most of it is true
correct if the first part is the key one
a safe choice when time is short
kahoot.explain: Qisman to'g'ri variant — tuzoq: ikkala qism ham matnga mos kelishi shart.

kahoot.q: Text: 'The council suggested a new bus route in 2019.' Option: 'The council approved a new bus route in 2019.' The option is…
options: right: the two verbs mean the same
right: the date and the topic match
not possible to check in the text
kahoot.explain: Taklif qilish (suggest) va tasdiqlash (approve) — boshqa-boshqa harakat; sana mos kelgani yetarli emas.

kahoot.q: What should you write next to each option you reject?
options: A short reason why it is wrong
The answer to the next question
A new option of your own
kahoot.explain: Har rad etilgan variantga sabab yoziladi: matn qarshi, aytilmagan, qisman to'g'ri yoki juda kuchli.

kahoot.q: An option is true according to the text, but it does not answer the question. It is…
options: a trap — true, but not the answer
the answer, because it is true
the answer, if it is near the start
kahoot.explain: Matnda bor, lekin savolga javob bo'lmagan variant — eng ko'p uchraydigan tuzoq; avval savol nimani so'rayotganini aniqlang.

kahoot.q: Question: 'Why was the bridge built?' Text: 'It was built to reduce traffic; as a result, shops lost customers.' Answer:
kahoot.explain: Savol MAQSADni so'rayapti (to reduce traffic); "shops lost customers" — natija, maqsad emas.

kahoot.q: A question is very long. What is the best first step?
options: Split it: who, what, which part?
Read all four options very quickly
Look for the longest option first
Skip it and never come back
kahoot.explain: Uzun savolni qismlarga bo'ling: kim haqida, nima so'ralyapti, matnning qaysi qismi.

kahoot.q: Time is almost over and you are not sure. What should you do?
options: Write two letters to be safe
Write the answer in full words
kahoot.explain: Bo'sh javob ball bermaydi: eng ehtimolli variantni tanlang, lekin faqat bitta harf yozing.

kahoot.q: 'Humidity' is closest in meaning to…
kahoot.explain: Humidity — namlik, havodagi suv bug'i miqdori.

kahoot.q: Electric scooters really ___ off in our city last summer. (= became popular)
kahoot.explain: Take off — to'satdan ommalashmoq, tez rivojlanmoq (o'tgan zamonda: took off).

kahoot.q: A 'luxury' is something that is…
options: needed by everyone to stay alive
kahoot.explain: Luxury — hashamat: yoqimli, lekin zarur bo'lmagan (ko'pincha qimmat) narsa.

kahoot.q: Which word means 'how much work a person or company produces'?
kahoot.explain: Productivity — unumdorlik; profitability esa foyda keltirish darajasi.

kahoot.q: A 'critic' of a new law is a person who…
options: says what is wrong with it
helped to write and pass it
has to obey it every day
kahoot.explain: Critic — tanqidchi: biror narsaning kamchiligini aytadigan odam.

kahoot.q: If a water bottle 'leaks', the water…
options: turns a strange colour after a day
kahoot.explain: Leak — oqib chiqmoq: suyuqlik chiqmasligi kerak bo'lgan joydan chiqadi.

kahoot.q: A 'reliable' source of information is one you can…
kahoot.explain: Reliable — ishonchli: unga ishonsa bo'ladi.

kahoot.q: In a court case, a 'witness' is a person who…
kahoot.explain: Witness — guvoh: voqeani o'z ko'zi bilan ko'rgan odam.

lessons.title: Listening: Sentence Completion (Part 2)
lessons.grammar_topic: Sentence completion — gapni to'ldirish (2-bo'lim, monolog)
lessons.book_ref: Jony Academy materiali — ustoz bergan audiolar (Track 22 Electronics exhibition, Track 10 Joe) va 3 ta mualliflik skripti.
objectives: Part 2 (bitta so'zlovchi, monolog) formatiga ko'nikish: asosiy ish — wildlife park va summer festival monologlarida; Track 22 va Track 10 — dialog (Part 1 uslubidagi sentence completion), isinish uchun.
Bo'sh joyni grammatik jihatdan to'g'ri to'ldirish: ot, fe'l, son yoki sifat.
Gapdagi kalit so'zga qarab audio bo'yicha "qayerdaman" degan savolga javob berish.
Paraphrase kutish: gapda bir so'z, audioda boshqasi.
So'z chegarasini va grammatik mosligini tekshirish (birlik/ko'plik, zamon).
materials: Audio: ielts5_12_exhibition.mp3 (Track 22, Electronics exhibition) va ielts5_12_joe_habits.mp3 (Track 10, Joe) — kolonka darsdan oldin ulanib, ovozi sinab ko'riladi; har ikkalasi faqat BIR MARTA qo'yiladi.
Sinf savol varaqlari — Electronics exhibition 1–6, Joe 1–6, wildlife park 10 gap va summer festival 12 gap: har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa, javobsiz va transkriptsiz.
Ustoz nusxasi: 3 ta Jony Academy skripti (wildlife park, summer festival, sports hall) yirik shriftda chop etilgan — bular audio emas, ustoz ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi.
Doskaga dars boshlanishidan oldin yoziladi: 6 bosqich (o'qi — turkumni belgila — kalit so'z — paraphrase — yoz — gapni qayta o'qi) va to'rt belgi: ot / fe'l / son / sifat.
Doskaning o'ng yarmi "gapdagi so'z — audiodagi so'z" ikki ustuni uchun bo'sh qoldiriladi: paraphrase juftlari (deals with — is all about, checking — measuring) shu yerga yoziladi.

Sekundomer yoki telefon taymeri (har skriptdan oldin gaplarni o'qishga 45 soniya) va uyga vazifa varag'i: "Introduction to the sports hall" 10 gapi + bashorat mashqining 15 gapi, har o'quvchida xatolar daftari va qalam.

Sports hall skripti (10 gap), Bashorat mashqi (15 gap) va Xato tahlili uyga; xatolar daftari to'ldiriladi

intro: Sentence completion — to'liq gap beriladi, ichida bo'sh joy bor. Javob gapga GRAMMATIK jihatdan mos tushishi shart.
Avval gapni o'qing va bo'sh joydan oldingi va keyingi so'zga qarang: "a ___ of" — ot; "will ___ the cost" — fe'l.
Part 2 monolog: so'zlovchi mavzu bo'ylab tartib bilan yuradi. Savollar ham shu tartibda.
Paraphrase: gapda "students can borrow", audioda "students are allowed to take out". Ma'no bir xil, so'z boshqa.
Javobni yozgach gapni ichingizda to'liq o'qing: mantiq va grammatika to'g'rimi?
Ko'p uchraydigan xato: javobni audiodan eshitilgandek yozib, gapga mos kelmasligi (masalan, "to go" o'rniga "going").
So'z chegarasi buzilmasin: "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS" bo'lsa, uch so'z — 0 ball.
presentation: Javob gapga mos kelmayapti. Nima qilay?
Shaklni o'zgartiring: -ing, -s yoki infinitiv kerak bo'lishi mumkin.
Audioda boshqa so'z eshitdim.
Bu paraphrase bo'lishi mumkin — ma'noga qarang.
Bo'sh joy oldida "a" bor.

Keyingi so'zga ham qarang. "Please take a ___." — birlikdagi sanaladigan ot (a map). "Buy a ___ ticket" — bo'sh joydan keyin ot bor, demak bo'sh joyga uni aniqlovchi so'z kerak (a family ticket, a student ticket).
Ikki so'z eshitdim, chegarada bitta.

Bo'sh joy atrofidagi so'zlarni tekshiring: gapda bor so'zni takrorlamang. Masalan, "Meet at the ___ station" uchun "bus station" eshitsangiz, faqat "bus" yoziladi. Qaysi so'z kerakligini gap hal qiladi.
Part 2 da nechta so'zlovchi?
Odatda bitta: kundalik mavzudagi tanishtiruv, e'lon yoki radio ko'rsatuv (akademik ma'ruza esa Part 4 da).
Javoblar tartibdami?
Ha, sentence completion tartibda keladi.
notes: Ustoz gaplarni o'qish uchun 45 soniya beradi; keyin skriptni BIR MARTA o'qiydi.
Tekshirishda har javob uchun grammatik asosni so'rang: "nega -ing?", "nega ko'plik?".
Transkriptdan paraphrase juftlarini yozdiring: gapda — audioda.
Xatolarni uch turga ajrating: eshitish, grammatika, so'z chegarasi.

class_ex.title: So'z turkumini bashorat qiling
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi, o'quvchi bo'sh joyga qanday so'z kerakligini aytadi.
items: "The museum offers a free ___ for school groups."
"Visitors must ___ their bags at the entrance."
"The tour lasts about ___ minutes."
"The café is open from ___ until ten."
"The new hall is ___ than the old one."
"Students can borrow up to ___ books."
why: "A ... for" — birlikdagi ot.
"Must" dan keyin infinitiv.
"Minutes" oldida raqam.
"From ... until" oraliq.
"Than" solishtiruvni bildiradi.
"Up to ... books".
class_ex.note: Bashorat qilingach, audioda faqat o'sha turdagi so'zni kutasiz.

listenings.title: Track 22. Electronics exhibition — ticket options
intro: Irina elektronika ko'rgazmasida chipta haqida so'rayapti; xodim bo'limlarni tushuntiradi. Avval 6 ta gapni o'qing va har bo'sh joyga qanday so'z kerakligini ayting (fe'l? ot?). Keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Write ONE WORD ONLY for each answer. Gaplar bo'limlar tartibida: 1–2 — birinchi bo'lim, 3–5 — ikkinchi, 6 — uchinchi.
transcript: IRINA: Good morning. Can you tell me about the ticket options, please?

MAN: Certainly, we've got various options, depending on whether you want to just visit parts of the exhibition or all of it. It's organised into various different sections, and because it's so large, you may not be interested in everything or have time for everything. You can buy tickets just for the sections you want to visit, and that makes it a lot cheaper.
IRINA: Well, um, I've really come here to see things to do with electronics.

MAN: Right. Then I think you'll find the first part of the exhibition as you go in is quite relevant. It's all about electronics and how we can use them to protect the world around us – you know, the environment and what we can do to avoid damaging it further.
IRINA: Protecting the environment. That sounds interesting. Anything I should specially look out for there?

MAN: There are lots of new devices. One which fascinated me when I went round was a new instrument for measuring how the temperature of the ocean changes at different levels, and this can be done from a ship on the surface right down to the bottom.
IRINA: Great, I'll look out for that.

MAN: OK, and I see you've got your son with you, which is nice because the subject of the next section is all about different things for keeping an eye on your children and looking after their safety. It contains a range of things, from electronic instruments used in medicine to children's electronic games and even a number of new devices to prevent children from having an accident when they're at home.
IRINA: That sounds useful.

MAN: Yes, there's even an invention for older children – you'll see a demonstration of it while you're there – which helps parents to make sure their kids are going to school. Really useful in families where both parents work. It sort of electronically tells parents about their kids' attendance and sends them a signal via the Internet.
IRINA: Very convenient. But my son is a bit young to worry about that yet. Are there any other sections which feature electronics?

MAN: Sure. There's another section – it's the third you come to, I think – which should interest everyone. It contains lots of new electronic instruments or devices for looking after and working with money – you know, like that thing you must have heard of which counts what you're putting into your supermarket trolley and adds up the bill as you go around.
IRINA: Right, money – that sounds interesting, too. Well, thanks for the information. I'd like tickets for myself and my son for those three sections, then, please.

tasks.title: Questions 1–6: Electronics exhibition — complete the sentences
tasks.instr: Gaplar audio tartibida (ALWAYS). Javob gapga grammatik mos kelishi shart.
items: The first section deals with electronics designed to ___ the environment.
One new device is for checking ___ temperatures at different levels.
The theme of the second section is children and their ___.
There are a number of inventions to avoid an ___ in the home.
They demonstrate a device for checking if older children are at ___.
The third section contains devices for dealing with ___.
why: "How we can use them to protect the world around us – you know, the environment". "Designed to ___" — fe'l (asos shakl). Tuzoq: "protecting" — gapga mos emas.
"Measuring how the temperature of the ocean changes at different levels". Checking = measuring. Tuzoq: "ship", "surface" — o'lchanadigan narsa emas.
"Keeping an eye on your children and looking after their safety". "Their ___" — ot.
"Devices to prevent children from having an accident when they're at home". Avoid = prevent. "An" — unli bilan boshlanadigan ot.
"Helps parents to make sure their kids are going to school". Checking = make sure. Tuzoq: "Internet" — signal yuborish yo'li, joy emas.
"Devices for looking after and working with money". Dealing with = working with.
tasks.note: Kalit transkript bo'yicha tekshirilgan; har javob bitta so'z. Tekshirishda har javobning grammatik asosini so'rang (fe'l, ot, artikl).

checking

2 va 5-savollar.
