listenings.title: Track 10. Joe — buying electronics
listenings.qtype: Sentence completion (1–6) — dialog (Part 1 uslubida), qo'shimcha mashq
intro: Kompaniya xodimi Joedan elektronika sotib olish odatlari haqida so'raydi. Avval gaplarni o'qing, bo'sh joy turini bashorat qiling, keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Write ONE WORD for each answer.
transcript: WOMAN: Hello, Joe, good to see you again.
JOE: Hi, you too.
WOMAN: So, how did you get on with the devices we asked you to test for us?
JOE: Oh, fine. Well, mostly.

WOMAN: OK, well, we'll come back to those in a minute. First of all, I was wondering if I could ask you a few questions about your attitude to new electrical products. This will help us with future marketing. Is that OK?
JOE: Sure.
WOMAN: OK. First of all, how much do you spend on electronic items a month?

JOE: Hmm, let me see. I don't earn a lot, so I don't have much left after I've paid for things like rent, bills, food and so on. Anything else is a luxury. So I'd guess about five percent, maybe ten percent of my monthly salary.
WOMAN: All right, and what influences you in your choice of product? Say you wanted a new mobile phone, how would you decide which one to buy?

JOE: Well, first I look at reviews on the Internet, you know, what other customers think about them. Then I'll ask my friends what they think. In fact, their opinions are probably more important than anything.
WOMAN: How much does advertising help you choose a product?
JOE: I think that depends on how the product is advertised and who is advertising it.
WOMAN: For example?
JOE: Well, if it's someone I respect, you know, like a famous sportsman or actor, that can certainly make a difference. I know it shouldn't really, but it does.
WOMAN: And where do you buy most of these products? The high street, the Internet?
JOE: Most people seem to avoid shops these days, don't they, for things like that? They think they can get things cheaper on the Internet.
WOMAN: Right.
JOE: But I find that if you say to a shop assistant that you can get a new camera, for example, for a hundred pounds on the Internet, they'll often match the price. So that's where I go.
WOMAN: Any other advantages?

JOE: Well, you get personal service, and you don't have to wait for the product to be delivered. Ordering online means you have to wait, sometimes for ages, to get the things you've just bought. I hate that. I guess I'm just very impatient.
WOMAN: OK, one final question. Do you ever see a product and think, I've absolutely got to get one of those?

JOE: Oh, all the time, especially if I'm walking past a shop and I see a new electronic item in the window. Especially if it's unusual, you know, something I've never seen before. It takes a lot of willpower.

tasks.title: Questions 1–6: Complete the sentences
items: Joe's low ___ doesn't allow him to buy many electronic goods.
He's often influenced by his ___ when he buys electronic items.
Advertisements featuring somebody ___ sometimes help him decide which product to buy.
Joe prefers to get new products from ___.
He doesn't like waiting for a long time after ___ something.
He finds it hard to resist buying electronic products if they are new and ___.
why: "I don't earn a lot ... about five percent, maybe ten percent of my monthly salary". "Low ___" — ot. "Income" ham ma'noga mos, lekin audioda "salary" eshitiladi.
"I'll ask my friends ... their opinions are probably more important than anything". Tuzoq: "reviews on the Internet" — birinchi qadam, lekin eng muhimi do'stlar.
"Someone I respect, you know, like a famous sportsman or actor". "Somebody ___" — sifat.
"Most people seem to avoid shops ... So that's where I go". Tuzoq: "the Internet" — boshqalar tanlovi.

"Ordering online means you have to wait, sometimes for ages ... I hate that". "After ___ something" — -ing shakl. "Buying" ma'noga yaqin, lekin audioda aytilgan so'z — "ordering"; kalit faqat "ordering".
"Especially if it's unusual, you know, something I've never seen before. It takes a lot of willpower". Hard to resist = takes a lot of willpower.
tasks.note: Kalit transkript bo'yicha tekshirilgan; har javob bitta so'z. 3-savolda sifat (somebody ___), 5-savolda -ing shakl (after ___) kerak — tekshirishda shuni so'rang.

tasks.title: Grammatika tekshiruvi
items: 3-savol: famous
5-savol: ordering
4-savol: shops
why: "somebody + sifat" (somebody famous).
"after + -ing" (after ordering).
"from shops" — umumiy ma'no.

listenings.title: Welcome talk at a wildlife park
intro: Tabiat bog'iga kirishdagi tanishtiruv. BIR MARTA tinglang; gaplarni to'ldiring.
Ko'rsatma: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER for each answer.
transcript: GUIDE: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Ashcroft Wildlife Park. My name's Olivia and I'll give you a short introduction before you go in.
GUIDE: The park opened in 1974 as a small farm with six species. Today we care for just over four hundred animals, and about half of them were born here.

GUIDE: The park covers 60 hectares, so please take a map — they're free, next to the ticket desk. If you'd rather not walk, the land train runs every twenty minutes from the main gate, and it's included in your ticket.

GUIDE: A few rules. Please don't feed the animals: our diets are prepared by a nutritionist and even a piece of bread can make an animal ill. Keep your voice down near the big cats, especially in the morning, when they are most active. And children under twelve must stay with an adult at all times.

GUIDE: Now, what to see. The most popular area is the wetland walk, where you can see storks and otters. The best time for the otters is feeding time at half past eleven. The reptile house is warm, so leave your coat in the cloakroom; it's free but you'll need a two-pound coin, which you get back.
GUIDE: For lunch, the restaurant serves hot food until three o'clock, and the picnic area behind the education centre is open all day. There's a water fountain there, so you can refill your bottles.

GUIDE: Finally, if you would like to support us, you can adopt an animal for thirty pounds a year. The money pays for food and veterinary care, and you receive a photograph and two free tickets. Enjoy your visit.

tasks.title: Sentence completion
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER
items: The park first opened in ___.
There are now over ___ animals in the park.
The park covers ___ hectares.
The land train leaves every ___ minutes.
Visitors must not ___ the animals.
Children under ___ must stay with an adult.
The otters are fed at ___.
The cloakroom needs a ___ coin.
Hot food is served until ___.
You can adopt an animal for ___ a year.
why: "The park opened in 1974 as a small farm".
"Just over four hundred animals".
"The park covers 60 hectares".
"Runs every twenty minutes".
"Please don't feed the animals" — fe'l kerak.
"Children under twelve".
"Feeding time at half past eleven". Raqam bilan yozing: "half past eleven" — 3 so'z, TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER chegarasidan oshadi.
"You'll need a two-pound coin". "£2" ham to'g'ri: gapda "coin" bor, "pound" so'zi yo'q.
"The restaurant serves hot food until three o'clock".
"Adopt an animal for thirty pounds a year".

tasks.title: Paraphrase va grammatika
items: "Visitors must not ___ the animals" — nega "feed"?
"over ___ animals" — nega raqam?
Audioda "included in your ticket" — qaysi gapga tegishli?
Chalg'ituvchi: "six species"
why: "Feeding" yozilsa grammatik xato.
Son kutiladi.
Poyezd chiptaga kiritilgan.
Hozirgi son 400 dan ortiq.

listenings.title: Radio announcement: the summer festival
intro: Radio orqali yozgi festival haqida e'lon. BIR MARTA tinglang.
transcript: PRESENTER: And now the details of this year's Riverside Summer Festival, which starts on Friday the 9th of August and runs for three days.

PRESENTER: The festival has moved. For the last eleven years it was held in Castle Park, but the ground there was damaged by flooding in spring, so this year everything takes place on the school playing fields on Ashton Road.

PRESENTER: Tickets are ten pounds for adults and free for anyone under sixteen. A weekend pass costs twenty-five, which saves you five pounds, and you can buy it online until Thursday evening; after that, tickets are only available at the gate, and cash only, so please come prepared.

PRESENTER: There is no parking on site. The organisers ask visitors to use the station car park, which is a ten-minute walk away, or to take the number 4 bus, which will run every fifteen minutes until midnight on all three days.

PRESENTER: Music starts at two in the afternoon on Friday, but on Saturday and Sunday the gates open at eleven in the morning for the food market. There will be thirty stalls this year, twice as many as last summer.

PRESENTER: The main stage closes at eleven at night because of noise rules, but the acoustic tent continues until one. Please remember that glass bottles are not allowed; you can bring your own plastic bottle and fill it at the water points.

PRESENTER: All profits this year go to the children's hospital, which last year received nine thousand pounds from the festival. Volunteers are still needed, especially for Sunday afternoon; if you can help, call the number on our website.

tasks.title: Sentence completion
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER
items: The festival begins on ___ August.
It lasts for ___ days.
This year it is held on the school ___ on Ashton Road.
Entry is free for people under ___.
A weekend pass saves you ___ pounds.
At the gate you can pay only by ___.
Visitors should park at the ___ car park.
The number 4 bus runs every ___ minutes.
On Saturday the gates open at ___ for the food market.
There will be ___ food stalls.
The acoustic tent stays open until ___.
___ bottles are not allowed.
why: "Starts on Friday the 9th of August".
"Runs for three days".
"Everything takes place on the school playing fields".
"Free for anyone under sixteen".
"Which saves you five pounds".
"Tickets are only available at the gate, and cash only".
"Use the station car park".
"Every fifteen minutes until midnight".
"The gates open at eleven in the morning".
"There will be thirty stalls this year".
"The acoustic tent continues until one".
"Glass bottles are not allowed".

tasks.title: Chalg'ituvchilar
items: "Castle Park"
"ten pounds" (weekend pass)
"midnight" (main stage)
"fifteen stalls"
why: "For the last eleven years it was held in Castle Park" — bu yil boshqa joyda.
10 funt — kattalar uchun bir kunlik chipta; hafta oxiri passi 25 funt turadi va 3 kunga 5 funt tejaydi.
Asosiy sahna 11 da yopiladi.
Bu yil 30, ya'ni ikki barobar.

listenings.title: Introduction to the sports hall
intro: Yangi sport zali haqida tanishtiruv. Uyda bir marta tinglang (audio bo'lmasa — birovga bir marta o'qitib eshiting).
transcript: MANAGER: Hello everyone, and thank you for coming to the opening week of the Northside Sports Hall.
MANAGER: The building took eighteen months to complete and cost four million pounds, half of which came from the city council and half from a national sports fund.

MANAGER: The main hall can be divided into three courts, so we can run badminton, basketball and volleyball at the same time. The floor is made of wood rather than plastic, because it is better for the knees, and it took five weeks to lay.

MANAGER: Downstairs you'll find the fitness room with forty machines, and next to it a studio for classes such as yoga and dance. Classes must be booked in advance; the most popular is spinning on Tuesday evenings, which fills up about two days before.
MANAGER: Membership costs thirty-two pounds a month, but if you pay for a year you get one month free. Students, over-sixties and anyone who lives in the two streets nearest the hall pay twenty-four.
MANAGER: Opening hours are six in the morning until ten at night on weekdays. At weekends we close at eight, apart from the swimming pool, which stays open an hour longer.

MANAGER: A few requests. Please bring a towel to the fitness room and wipe the machines after use. Outdoor shoes are not allowed on the wooden floor — there is a rack for them by the door. And the lockers are free, but you must empty them before you leave; anything left is given to charity after a month.
MANAGER: Finally, we are looking for a full-time receptionist and two part-time coaches. Details are on the noticeboard next to the café.

tasks.title: Sentence completion
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER
items: The building took ___ months to finish.
It cost ___ pounds in total.
The main hall divides into ___ courts.
The floor is made of ___.
The fitness room has ___ machines.
The most popular class is ___.
Standard membership costs ___ a month.
On weekdays the hall closes at ___.
Members must bring a ___ to the fitness room.
Items left in lockers are given to ___ after a month.
why: "Took eighteen months to complete".
"Cost four million pounds". Gapda "pounds" bor, shuning uchun "£4m" yoki "four million pounds" yozilmaydi — faqat son.
"Can be divided into three courts".
"The floor is made of wood rather than plastic".
"The fitness room with forty machines".
"The most popular is spinning on Tuesday evenings".
"Membership costs thirty-two pounds a month". 24 — chegirmali narx.
"Six in the morning until ten at night on weekdays".
"Please bring a towel to the fitness room".
"Anything left is given to charity after a month".

tasks.title: Grammatika tekshiruvi
items: "The floor is made of ___"
"Members must bring a ___"
"It cost ___ pounds"
"closes at ___"
why: "Wood" — to'g'ri; "wooden" bu yerda mos emas.
"A towel" — "towels" xato bo'lardi.
"Four million" (yoki "4 million", "4,000,000") — chegaraga sig'adi; "pounds" gapda bor, uni takrorlamang.
Raqam bilan yozish tez va xavfsiz.

homework_intro: Bugun gapni oldin o'qib, bo'sh joyga qanday so'z kerakligini aytib olib, keyin bir marta tinglab to'ldirdik — uyga vazifa ham aynan shu, faqat endi buni yolg'iz o'zingiz, ustozsiz qilasiz.

Birinchi vazifa — "Introduction to the sports hall" skripti: avval 10 gapni 45 soniya o'qib chiqing va har bo'sh joyning chetiga ot / fe'l / son / sifat deb belgilab qo'ying, keyin FAQAT BIR MARTA eshiting (audio bo'lmasa — birovga bir marta o'qitib eshiting), to'xtatmang, transkriptni esa hammasini to'ldirib bo'lganingizdan keyin oching; hammasi 10 daqiqa.

Ikkinchisi — "Bashorat mashqi": 15 gap beriladi, audio yo'q, har gapga faqat bo'sh joy turini (ot / fe'l / son / sifat) yozasiz, 10 daqiqa; uchinchisi — "Xato tahlili": bugungi skriptlardagi xatolaringizni uch turga ajratib, har tur uchun kamida bitta misol yozasiz — eshitish, grammatika, so'z chegarasi.

Eng ko'p qilinadigan xato — javobni audiodan eshitilgandek ko'chirib qo'yish: bugungi wildlife park'da "Visitors must not ___ the animals" ga "feeding" emas, "feed" yoziladi, Track 22 da "designed to ___ the environment" ga "protecting" emas, "protect" — shuning uchun har javobdan keyin gapni boshidan oxirigacha qayta o'qing va ikki so'z chegarasidan oshmang.
Uchala vazifani ham keyingi dars boshida daftar ochiq holda stolga qo'yasiz, javoblarni birga tekshiramiz va men har javob uchun "nega aynan shu shakl?" deb so'rayman.

homework.title: 3-skript: "Introduction to the sports hall"
homework.instr: Uyda bir marta tinglang (audio bo'lmasa — birovga bir marta o'qitib eshiting), gaplarni to'ldiring, keyin transkript bilan tekshiring.
homework.answers: Javoblar Listening bo'limida izoh bilan.

homework.title: Bashorat mashqi
homework.instr: 15 ta gap: audiosiz, har bo'sh joyga qanday so'z kerakligini yozing (ot / fe'l / son / sifat) va sababini ayting.
items: "The tour of the old town starts at the ___ of the bridge."
"Visitors are asked to ___ their phones during the film."
"The swimming pool is ___ metres long."
"Tickets are cheaper for groups of more than ___ people."
"The new library is much ___ than the old one."
"Please bring a ___ and a pair of gloves."
"The workshop is suitable for complete ___."
"The guide recommends ___ comfortable shoes."
"The castle was built in the ___ century."
"The café closes at ___ on Sundays."
"Children must be ___ by an adult at all times."
"Parking costs £___ per hour."
"The museum shop sells ___ souvenirs."
"The talk will explain how to ___ energy at home."
"There are several ___ near the main entrance."
why: "The ___ of" — artikl va "of" orasida ot turadi (masalan, end, foot).
"Asked to ___" — "to" dan keyin fe'lning asos shakli (switch off).
"___ metres" — o'lchov birligi oldida son.
"More than ___ people" — miqdor, son kerak.
"Much ___ than" — "than" qiyoslashni bildiradi: bigger, quieter.
"A ___" — birlikdagi sanaladigan ot (hat, torch).
"Complete ___" — artikl yo'q, "complete" sifatidan keyin ot keladi; ma'no bo'yicha ko'plik: beginners.
"Recommend" dan keyin -ing shakl: recommends wearing.
"The ___ century" — tartib son: 15th.
"Closes at ___" — soat, ya'ni son yoki vaqt.
"Must be ___ by" — majhul nisbat, fe'lning III shakli: accompanied, supervised.
"£___" — pul belgisidan keyin faqat son.
"Sells ___ souvenirs" — ot oldida sifat: cheap, local.
"How to ___" — "to" dan keyin fe'lning asos shakli: save.
"Several ___" — "several" dan keyin ko'plikdagi ot: shops, benches.

homework.title: Xato tahlili
homework.instr: Bugungi 4 ta mashqdagi (2 audio, 2 skript) xatolaringizni uch turga ajrating: eshitish, grammatika, so'z chegarasi.
homework.answers: Har tur uchun kamida bitta misol.

kahoot.q: What should you do BEFORE the recording starts?
options: Predict the word type for each gap
Try to write down every word you hear
Read the transcript at the back
Close your eyes and just relax
kahoot.explain: Tinglashdan oldin gaplarni o'qib, har bo'sh joyga qanday so'z (ot, fe'l, son, sifat) kerakligini aniqlang.

kahoot.q: Gap: 'Guests should ___ their keys at reception.' What kind of word is needed?
options: a verb in the base form
a noun in the plural form
kahoot.explain: "Should" dan keyin fe'lning asos shakli keladi (leave, return).

kahoot.q: Gap: 'There is a small ___ for each visitor.' What does 'a' before the gap tell you?
options: a verb in the past tense
kahoot.explain: "A small ___ for" — artikl va sifatdan keyin, bo'sh joydan keyin ot yo'q: birlikdagi sanaladigan ot kerak (a small gift, a small fee).

kahoot.q: Instructions: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER. Which answer breaks the rule?
kahoot.explain: "A large wooden box" — 4 so'z; ko'pi bilan 2 so'z va/yoki bitta son yozish mumkin.

kahoot.q: You hear: 'It's an eight-minute walk from the station.' Gap: 'The hotel is ___ minutes from the station.' You write:
kahoot.explain: Gapda "minutes" bor, shuning uchun faqat son yoziladi: 8 (yoki eight).

kahoot.q: The sentence says 'not allowed'. The speaker says 'forbidden'. This is…
kahoot.explain: Ma'no bir xil, so'z boshqa — bu paraphrase; IELTS da gap va audio ko'pincha shunday farq qiladi.

kahoot.q: You hear: 'The class was on Monday, but it has moved to Wednesday.' Gap: 'The class is now on ___.'
kahoot.explain: "Was on Monday" — eski ma'lumot (chalg'ituvchi); "has moved to Wednesday" — yangi, to'g'ri javob.

kahoot.q: Gap: 'You can relax after ___ the tour.' Which form fits?
kahoot.explain: "After" predlogidan keyin fe'lning -ing shakli keladi: after finishing.

kahoot.q: How many times do you hear each recording in the IELTS Listening test?
kahoot.explain: IELTS Listening da har audio faqat BIR MARTA eshittiriladi.

kahoot.q: You have written an answer. What should you do next?
options: Write a second answer next to it
Change it to a longer word
kahoot.explain: Javobni yozgach gapni to'liq qayta o'qing: grammatika va ma'no mos kelishi kerak.

kahoot.q: Gap: 'Please bring two ___ to the first lesson.' You hear: 'You'll need a couple of photographs.' You write:
kahoot.explain: "Two ___" dan keyin ko'plikdagi ot kerak: photographs.

kahoot.q: You hear 'seventeen pounds'. Gap: 'A ticket costs £___.' What do you write?
kahoot.explain: Gapda "£" belgisi bor, shuning uchun faqat son yoziladi; "pounds" ni takrorlash xato.

kahoot.q: An 'exhibition' is…
kahoot.explain: Exhibition — ko'rgazma: buyumlar hammaga ko'rsatiladigan tadbir.

kahoot.q: A 'device' is…
options: a detailed plan for the future
kahoot.explain: Device — qurilma, moslama; "advice" (maslahat) bilan adashtirmang.

kahoot.q: High 'attendance' at a football match means that…
options: the match lasted a long time
kahoot.explain: Attendance — qatnashuv, davomat: tadbir yoki darsga kelgan odamlar (soni).

kahoot.q: 'Willpower' is the ability to…
options: speak well in front of people
kahoot.explain: Willpower — iroda kuchi: o'zingizni boshqarish qobiliyati (masalan, keraksiz narsani sotib olmaslik yoki har kuni o'qishga o'zingizni majburlash).

kahoot.q: Where do you leave your coat in a theatre or museum?
kahoot.explain: Cloakroom — kiyimxona (garderob), palto va sumkalar qoldiriladigan joy.

kahoot.q: A 'volunteer' is a person who works…
kahoot.explain: Volunteer — ko'ngilli: pul olmasdan ishlaydigan odam.

kahoot.q: After the storm there was 'flooding' in the town. This means…
kahoot.explain: Flooding — suv toshqini: suv yerni, ko'chalarni bosadi.

kahoot.q: Which word means 'different kinds of animals or plants'?
kahoot.explain: Species — biologik tur; spices — ziravorlar, spaces — bo'sh joylar.

lessons.title: Listening: Pick from a List (Part 2-3)
lessons.grammar_topic: Pick from a list (listening) — ro'yxatdan ikki (yoki uch) javob tanlash
lessons.book_ref: Jony Academy materiali — ustoz bergan audiolar (Track 23 Irina survey, Track 11 Joe devices) va 3 ta mualliflik skripti.
objectives: "Choose TWO letters" listening savolida ikkala javobni ham eshitib topish.
Savol va 5 ta variantni (A–E) tinglashdan OLDIN o'qib, kalit so'zlarni belgilash.
Chalg'ituvchi variantlarni ajratish: audioda tilga olinadi, lekin inkor qilinadi yoki boshqa narsa haqida.
Har javob alohida ball olishini bilish — bittasini eshitib qolsangiz ham yozing.
5 ta mashqda (2 ta ustoz audiosi + 3 ta skript) ishlash.
materials: Track 23 (Irina) savol varag'i: 7–10-savollar va har biriga A–E variantlar — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa; transkript faqat ustozda, tekshirishdan keyin tarqatiladi.
Track 11 (Joe) savol varag'i: 1–4-savollar va A–E variantlar — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa.
Ikki audio — ielts5_13_irina_survey.mp3 va ielts5_13_joe_devices.mp3 — qo'ng'iroqdan oldin kolonkaga ulanib, ovozi sinab ko'rilsin va fayl boshiga qaytarilsin (har biri BIR MARTA qo'yiladi).

Doskaga dars boshlanishidan oldin ikki ustun yoziladi: INKOR — but, however, not, decided not, I'm not keen on; TASDIQ — really like, that's great, definitely. "Tasdiq yoki inkor?" sinf mashqi shu ustunlarga tayanadi.
3 ta skript chop etilgan holda ustoz qo'lida (Foto klub, Ko'ngillilar kuni, Maya — Dr Reed) — audiosi yo'q, ustoz ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi.
Har o'quvchiga "Chalg'ituvchi tahlili" uchun 3 ustunli bo'sh jadval: variant | audioda qanday eshitildi | nega javob emas — uyga vazifada shu jadval to'ldiriladi.
timeline: Salomlashish, o'tgan darsdagi savol turini (sentence completion) 3 savolda eslatish
Ustoz doskada: 6 bosqich, INKOR / TASDIQ signal ustunlari, chalg'ituvchining ikki turi, tipik xatolar
"Tasdiq yoki inkor?" (5 gap, og'zaki), keyin Track 23 (Irina) 7–10: variantlarni o'qish, BIR MARTA tinglash, tekshirish
Track 23: har rad etilgan variant audioda qaysi ibora bilan eshitilgani doskaga yoziladi; paraphraselar (laptop = computer) ko'rsatiladi
1–4-savollar (har birida 2 harf), BIR MARTA tinglanadi; keyin "Chalg'ituvchi tahlili"
Ustoz Part 2 monologini BIR MARTA o'qiydi, 1–4; keyin rad etilgan variant tahlili
IELTS tezligida BIR MARTA o'qiladi, 1–4; keyin tekshirish va rad etilgan variant tahlili
Xatolar daftari: har xato sababi bilan — eshitmadim / rad etilgan variantni oldim / bitta harf yozdim
"Student union — group project tutorial" skripti uyga; Chalg'ituvchi daftari va Ikki javob mashqi tushuntiriladi; xatolar daftari to'ldiriladi

intro: Listening pick from a list — savol va 5 ta variant (A–E) beriladi, ulardan IKKITASI to'g'ri. Ba'zan Part 3 da uchtasi.
Ikkala harf ham alohida ball: 7–8-savol = 2 ball. Tartib muhim emas: "B, C" = "C, B".
Eng muhim qoida: variantlarni tinglashdan OLDIN o'qing. Audioda vaqt kam — kalit so'zlarni oldindan bilsangiz, tez ilg'aysiz.

Ko'pincha aksariyat variantlar audioda biror shaklda tilga olinadi, lekin ba'zilari umuman aytilmaydi — ularni tez o'chiring. "Eshitildi" degani "javob" degani emas — variant TASDIQLANDIMI yoki INKOR qilindimi, shuni tinglang.
Chalg'ituvchining ikki turi: 1) variant aytiladi, keyin rad etiladi ("I was going to buy a smartwatch, but I decided it wasn't necessary"); 2) variant boshqa kishi/narsa haqida.
Part 2 — monolog (bitta so'zlovchi); Part 3 — suhbat (2–4 kishi). Kim gapirayotganini kuzating.
presentation: Faqat bittasini eshitib qoldim.
Yozing — har javob alohida ball. Ikkinchisiga eng ehtimollisini tanlang.
Javoblar tartibi muhimmi?
Yo'q. "A, C" va "C, A" bir xil.
Barcha variant eshitildi. Qaysi biri?
Tasdiqlangan ikkitasini oling; qolganlari rad etilgan yoki boshqa narsa haqida.
Part 2 va 3 farqi?
2 — monolog; 3 — suhbat. Usul bir xil.
Variantni o'qishga ulgurmadim.
Keyingi savol boshlanishidan oldingi pauzada o'qing; audio to'xtamaydi.
Uchta to'g'ridek tuyuldi.
Uchinchisini qayta o'ylang: u aniq tasdiqlandimi yoki faqat tilga olindimi?
notes: Track 23 (Irina) va Track 11 (Joe) — 12-darsdagi Irina va Joe suhbatlarining davomi. Bir mavzu ikki savol turi bilan.
Javob kalitlari transkript bilan tekshirilgan: har javobda transkriptdagi tasdiqlovchi iborani o'quvchilarga ko'rsating.
Har javobdan keyin so'rang: "qaysi so'z tasdiqladi? qaysi variant nega rad etildi?"
Chalg'ituvchi tahlili — darsning asosiy ishi: har rad etilgan variant audioda qanday eshitilgani yozdiriladi.
mistakes: Ko'p variant tilga olinadi, lekin faqat ikkitasi tasdiqlanadi

core: I read technology news every morning to keep up with the latest gadgets.
Eng so'nggi gadjetlardan xabardor bo'lib turish uchun har kuni ertalab texnologiya yangiliklarini o'qiyman.
My grandfather never buys new gadgets because he finds them too complicated.
Bobom hech qachon yangi gadjetlar sotib olmaydi, chunki ularni juda murakkab deb hisoblaydi.
A smartphone is one device that can replace a camera, a radio and a calculator.
Smartfon — kamera, radio va kalkulyator o'rnini bosa oladigan bitta qurilma.
Our new classroom is bright and spacious, so thirty students fit in easily.
Yangi sinfxonamiz yorug' va keng, shuning uchun o'ttiz o'quvchi bemalol sig'adi.
We had to queue for forty minutes to buy tickets for the concert.
Konsertga chipta olish uchun qirq daqiqa navbatda turishimizga to'g'ri keldi.
The shop window was full of bright, eye-catching posters.
Do'kon vitrinasi yorqin, ko'zni o'ziga tortadigan plakatlarga to'la edi.
This camera is so compact that it fits in my jacket pocket.
Bu kamera shunchalik ixchamki, kurtkamning cho'ntagiga sig'adi.
Our old car is not very reliable — it often breaks down in winter.
Eski mashinamiz unchalik ishonchli emas — qishda tez-tez buzilib qoladi.
If you turn the speaker up too high, the music sounds distorted.
Karnay ovozini juda baland qilsangiz, musiqa buzilib eshitiladi.
My sister works as a volunteer at the city library every Saturday.
Singlim har shanba shahar kutubxonasida ko'ngilli bo'lib ishlaydi.
Many families donate old books and toys to the local school.
Ko'p oilalar eski kitob va o'yinchoqlarni mahalliy maktabga hadya qiladi.
Every student who finishes the course receives a certificate.
Kursni tugatgan har bir o'quvchi sertifikat oladi.
The shop assistant quickly sorted out the problem with my new phone.
Do'kon xodimi yangi telefonimdagi muammoni tezda hal qilib berdi.
He felt confident before the exam because he had practised every day.
U har kuni mashq qilgani uchun imtihon oldidan o'ziga ishonchi komil edi.

class_ex.title: Tasdiq yoki inkor?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz avval savolni (Q), keyin gapni o'qiydi; o'quvchi shu savolga nisbatan "javob (tasdiq)" yoki "chalg'ituvchi (inkor)" deydi.
items: Q: Which TWO devices has Sam bought this year? — "I nearly bought a tablet, but in the end I decided my phone was good enough."
Q: Which TWO devices has Sam bought this year? — "In March I finally got myself a new printer."
Q: Which TWO problems did Lola have with her headphones? — "The battery lasts for ages — I only charge them once a week."
Q: Which TWO problems did Lola have with her headphones? — "After about an hour, they started to hurt my ears."
Q: What TWO things does Bekzod like about the new library? — "I'm not so keen on the lifts, though. They're always full."
why: "but in the end I decided my phone was good enough" — planshetni sotib olmagan.
"I finally got myself a new printer" — printerni sotib olgan (got = bought).
"lasts for ages ... only charge them once a week" — batareya yaxshi, demak bu muammo emas.
"they started to hurt my ears" — quloqni og'ritadi, bu muammo.
"I'm not so keen on" — liftlar unga yoqmaydi.
class_ex.note: Signal so'zlar doskada: but, however, not, decided not, I'm not keen on (inkor); really like, that's great, definitely (tasdiq). Gaplar dars audiolaridan olinmagan — mashq listeningdan oldin o'tkaziladi va audio javoblarini oshkor qilmaydi.

listenings.title: Track 23. Irina at the electronics exhibition — a survey
intro: So'rovnoma o'tkazuvchi ayol Irina bilan gaplashmoqda (12-darsdagi Track 22 dan keyin). Avval 7–10-savollar va A–E variantlarni o'qing, kalit so'zlarni belgilang. Keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Choose TWO letters, A–E for each question. Har savolda IKKI javob.
transcript: WOMAN: Excuse me.
IRINA: Yes?
WOMAN: Before you go through, I wonder if you could help us by answering a few questions for a survey. It won't take long.
IRINA: No problem. We're not in any hurry.
WOMAN: Fine, thanks. Now, er, let's look at the questions. First one. Why are you visiting the exhibition?

IRINA: Well, I want to keep up with the latest developments in electronics, you know – I was recommended by a friend to come here and see what new devices and inventions are coming out and learn a bit. I mean, I don't generally go shopping for new electronics – I'm not the sort of person who goes out and buys all the latest gadgets – the prices are too high when they're new. But it interests me, and I thought also there would be things which would interest my son and he'd enjoy it as well, so that's why we're here.
WOMAN: OK ... and here's a question to find out what sort of consumer you are. Have you bought any electronics recently?

IRINA: Recently? Sure. I was thinking of buying a new calculator for the office, but I decided it wasn't really necessary because I can do all the calculations just as easily on a computer. Anyway, I got a new laptop recently, you know, they have so many applications and they don't take up much space either. Better to have lots of things on the same device, I think. The other thing I bought was a present for my husband's birthday. I thought it would be nice to have a record of our holidays, so I bought him a camera, and I'm hoping to get him more interested in photography.
WOMAN: Right ... and here's a question about this building. I know you haven't had a chance to look around a lot yet, but at first sight, what do you think of it?

IRINA: Oh, it looks pretty good to me. It's got lots of natural light, so you don't have to put up with lots of electric lighting, which is quite tiring on the eyes. It feels very large and spacious, which is great because although it's full of activity and quite noisy, it doesn't feel too crowded. Also, when you look up at the ceiling near the entrance, with the design of stars and planets on it, that's something I really like. I'm not so keen on those revolving doors, though. I always feel I'm going to get stuck in one.
WOMAN: Did you have any difficulties getting to the exhibition?

IRINA: Well, coming at this time of day the roads weren't too busy, so that was all right, and there were plenty of signposts, so the car park was easy to find. The only problem was it was full when I arrived – I guess I should have come earlier – so I had to find another one quite a long walk away, which was a pity. Then we had to stand outside for quite a long time queuing to get in – this exhibition is pretty popular. That was a bit of a problem, because my son gets impatient, but fortunately it wasn't raining, otherwise we might have gone home.

tasks.title: Questions 7–10: Choose TWO letters, A–E
tasks.instr: Har savolda ikki javob. Har variant uchun tasdiq/inkorni belgilang.
items: 7 Which TWO reasons does Irina give for visiting the exhibition? A) to meet a friend B) to improve her knowledge C) to buy something D) to check prices E) to entertain her child
8 Which TWO devices has Irina bought recently? A) a calculator B) a computer C) a camera D) a phone E) a digital recorder
9 What TWO things does Irina like about the building? A) the electric lights B) the space C) the activity D) the ceiling E) the entrance
10 Which TWO problems did Irina have coming to the exhibition? A) driving in heavy traffic B) finding the car park C) parking the car D) waiting to enter E) standing outside in the rain
why: "Keep up with the latest developments ... learn a bit" (B) va "things which would interest my son and he'd enjoy it" (E). A tuzoq: do'st TAVSIYA qilgan, uchrashish uchun emas. C teskari: "I don't generally go shopping". D — narx yuqori, lekin tekshirish maqsad emas.
"I got a new laptop recently" (B — computer) va "I bought him a camera" (C). A tuzoq: kalkulyator — "decided it wasn't really necessary", sotib olmagan.

"It feels very large and spacious" (B) va "the ceiling near the entrance ... that's something I really like" (D). A tuzoq: tabiiy yorug'lik yoqadi, elektr yorug'lik "tiring on the eyes". E tuzoq: shift kirish yonida, lekin u SHIFTni yaxshi ko'radi.
To'xtash joyi to'lgan, boshqa joy topgan (C) va "stand outside ... queuing to get in" (D). A teskari: "roads weren't too busy". B teskari: "car park was easy to find". E teskari: "it wasn't raining".
tasks.note: Javoblar (transkript bo'yicha tasdiqlangan): 7 B, E · 8 B, C · 9 B, D · 10 C, D.

tasks.instr: Har rad etilgan variant audioda qanday eshitildi?
items: 8 A (calculator)
9 A (electric lights)
10 B (finding car park)
10 E (rain)
answers: "you don't have to put up with lots of electric lighting"
"the car park was easy to find"
why: Sotib olmagan.
Tabiiy yorug'lik yaxshi.
Muammo — to'lgani.
Yomg'ir yo'q edi.

listenings.title: Track 11. Joe tests three devices
listenings.qtype: Pick from a list (1–4) — qo'shimcha mashq
intro: Joe uchta qurilmani sinab ko'rgan: mobil telefon, radio va noutbuk. Avval savollarni va variantlarni o'qing. Keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Choose TWO letters, A–E for each question.
transcript: WOMAN: Right, Joe. Let's move on. Now, we gave you three items to test for us. Let's start with the mobile phone.
JOE: OK. Well, it has its good points and its bad points. The purple and silver make it quite eye-catching, you know, modern, exciting.
WOMAN: Right. Anything else?
JOE: Well, it's very small, isn't it? I know people say small is good, but in this case, I think you might have gone too far.
WOMAN: In what way?

JOE: It can be a bit difficult to use, especially if you've got big hands like mine. You press one key and you end up pressing another at the same time. On the other hand, thanks to the oval design, it does fit comfortably in your hand. Mobiles are usually sort of rectangular, aren't they? I think this is much better.
WOMAN: OK. What else?

JOE: When I was sending text messages, I had real problems seeing what I was writing. It's not that the screen was too small, just that it was a bit dark. If you're outside, you can hardly see anything on it.
WOMAN: We added a few things that you don't get on other mobiles. What did you think about those?
JOE: Ah, right. Well, that noise it makes if you move away from it? That's really annoying. It's basically a good idea, but I think that after a while, it would drive me mad.
WOMAN: So you probably wouldn't buy it?

JOE: Probably not. When I buy a mobile phone, I don't want one that's going to be difficult to operate. There's no point having a phone that looks good if you have to spend ages trying to make a call or send a text message. It's funny, but I find that more expensive mobile phones are more difficult to use than cheaper ones. It should be the other way round. So keep it simple. And I want a phone that doesn't have problems picking up a signal or doesn't cut you off halfway through a call. And all those games and other things you get on a mobile, I really can't see the point in those.
WOMAN: Fair point. Next, the digital radio. What did you think?
JOE: The audio quality was crisp and clear. Even if you turned it up really loud, some sound systems can sound a bit distorted at higher volumes, but not on this one. So ten out of ten for that.
WOMAN: Great.

JOE: The thing is, I'm not sure if it's the area I live in, but the choice of radio stations seemed very limited. It didn't make any difference what I did with the aerial or where I put the radio, high up on a shelf, low down on the floor. And there seemed to be a delay when you turned up the volume.
WOMAN: What do you mean?
JOE: Well, when you press the volume control, for example, nothing seems to happen for a few seconds. And the same thing happens when you want to change radio stations.
WOMAN: Hmm, OK. The third item was the laptop computer. What's your opinion on that?

JOE: Oh, I really liked it. It's so small, so compact, but easy to use at the same time. I don't think you could make it smaller if you tried. But at 900 pounds, I'm not sure you'd get many customers. That's a lot of money for a laptop. Bring that down to, say, 400 pounds and things might be different.
WOMAN: Any other changes you'd make, like adding more memory, for example?

JOE: Oh, I think that's fine as it is. 300 gigabytes of memory is probably more than enough for most people. Oh, and incidentally, the way the keyboard folds out so that it's like a full-sized one, that's really clever. But the computer doesn't have anywhere you can play CD-ROMs. And I'd include a light in the keyboard so you can use it when it's dark.

tasks.title: Questions 1–4: Choose TWO letters, A–E
items: 1 What TWO things did Joe like about the mobile phone? A) its colour B) its size C) its shape D) its screen E) its unique features

2 What TWO things does Joe usually look for when he buys a mobile phone? A) It should be easy to use. B) It should look good. C) It should be cheap. D) It should be reliable. E) It should have a variety of games.

3 Which TWO problems did Joe have with the radio? A) It didn't sound good. B) It wasn't loud enough. C) It didn't pick up many radio stations. D) He couldn't find anywhere to put it. E) The control features didn't work properly.
4 What TWO things does Joe think would improve the computer? A) making it smaller B) reducing the price C) increasing the memory D) increasing the size of the keyboard E) adding more features
why: "The purple and silver make it quite eye-catching" (A) va "thanks to the oval design, it does fit comfortably ... much better" (C). B teskari: "gone too far" (juda kichik). D teskari: ekran qorong'i. E teskari: shovqin "really annoying".

"I don't want one that's going to be difficult to operate" (A) va "doesn't have problems picking up a signal or ... cut you off" (D). B teskari: "no point having a phone that looks good if...". E teskari: "games ... can't see the point".

"The choice of radio stations seemed very limited" (C) va "delay when you turned up the volume ... change radio stations" (E). A teskari: "crisp and clear, ten out of ten". B teskari: "turned it up really loud". D tuzoq: joyni sinagan, lekin bu qabul haqida.

"at 900 pounds ... bring that down to, say, 400 pounds" (B) va "doesn't have anywhere you can play CD-ROMs ... include a light in the keyboard" (E). A teskari: "couldn't make it smaller". C teskari: "more than enough". D tuzoq: klaviatura allaqachon to'liq o'lchamda ochiladi.
tasks.note: Javoblar (transkript bo'yicha tasdiqlangan): 1 A, C · 2 A, D · 3 C, E · 4 B, E. Har savolda 5 variantning hammasi tilga olinadi, lekin faqat 2 tasi savolga mos keladi.

tasks.title: Chalg'ituvchi tahlili
tasks.instr: Har rad etilgan variant qanday eshitildi?
items: 1 B (size)
2 B (look good)
3 A (sound)
4 C (memory)
answers: "no point ... if you have to spend ages"
why: Juda kichik — kamchilik.
Ko'rinish yetarli emas.
Ovoz a'lo.
Xotira yetarli.

listenings.title: The photography club — evening talk
intro: Foto klub rahbari yangi a'zolarga so'zlamoqda (Part 2 monolog). Avval savollarni o'qing, keyin skriptni bir marta tinglang (ustoz o'qiydi).
transcript: Good evening, everyone, and welcome to the Riverside Photography Club. Let me tell you a bit about what we do.

First, why do people join us? Some come because they've just bought their first proper camera and want to learn how to use it. Others already know the technical side but want to meet people who share the same hobby — that's actually the most common reason. A few people ask whether they'll be able to sell their photos through the club, but I'm afraid we don't do that — we're a hobby club, not a business. And some simply want a reason to get out of the house on a cold evening.

Now, our meetings. We meet every Tuesday. On the first Tuesday of the month, we have a guest speaker — usually a professional photographer. On the second, we go out together to take photos, weather permitting. The third Tuesday is for editing on the computer, and on the last one, members show their best work and we discuss it.

What equipment do you need? Well, obviously a camera, though it doesn't have to be expensive — some of our best work is done on phones. You'll also find a tripod useful for evening shots. You don't need editing software of your own, as we have computers here. And please don't bring a printer — we have a professional one at the club.

Finally, the trips. This year we're planning a day at the coast in spring, a weekend in the mountains in summer, and a visit to a city at night to practise with lights. We had hoped to organise a trip abroad, but unfortunately it proved too expensive this year.

tasks.title: Choose TWO letters, A–E
items: 1–2 What TWO reasons does the speaker give for people joining the club? A) to learn to use a new camera B) to meet people with the same hobby C) to become professional photographers D) to sell their photographs E) to earn extra money
3–4 Which TWO items does the speaker say members do NOT need to bring? A) a camera B) a tripod C) editing software D) a printer E) a phone
why: "Learn how to use it" (A) va "meet people who share the same hobby — the most common reason" (B). D tuzoq: suratlarni sotish haqida so'rashadi, lekin "we don't do that" — rad etilgan. C tuzoq: "professional photographer" — mehmon ma'ruzachi haqida, a'zolarning maqsadi emas. E aytilmagan.
"You don't need editing software ... we have computers" (C) va "please don't bring a printer" (D). A, B kerak; E — telefon bilan olish mumkin, lekin "keltirmang" deyilmagan.

tasks.title: Chalg'ituvchi tahlili
items: 1–2 D (sell photos)
3–4 A (camera)
why: Klub suratlarni sotmaydi — variant rad etilgan.
Asosiy jihoz.

listenings.title: Volunteer open day — introduction
intro: Ko'ngillilar tashkiloti muvofiqlashtiruvchisi (Part 2). Avval savollarni o'qing, keyin bir marta tinglang.
transcript: Hello and thank you all for coming to our volunteer open day. I'll explain how you can help and what we can offer you.

There are several ways to get involved. Some volunteers work in our charity shop, sorting and selling donated items. Others prefer to be outdoors, helping to plant trees and clean up the river. We also need people to answer the phones in the office, and a few volunteers visit elderly people at home. What we no longer do, by the way, is door-to-door collection — we stopped that last year.

Now, what do we ask of you? We ask for at least three hours a week, though many people do more. You don't need any experience, as we provide full training. You do, however, need to be over sixteen, and for the home visits only, you'll need a background check, which we arrange and pay for.

What do you get in return? Well, we can't pay you, of course, but we do cover your travel costs. You also get a free lunch on the days you work, and after six months, we give you a certificate that many people find useful for job applications. Some volunteers say the best thing, though, is simply the friends they make.

tasks.title: Choose TWO letters, A–E
items: 1–2 Which TWO tasks can volunteers do? A) sell items in a shop B) collect money door to door C) plant trees D) manage the office E) teach children
3–4 What TWO things does the organisation give volunteers? A) a small wage B) travel costs C) a free lunch D) a uniform E) experience only
why: "Work in our charity shop, sorting and selling" (A) va "helping to plant trees" (C). B tuzoq: "we stopped that last year". D — telefonga javob berish, boshqarish emas.
"we do cover your travel costs" (B) va "a free lunch on the days you work" (C). A teskari: "we can't pay you". D aytilmagan.

tasks.title: Chalg'ituvchi tahlili
items: 1–2 B (door to door)
3–4 A (wage)
why: Endi qilinmaydi.
Maosh yo'q.

listenings.title: Student union — tutorial about a group project
intro: Talaba (Maya) va o'qituvchi (Dr Reed) guruh loyihasi haqida gaplashmoqda (Part 3 suhbat). Uyda bir marta tinglang.
transcript: DR REED: Come in, Maya. So, how's the group project going?
MAYA: Quite well, thanks, though we've had a few problems.
DR REED: Tell me about them.

MAYA: Well, at first we couldn't agree on a topic. Everyone had a different idea. And then, once we chose one, we found it hard to divide the work fairly — some people ended up doing much more than others. The good news is we sorted that out in the end.
DR REED: That's common in group work. Anything else?
MAYA: The biggest issue now is meeting up. We all have different timetables, so finding a time when everyone is free is almost impossible. We tried meeting online, but the connection was often poor.
DR REED: Have you thought about sharing documents online instead of always meeting?
MAYA: Yes, that's worked really well, actually. We use a shared folder, so everyone can add their part whenever they're free. And we keep a list of who's doing what, which stops arguments.
DR REED: Good. Now, for the presentation, what do you still need help with?
MAYA: Two things, really. First, none of us is confident about speaking in front of the class, so any tips would be welcome. And second, we're not sure how much detail to include on the slides.
DR REED: I can help with both. What I wouldn't worry about is the length — twenty minutes is plenty, and you clearly have enough material.

tasks.title: Choose TWO letters, A–E
items: 1–2 What TWO problems did the group solve? A) choosing a topic B) dividing the work C) meeting up D) a poor internet connection E) arguments about marks
3–4 What TWO things does Maya ask for help with? A) speaking to the class B) choosing software C) making the slides D) the length of the talk E) finding more material
why: "At first we couldn't agree on a topic ... sorted that out" (A) va "hard to divide the work fairly ... we sorted that out in the end" (B). C tuzoq: uchrashish — "the biggest issue now", hal bo'lmagan. D — hal qilinmagan.

"None of us is confident about speaking in front of the class" (A) va "not sure how much detail to include on the slides" (C). D teskari: Dr Reed "wouldn't worry about the length". E teskari: "you clearly have enough material".

tasks.title: Chalg'ituvchi tahlili
items: 1–2 C (meeting up)
3–4 D (length)
why: Hali hal bo'lmagan.
Muammo emas.

homework_intro: Bugun biz variantlarni tinglashdan OLDIN o'qishni va "eshitildi" bilan "tasdiqlandi" ni ajratishni mashq qildik — uyda endi xuddi shu ishni yolg'iz o'zingiz bajarasiz.

Birinchi vazifa — "Student union — group project tutorial" skripti (Part 3 suhbat): avval savollarni va A–E variantlarni o'qib kalit so'zlarni belgilang, keyin bir marta tinglang yoki birovga bir marta o'qitib bering, to'xtatmang, 1–2 va 3–4 savollarga ikkitadan harf yozing va faqat shundan keyin transkriptni ochib tekshiring — hammasi 10 daqiqa vaqt oladi.

Ikkinchisi — "Chalg'ituvchi daftari": Track 23 (Irina) va Track 11 (Joe) dan 8 ta rad etilgan variantni ko'chirib, har birining yoniga audioda qaysi so'z bilan rad etilganini yozasiz (but / not / decided not / more than enough); uchinchisi — "Ikki javob mashqi": bugungi besh mashqdan 10 ta savolni olib, har biriga ikkala harfni ham yozasiz — ikkalasi birga 20 daqiqacha.

Eng ko'p qilinadigan xato — bitta harfni yozib, ikkinchisini bo'sh qoldirish: har harf alohida ball, bo'sh qator esa 0 ball, shuning uchun ikkinchisini eshitmay qolsangiz ham eng ehtimollisini belgilang; chalg'ituvchi daftarida ham inkor signali ko'rsatilmagan qator qabul qilinmaydi, u qator uchun ball yo'q.

Uchala vazifani ham keyingi dars boshida daftar ochiq holda stolga qo'yasiz, javoblarni birga tekshiramiz va men har javob uchun "qaysi so'z tasdiqladi, qolgan variantlar nega rad etildi?" deb so'rayman.

homework.title: 5-skript: "Student union — group project tutorial"
homework.instr: Uyda bir marta tinglang (yoki o'qitib eshiting), javoblarni belgilang, keyin transkript bilan tekshiring.
homework.answers: Javoblar Listening bo'limida.

homework.title: Chalg'ituvchi daftari
homework.instr: Track 23 (Irina) va Track 11 (Joe) dan 8 ta rad etilgan variantni yozing va har biri audioda qaysi so'z bilan rad etilganini belgilang (but / not / decided not / more than enough).
homework.answers: Har qatorda inkor signali bo'lishi shart.

homework.title: Ikki javob mashqi
homework.instr: Bugungi 5 mashqdan 10 ta savolni oling va har biriga ikkala harfni yozing; bittasini eshitmasangiz ham eng ehtimolini belgilang.
homework.answers: Ustoz tekshiradi.

kahoot.q: In a 'Choose TWO letters, A–E' question, how many marks can you get?
options: Two — one for each correct letter
One — only if both letters are right
Five — one mark for each option
None unless the order is correct
kahoot.explain: Har to'g'ri harf alohida 1 ball: ikkala harf to'g'ri bo'lsa — 2 ball, bittasi to'g'ri bo'lsa — 1 ball.

kahoot.q: When should you read the five options (A–E)?
kahoot.explain: Variantlar tinglashdan OLDIN o'qiladi va kalit so'zlar belgilanadi, chunki audio to'xtamaydi.

kahoot.q: The key says 'A, C'. A student writes 'C, A'. How many marks does the student get?
options: Two — the order does not matter
One — only the first letter counts
One — a mark is lost for order
kahoot.explain: "Choose TWO" savolida harflar tartibi ahamiyatsiz: "C, A" = "A, C".

kahoot.q: Q: Which TWO sports does Tom play now? Tom: 'I used to play tennis, but I gave it up last year.' Is tennis an answer?
options: Only if tennis is option A
kahoot.explain: "used to ... but I gave it up" — variant tilga olindi, lekin rad etildi, demak bu chalg'ituvchi.

kahoot.q: Which word or phrase most often signals that an option is being REJECTED?
kahoot.explain: "However", "but", "not" — inkor signali: ulardan keyin variant ko'pincha rad etiladi.

kahoot.q: Q: What TWO problems did Ana have at the hotel? Ana: 'It was noisy at night, but the staff were really helpful.' Which is a problem?
kahoot.explain: "noisy" — muammo; "but the staff were really helpful" — xodimlar maqtalgan, joy va nonushta esa umuman aytilmagan.

kahoot.q: An option is never mentioned in the recording at all. What should you do with it?
options: Write it as a second answer
kahoot.explain: Ba'zi variantlar umuman aytilmaydi — ularni darhol o'chirib, qolganlari orasidan tanlang.

kahoot.q: How are IELTS Listening Part 2 and Part 3 different?
options: Part 2 has one speaker; Part 3 is a discussion
Part 2 is a group discussion; Part 3 has one speaker
Part 2 is a phone call; Part 3 is a lecture
Both parts have one speaker only
kahoot.explain: Part 2 — monolog (bitta so'zlovchi, kundalik mavzu); Part 3 — 2–4 kishining o'quv mavzusidagi suhbati.

kahoot.q: You heard only ONE of the two answers. What is the best thing to do?
options: Write it and guess the other
Wait and ask for the audio again
kahoot.explain: Har harf alohida ball: eshitganingizni yozing, ikkinchisiga eng ehtimolli variantni belgilang — bo'sh joy 0 ball.

kahoot.q: In Part 3, why must you follow WHO is speaking?
options: One speaker may reject another's idea
The two speakers always agree with each other
Only the first speaker ever gives the answers
The questions usually ask for the speakers' names
kahoot.explain: Suhbatda bir kishi taklif qiladi, ikkinchisi uni rad etishi mumkin — savol kimning fikrini so'rayotganiga qarang.

kahoot.q: Q: Which TWO facilities does the gym offer? Speaker: 'We have a pool, and a sauna is planned for next year.' Is the sauna an answer?
options: No — it does not exist yet
Only if the pool is not listed
kahoot.explain: "is planned for next year" — sauna hali yo'q, shuning uchun hozir taklif qilinadigan narsa emas.

kahoot.q: The instruction says 'Choose THREE letters, A–G'. How many of the options are NOT answers?
kahoot.explain: A–G — 7 ta variant; 3 tasi javob, qolgan 4 tasi chalg'ituvchi. Har to'g'ri harf alohida ball.

kahoot.q: What is a 'gadget'?
kahoot.explain: Gadget — kichik, foydali (ko'pincha elektron) qurilma: smart soat, powerbank va hokazo.

kahoot.q: A 'compact' laptop is…

lessons.title: Reading: Summary Completion (Passage 2)
lessons.grammar_topic: Summary completion — xulosani to'ldirish (2 turi: matndan so'z / ro'yxatdan tanlash)
lessons.book_ref: Jony Academy materiali — ustoz matnlari va mualliflik matnlari.
objectives: Summary (xulosa) matnning qaysi qismini qamrab olishini topish: butun matnmi yoki bir-ikki xatboshimi.
Ikki turni farqlash: 1) javob MATNDAN olinadi (so'z chegarasi bilan); 2) javob tayyor RO'YXATDAN (box) tanlanadi.
Bo'sh joy grammatikasidan foydalanish: ot, fe'l, sifat, ko'plik (farosat usuli).
Xulosadagi paraphraseni matndagi asl ibora bilan bog'lash.
Javoblar odatda (USUALLY) matn tartibida kelishini bilib, shundan foydalanish.
materials: Reading #17 "Rubik's Cube" matni va 1–7 xulosasi — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa (sinf mashqidan keyin birga bajariladi).
Reading #18 "Marcel Bich" hamda "The sticky note that nobody wanted" matnlari (glossariysi bilan) — har o'quvchiga bittadan nusxa.
"The invention of the bar code" matni va A–J ro'yxati; o'sha 10 so'z alohida qirqilgan kartochka qilib tayyorlansin — har juftlikka bitta to'plam (2-tur, box mashqi uchun).
Uyga vazifa matni "The man who made the world wear jeans" — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa, dars oxirida tarqatiladi.
Doskada dars boshlanishidan oldin: farosat jadvali ("the ___ of" — ot, "to ___ a pen" — fe'l, "a ___ pen" — sifat yoki ot, "are ___" — sifat) va yirik harflar bilan "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS".
O'quvchilarda: paraphrase daftari, xatolar daftari va qalam (javoblar avval qalamda yoziladi); ustozda soat yoki sekundomer — "The sticky note that nobody wanted" 8 daqiqa vaqt bilan bajariladi.
timeline: Salomlashish, o'tgan darsdagi savol turini 3 savolda eslatish
Ustoz doskada: 2 tur (matndan / box), 6 bosqich, farosat jadvali, tipik xatolar
"Farosat: bo'sh joy turi" (6 band, matnsiz, og'zaki), keyin Reading #17 "Rubik's Cube" 1–7 birga: har javobda bashorat qilingan tur tekshiriladi
Rubik's Cube: xulosadagi ibora — matndagi ibora juftlari (originally named = he called ...) doskada; o'quvchilar ovoz chiqarib topadi
1–7 mustaqil: avval har bo'sh joy turi aytiladi, keyin javoblar paraphrase bilan tekshiriladi
"The sticky note that nobody wanted" 1–6 — 8 daqiqa sekundomer bilan, keyin tekshirish
"The invention of the bar code" — juftlikda A–J kartochkalari bilan 1–6, ortiqcha so'zlar o'chirib boriladi; keyin tekshirish (circular = round)
Xatolar daftari: har xato sababi bilan — so'z chegarasi / grammatika (farosat) / paraphrase topilmadi
"The man who made the world wear jeans" uyga (8 daqiqa); paraphrase daftari (15 juft) va box mashqi tushuntiriladi

intro: Summary completion — matnning qisqa mazmuni beriladi, ichida bo'sh joylar bor. Xulosa matnni boshqa so'zlar bilan qayta aytadi, shuning uchun bu tur 1-darsdagi paraphrase ko'nikmasiga tayanadi.
1-TUR (matndan): "Choose NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage". Javob matndagi so'z bilan, o'zgartirmasdan yoziladi.
2-TUR (box): so'zlar ro'yxati beriladi, ulardan tanlanadi. Ro'yxatdagi so'zlar matnda BOSHQA shaklda bo'lishi mumkin — ma'noga qarang. Ro'yxatda ortiqcha so'zlar bor.
Birinchi qadam: xulosaning sarlavhasi va birinchi gapini o'qing, matnning qaysi qismi ekanini toping. Ba'zan xulosa faqat 1–2 xatboshini qamraydi.
Ikkinchi qadam — farosat: bo'sh joydan oldingi va keyingi so'zga qarab turini aniqlang. "the ___ of" — ot; "to ___ a pen" — fe'l; "a ___ pen" — sifat yoki ot.
Xulosa odatda (USUALLY) matn tartibida boradi: 3-javob 2-javobdan keyin turadi.
Javobni yozgach, butun gapni o'qing: grammatika va ma'no to'g'rimi? "the colours ... are ___" — "are" dan keyin sifat kerak (identical), ot (identity) emas.
presentation: Summary butun matnnimi qamraydi?
Har doim emas. Sarlavha va birinchi gap qaysi qism ekanini aytadi.
Javobni o'z so'zim bilan yozsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. 1-turda matndagi so'z, 2-turda ro'yxatdagi so'z yoziladi.
Box'dagi so'z matnda yo'q, nima qilaman?
Ma'nosini qidiring — box so'zi matndagi so'zning paraphrasei bo'lishi mumkin.
"a ___ ballpoint pen" — qanday so'z?
Otni aniqlovchi so'z yoki birikma: sifat ("a new ballpoint pen"), ravish + sifat ("a surprisingly light ballpoint pen") yoki ot ("a metal ballpoint pen"). Ikki so'zli birikma ham chegaraga sig'adi.
Javoblar tartibdami?
Odatda (USUALLY) ha. Topilmasa, kalit so'zga qayting.
Ikki so'zli javob yozsam bo'ladimi?
Ko'rsatma "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS" bo'lsa, ha.
notes: Summary completion — Passage 2 da ko'p uchraydi. Bu dars 1-dars (paraphrase) va 2-dars (farosat) ko'nikmalarini birlashtiradi.
Har javobdan keyin so'rang: "xulosadagi qaysi so'z matndagi qaysi iboraga teng?"
2-tur (box) uchun ortiqcha so'zlarni o'chirib borish odatini shakllantiring.
mistakes: Box so'zi matnda boshqa shaklda bo'ladi
Bo'sh joy oldida aniqlovchi (its / the / his) allaqachon bor

class_ex.title: Farosat: bo'sh joy turi
class_ex.instr: Matnga qaramasdan har bo'sh joy uchun qanday so'z kerakligini ayting.
items: Originally named the ___
organised in ___
though not ___
The Cube's ___ is shaped
the colours ... are ___

why: "named the" dan keyin nom keladi.
"organised in" — nimalar ichida joylashgan.
"twisted ... though not ___" — qanday qilib, ravish.

readings.title: Reading #17. Rubik's Cube - How the puzzle achieved success
text: Erno Rubik first studied sculpture and then later architecture in Budapest, where he went on to become a teacher of interior design. It was while he was working as a teacher that he began the preliminary work on an invention that he called the 'Magic Cube'.

Rubik was inspired by geometric puzzles such as the Chinese tangram, a puzzle consisting of various triangles, a square and a parallelogram which can be combined to create different shapes and figures. However, unlike the tangram, which is two-dimensional, Rubik was more interested in investigating how three-dimensional forms, such as the cube, could be moved and combined to produce other forms.

His design consisted of a cube made up of layers of individual smaller cubes, and each smaller cube could be turned in any direction except diagonally. To ensure that the cubes could move independently, without falling apart, Rubik first attempted to join them together using elastic bands. However, this proved to be impossible, so Rubik then solved the problem by assembling them using a rounded interior. This permitted them to move smoothly and easily. He experimented with different ways of marking the smaller cubes, but ended up with the simple solution of giving a different colour to each side. The object was to twist the layers of small cubes so that each side of the large cube was an identical colour.

Rubik took out a patent for the Cube in 1977 and started manufacturing it in the same year. The Cube came to the attention of a Hungarian businessman, Tibor Laczi, who then demonstrated it at the Nuremberg Toy Fair. When British toy expert Tom Kremer saw it, he thought it was amazing and he persuaded a manufacturer, Ideal Toys, to produce 1 million of them in 1979. Ideal Toys renamed the Cube after the toy's inventor, and in 1980, Rubik's Cube was shown at toy fairs all over the world. It won that year's prize in Germany for Best Puzzle. Rubik's Cube is believed to be the world's best-selling puzzle; since its invention, more than 300 million Cubes have been sold worldwide.
paraphrases: can be twisted in almost any way
could be turned in any direction
has sold more than any other

tasks.title: Questions 1–7: Complete the summary
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage
tasks.instr: 1-tur: javob matndan olinadi. Xulosa matn tartibida boradi (USUALLY).
why: "An invention that he called the 'Magic Cube'". "Originally named" = "he called". Ikki so'z, bosh harf bilan.
"A cube made up of layers of individual smaller cubes". "Organised in" = "made up of".
"Could be turned in any direction except diagonally". "Though not" = "except". Farosat: "twisted ... though not ___" — ravish kerak.
"Assembling them using a rounded interior. This permitted them to move smoothly". "Allows" = "permitted".
"So that each side of the large cube was an identical colour". "Are ___" — sifat kerak (identity emas).
"Ideal Toys renamed the Cube after the toy's inventor". "Changed the name" = "renamed". "its" dan keyin artikl kerak emas.
"The world's best-selling puzzle". "Sold more than any other" = "best-selling".
head: Rubik's Cube
rows: Originally named the (1), Rubik's Cube consists of a number of smaller cubes organised in (2). The smaller cubes can be twisted in almost any way, though not (3). The Cube's (4) is shaped in a way that allows the smaller cubes to move smoothly. Each side of the smaller cubes has a different colour, and the aim of the puzzle is to organise the cubes so that the colours on the sides of the large cube are (5). The manufacturers of the puzzle changed the name of the Cube to the name of its (6). It has now sold more than any other (7) in the world.

readings.title: Reading #18. Marcel Bich
text: The man who turned a luxury item into an everyday object

Marcel Bich, a French manufacturer of traditional ink pens, was the man who turned the ballpoint pen into an item that today almost anyone can afford. Bich was appalled at the poor quality of the ballpoint pens that were available, and was also shocked at their high cost. However, he recognised that the ballpoint was a firmly established invention, and he decided to design a cheap pen that worked well and would be commercially successful.

Bich went to the Biro brothers and asked them if he could use the design of their original invention in one of his own pens. In return, he offered to pay them every time he sold a pen. Then, for two years, Bich studied the detailed construction of every ballpoint pen that was being sold, often working with a microscope.

By 1950, he was ready to introduce his new wonder: a plastic pen with a clear barrel that wrote smoothly, did not leak and only cost a few cents. He called it the 'Bic Cristal'. The ballpoint pen had finally become a practical writing instrument. The public liked it immediately, and today it is as common as the pencil. In Britain, they are still called Biros, and many Bic models also say 'Biro' on the side of the pen, to remind people of their original inventors.

Bich became extremely wealthy thanks to his invention, which had worldwide appeal. Over the next 60 years his company, Société Bic, opened factories all over the world and expanded its range of inexpensive products. Today, Bic is as famous for its lighters and razors as it is for its pens, and you can even buy a Bic mobile phone.
paraphrases: most people are able to afford
asked them if he could use

It was the bad quality and (2) of the pens which were available at the time that inspired him to design a (3) ballpoint pen that would be both inexpensive and reliable. After getting permission from the Biro brothers to base his pen on their (4), he carefully (5) other ballpoints that were sold in the shops, and in 1950 introduced his own version, the 'Bic Cristal'. It was popular with the (6), and Bich became very rich. His company, Bic, now makes a variety of cheap (7), such as lighters and razors.

readings.title: The sticky note that nobody wanted
text: In 1968 Spencer Silver, a chemist at the American company 3M, was trying to develop a very strong glue for aircraft. Instead, he made the opposite: an adhesive so weak that it could be pulled off a surface without leaving a mark. Silver believed the glue must be useful for something, and for five years he gave talks about it inside the company. Nobody could think of a practical use.

The solution came from a colleague, Art Fry, who sang in a church choir. Every Sunday the paper bookmarks in his hymn book fell out. Fry remembered Silver's glue and put a little on the edge of a bookmark. It stayed in place, and it could be removed without damaging the pages.

The company was not impressed. Managers thought people would never pay for small pieces of paper when free scrap paper was everywhere. A first test in four cities in 1977 failed, because shoppers did not understand what the product was for. The next year, 3M tried a different approach: in the city of Boise, Idaho, it gave free samples to offices. Ninety percent of the people who tried them said they would buy them.

Post-it Notes went on sale across the United States in 1980 and in Europe a year later. Today they are sold in more than 150 countries, and the original yellow colour was chosen by accident — it was the only scrap paper available in the laboratory next door.
paraphrases: nobody could think of a use

tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage
why: "Trying to develop a very strong glue for aircraft". "Make" = "develop".
"For five years he gave talks about it inside the company". "Tried to interest colleagues" = "gave talks".
"The paper bookmarks in his hymn book fell out". Ko'plik — "stop the ___ falling out".
"When free scrap paper was everywhere". "Easy to find" = "everywhere".
"It gave free samples to offices". Ikki so'z.

head: How the Post-it Note began
rows: While trying to make a strong (1) for aircraft, Spencer Silver produced a weak adhesive. For (2) he tried to interest his colleagues in it. Art Fry used it to stop the (3) in his hymn book falling out. Managers doubted people would pay when free (4) was easy to find. After a failed test, the company gave (5) to offices in Boise. Interestingly, the original yellow colour had been chosen (6).

readings.title: The invention of the bar code
text: In 1948 a supermarket owner in Philadelphia visited a local university and asked whether there was a way to record product information automatically at the checkout. A graduate student, Bernard Silver, overheard the conversation and told his friend Joseph Woodland, a teacher of mechanical engineering.

Woodland left his job and moved to his grandfather's flat in Florida to think about the problem. Sitting on the beach one day, he pushed his fingers into the sand and pulled them towards him, making four lines. He realised that lines of different widths could be used like the dots and dashes of Morse code. His first design, however, was circular, like a target, so that it could be read from any direction.

The two men received a patent in 1952, but the technology to read the codes did not yet exist. The scanners of the time were enormous and expensive, and the idea was ignored for twenty years. Only when cheap lasers and computers appeared in the early 1970s did supermarkets become interested. A committee chose a rectangular design, which was easier to print than a circle.

The first product ever scanned was a packet of chewing gum, in Ohio, on 26 June 1974. The packet is now kept in a museum in Washington. Today about six billion bar codes are scanned every day, and Woodland, who earned almost nothing from the patent, was given a national medal for technology in 1992.
paraphrases: read without a person writing it

readings.title: The man who made the world wear jeans
text: In 1853 a young German immigrant, Levi Strauss, opened a shop in San Francisco selling cloth, blankets and clothing to the gold miners of California. The miners' trousers wore out quickly, and customers often complained that the pockets tore when they filled them with tools and pieces of gold.

One of Strauss's regular customers was a tailor in Nevada called Jacob Davis. A woman had asked Davis to make strong trousers for her husband, and Davis had the idea of putting small metal pins, called rivets, at the corners of the pockets, the points which usually tore first. The trousers were so successful that other workers soon wanted a pair.

Davis did not have the money to register a patent, which cost 68 dollars, so he wrote to Strauss and offered to share it if Strauss paid. In 1873 the two men received the patent together, and Strauss brought Davis to San Francisco to manage production.

The first "waist overalls", as they were called, were made from a heavy blue cotton cloth called denim. For almost eighty years jeans were working clothes for farmers, miners and factory workers. Only in the 1950s, when film stars wore them on screen, did young people begin to see jeans as fashionable. Today more than two billion pairs are sold every year.
paraphrases: person who often bought from him
be in charge of making the product

tasks.title: Complete the summary
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the passage

"The pockets tore when they filled them with tools". "Weak" = "tore".
"Small metal pins, called rivets". "Metal ___" — ot, ko'plik.
"Register a patent, which cost 68 dollars". Farosat: "___ dollars" — son.
"A heavy blue cotton cloth called denim".
"Only in the 1950s, when film stars wore them". Farosat: "in the ___" — davr.
head: The story of jeans
rows: Strauss's shop sold clothing to gold (1). Their trousers had weak (2), so Jacob Davis added metal (3) to strengthen them. Davis could not pay the (4) dollars needed for a patent, so the two men shared it. The first jeans were made of a cloth called (5). They became fashionable only in the (6), after film stars wore them.

homework_intro: Bugun xulosadagi iborani matndagi asl ibora bilan bog'lashni o'rgandik — uyda xuddi shu ishni yolg'iz o'zingiz qilasiz.

Birinchi vazifa — "The man who made the world wear jeans" matni: soatga qarab 8 daqiqa qo'ying va 1–6 bo'sh joyni shu vaqt ichida to'ldiring, har javobdan keyin gapni qayta o'qib grammatikasini tekshiring.

Keyin paraphrase daftariga bugungi readinglardan 15 juft ko'chiring — chapga xulosadagi ibora, o'ngga matndagi asl ibora — va "The invention of the bar code" box mashqidagi ortiqcha to'rt so'z nega mos emasligini bittadan gap bilan yozing; ikkalasi birga 20 daqiqacha oladi.

Eng ko'p uchraydigan xato — javobni o'z so'zingiz bilan yozish yoki uch so'z yozish: ko'rsatma "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER" deydi, shuning uchun so'z matndan, o'zgartirmasdan va ikkitadan oshmasdan olinadi.
Uchala vazifani ham keyingi dars boshida daftar ochiq holda stolga qo'yasiz, javoblarni birga tekshiramiz va men har javob uchun "bu xulosadagi qaysi ibora, matnda qaysi ibora?" deb so'rayman.

options: The box has more words than gaps
Every word in the box is used
All the box words are nouns
The box words are copied from the text
kahoot.explain: Box'da ortiqcha so'zlar bo'ladi — ishlatilmaydiganlarini o'chirib boring.

kahoot.q: The text says 'The plan was dropped.' The box has 'abandoned'. Can it fill the gap 'The plan was ___'?
options: No — it is a different word
Only if it has capital letters
kahoot.explain: Box so'zi ko'pincha matndagi so'zning paraphrasei bo'ladi: dropped = abandoned.

kahoot.q: Do the answers in a summary usually follow the order of the text?
kahoot.explain: Odatda (USUALLY) ha — 3-javob matnda 2-javobdan keyin keladi.

kahoot.q: Why should you read the whole summary sentence again after writing an answer?
options: to count the words in the text
to change it into your own words
kahoot.explain: Qayta o'qiganda grammatik yoki mantiqiy xato darrov seziladi.

kahoot.q: Instruction: '…from the passage'. The text says 'huge'. Can you write 'big' in the gap?
options: No — use the word from the text
Yes — the meaning is the same
Yes — any synonym gets a mark
kahoot.explain: "From the passage" — javob matndagi so'z bilan, o'zgartirmasdan yoziladi; sinonim ball olmaydi.

kahoot.q: The gap is 'an ___ idea'. What does 'an' tell you about the missing word?
options: It begins with a vowel sound
It is a plural noun ending in -s
It is a verb in the past tense
It is a name with a capital letter
kahoot.explain: "an" unli tovush bilan boshlanadigan birlikdagi so'z oldidan keladi: an interesting idea.

kahoot.q: The gap is 'his ___' and a student writes 'the tools'. What is wrong?
kahoot.explain: "his" allaqachon aniqlovchi, shuning uchun "the" ortiqcha: "his tools", "his the tools" emas.

kahoot.q: Complete: Before selling her invention, she took ___ a patent to protect it.
kahoot.explain: "Take out a patent" — ixtiroga patent olmoq, ya'ni uni rasman himoya qilmoq.

kahoot.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'wealthy'?
kahoot.explain: Wealthy — boy, badavlat; healthy (sog'lom) bilan adashtirmang.

kahoot.q: If you 'overhear' a conversation, you…
kahoot.explain: Overhear — boshqalarning gapini tasodifan eshitib qolmoq.

kahoot.q: A 'manufacturer' is a company that…
kahoot.explain: Manufacturer — mahsulotni (ko'pincha zavodda) ishlab chiqaruvchi kompaniya.

kahoot.q: Things that 'wear out'…
kahoot.explain: Wear out — ko'p ishlatilgani uchun eskirib, yeyilib ketmoq.

kahoot.q: If you 'persuade' someone to do something, you…
kahoot.explain: Persuade — dalil keltirib, kimnidir biror ishni qilishga ko'ndirmoq.

kahoot.q: Clothes that are 'fashionable' are…
kahoot.explain: Fashionable — hozir modada bo'lgan, zamonaviy.

kahoot.q: If you are 'appalled' by something, you feel…
kahoot.explain: Appalled — yomon narsadan dahshatga tushgan, qattiq norozi.

lessons.title: Reading: Sentence Completion
lessons.grammar_topic: Sentence completion — gapni matndagi so'z bilan to'ldirish
lessons.book_ref: Jony Academy materiali — ustoz matni (#20) va mualliflik matnlari.
objectives: Gapni to'ldirishda so'z chegarasini (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS) aniq saqlash.
Bo'sh joy oldidagi va keyingi so'zlarga qarab kerakli so'z turini topish (farosat usuli).
Gapdagi kalit so'zning matndagi paraphraseini topib, javobni o'sha joydan olish.
Javobni gapga qo'yib qayta o'qish: grammatika va ma'no to'g'rimi?
4 ta matnda (ustoz matni + 3 ta Jony Academy matni) ishlash va har javobni isbotlash.
materials: Reading #20 "The honey badger" matni, 1–8 gaplari va glossariysi — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa; lekin matn dars boshida ustozda turadi va faqat sinf mashqidagi 6 ta bashorat yozilgandan keyin tarqatiladi.

Sinf mashqining 6 ta gapi ("fearless, ___ and tough", "will attack ___", "make it ___", "meat-based and ___", "___ form the biggest part", "by their ___") alohida varaqqa chiqarilsin yoki doskaning yopiq qismiga qo'ng'iroqdan oldin yozib qo'yilsin — o'quvchilar ularni matnsiz ko'radi.
1-qo'shimcha matn "The octopus: a clever escape artist" (1–7 gaplari va so'z chegarasi tahlilidagi 4 ta noto'g'ri variant bilan) — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa, mustaqil bajariladi.
2-qo'shimcha matn "How camels survive the desert" (1–7 gaplari bilan) — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa; bu bosqich vaqt bilan o'tkaziladi, shuning uchun ustozda sekundomer yoki devor soati tayyor tursin.
Uyga beriladigan paket: "The return of the wolves" matni va 7 ta gapi — har o'quvchiga bittadan, dars oxirida tarqatiladi.

Doskada qo'ng'iroqdan oldin: yirik harflar bilan "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS" va yonida "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER", ostida esa 6-savol tahliliga bo'sh joy (honey badger tekshirilgandan keyin to'ldiriladi: matnda "sense of smell", javob — "smell"); o'quvchilarda paraphrase daftari, xatolar daftari va qalam bo'lsin — javoblar avval qalamda yoziladi, chunki gapni qayta o'qib tuzatiladi.
timeline: Salomlashish; 14-dars uyga vazifasi ("The man who made the world wear jeans") daftarlari ochiq — 3 ta javob tez tekshiriladi. Summary completion bo'yicha 3 ta tezkor savol: 1) Box'li summary'da so'z matndagi shaklda bo'lishi shartmi? (Yo'q — ma'noga qarab box'dan tanlanadi.) 2) "the ___ of" orasiga qanday so'z kerak? (Ot.) 3) Summary matn tartibida boradimi? (Odatda — ha.)
Ustoz doskada: qoida, bosqichlar, tipik xatolar
Farosat: 6 ta bo'sh joy turi matnsiz aytiladi, keyin "The honey badger" tarqatiladi va 1–8-savollar birga bajariladi, har javob izohlanadi
Honey badger: "Find the paraphrases" (gapdagi so'z — matndagi ibora), o'quvchilar ovoz chiqarib topadi; 6-savol (sense of smell → smell) doskada tahlil
"The octopus" (1–7) mustaqil bajariladi, keyin javoblar izoh bilan tekshiriladi va "So'z chegarasi" tahlili
Kahoot (20 savol): sentence completion qoidalari va hayvonlar/tabiat lug'ati; har xato javobdan keyin izoh o'qiladi
"How camels survive the desert" — 10 daqiqa vaqt bilan (IELTS tezligi), keyin tahlil va farosat tekshiruvi
Xatolar daftari: har xato javob sababi bilan yoziladi
"The return of the wolves" uyga (10 daqiqa); xatolar daftari to'ldiriladi

intro: Sentence completion — gapning bir qismi beriladi, bo'sh joyni matndagi so'z bilan to'ldirasiz. Javob matndan AYNAN olinadi, o'zgartirilmaydi.
Ko'rsatmani birinchi o'qing: "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS" — bir yoki ikki so'z. Uch so'z yozsangiz, to'g'ri bo'lsa ham 0 ball.
Gaplar matn tartibida keladi (ALWAYS). 3-javob 2-javobdan keyingi joyda turadi.
Farosat: bo'sh joydan oldingi so'zga qarang. "will attack ___" — ot (kimni?); "make it ___" — sifat; "by their ___" — ot; "have a ___ with" — ot.
Gapdagi so'zlar matnda boshqacha aytiladi: masalan, gapda "stay alive", matnda "survive". Kalit so'zning paraphraseini qidiring.
Tuzoq: matnda javob uch so'zli bo'lishi mumkin (masalan, "sense of hearing"). Unda gapga mos keladigan va chegaraga sig'adigan qismini yozing ("hearing").
Javobni yozgach gapni to'liq o'qing. Grammatika buzilsa (birlik/ko'plik, sifat/ot) — javob noto'g'ri.
presentation: Javobni o'z so'zim bilan yozsam bo'ladimi?
Yo'q. Faqat matndagi so'z, o'zgartirmasdan.
Matnda javob uch so'z bo'lsa-chi?
Gapga mos va chegaraga sig'adigan qismini yozing. Masalan "sense of hearing" emas, "hearing".
Artikl (a/the) yozishim kerakmi?
Odatda yo'q — artikl gapda allaqachon bor bo'ladi.
Katta-kichik harf muhimmi?
Yo'q, lekin imlo muhim.
Javoblar tartibdami?
Ha, sentence completion javoblari matn tartibida keladi.
Ikki javob ham to'g'ridek tuyulsa?
Gapning qolgan qismini matn bilan solishtiring — faqat bittasi ma'noga to'liq mos keladi.
notes: Bu dars 2-dars (farosat) va 14-dars (summary completion) ko'nikmalariga tayanadi. Farqi: bu yerda har gap alohida.
Har javobdan keyin so'rang: "gapdagi qaysi so'z matndagi qaysi iboraga teng?"
Ustoz matnining 6-savoli (sense of smell) so'z chegarasi haqida eng yaxshi misol — honey badger tekshirilgandan KEYIN doskada alohida tahlil qiling (oldindan aytilsa, javob ochilib qoladi).
mistakes: Gap sifat talab qiladi; matndagi shakl aynan ko'chiriladi

Yosh qushlar uyadan ilk bor chiqqanda juda himoyasiz bo'ladi.
The fox has a reputation for being clever.

Kichkina it qo'rqmas edi va katta hayvonlarni quvib yubordi.

Burgutlar quyon va sichqonlar uchun xavfli yirtqichlardir.
