The cat used its sharp claws to climb the tree.
Mushuk daraxtga chiqish uchun o'tkir tirnoqlaridan foydalandi.
Snakes, lizards and tortoises are all reptiles.
Ilonlar, kaltakesaklar va toshbaqalar — hammasi sudralib yuruvchilar.
The bees carried nectar back to the hive.
Asalarilar gul shirasini uyaga olib keldi.
The chameleon is a master of disguise and can hide almost anywhere.
Xameleon niqoblanish ustasi, u deyarli hamma joyda yashirina oladi.

Kecha tunda hayvonot bog'idan maymun qochib ketdi.
In summer, water is scarce in the desert.

Asrlar davomida otlar ishonchli transport vositasi bo'lgan.

class_ex.title: Farosat: bo'sh joy turi
class_ex.instr: Matnga qaramasdan har bo'sh joy uchun qanday so'z kerakligini ayting.
items: fearless, ___ and tough
will attack ___ if they need to protect themselves
make it ___
meat-based and ___
___ form the biggest part
by their ___
why: Ikki sifat orasida — sifat.
"attack" dan keyin to'ldiruvchi ot.
"make it + sifat".
"and" bilan bog'langan ikkinchi sifat.
"form" ko'plik fe'l — ko'plik ot.
"their" dan keyin ot.

readings.title: Reading #20. The honey badger
text: It looks harmless and vulnerable. But the honey badger is afraid of nothing... and will attack and eat almost anything

The honey badger (Mellivora capensis) is an African and south-Asian mammal that has a reputation for being one of the world's most fearless animals, _despite its small size_. And in spite of its gentle-sounding name, it is also one of its most _aggressive_. Honey badgers have been known to attack lions, buffalo, and snakes three times their size. Even _humans_ are not safe from a honey badger _if it thinks the human will attack or harm it_. They are also extremely tough creatures, and can recover quickly from injuries that would kill most other animals.

At first glance, honey badgers look like the common European badger. They are usually between 75cm and 1 metre long, although males are about twice the size of females. They are instantly _recognisable_ by grey and white stripes that extend from the top of the head to the tail. Closer inspection, which is probably not a wise thing to do, reveals pointed teeth, and sharp front claws which can be four centimetres in length.

Honey badgers are _meat-eating_ animals with an extremely _varied_ diet. They _mainly eat_ a range of _small creatures_ like beetles, lizards and birds, but will also catch larger reptiles like snakes and small crocodiles. Some mammals, such as foxes, antelope and wild cats also form part of their diet.

The badgers _locate their prey_ mainly using their excellent sense of _smell_, and catch most of their prey through digging. During a 24-hour period, they may dig as many as fifty holes, and travel more than 40 kilometres. They are also good climbers, and can easily climb very tall trees to steal eggs from birds' nests, or catch other tree-dwelling creatures.

As their name suggests, honey badgers have always been associated with honey, although they do not actually eat it. It is the highly nutritious bee eggs (called 'brood') that they prefer, and they will do anything to find it. They usually cause a lot of damage to the hive in the process, and for this reason, humans are one of their main predators. Bee-keepers will often set _special traps_ for honey badgers, to protect their hives.

One of the most fascinating aspects of the honey badger is its _working relationship_ with a bird called the greater honeyguide (Indicator indicator). This bird deliberately guides the badger to beehives, then waits while the badger breaks into the hive and extracts the brood. The two creatures, bird and mammal, then share the brood between them.
paraphrases: if it thinks the human will attack or harm it
the pattern and colours on its back
a bird called the greater honeyguide

tasks.title: Questions 1–8: Complete the sentences
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage
tasks.instr: Gaplar matn tartibida (ALWAYS). Javobni gapga qo'yib qayta o'qing.
items: Although they are not big animals, honey badgers are fearless, ___ and tough.
Honey badgers will attack ___ if they need to protect themselves.
The pattern and colours on the honey badger's back make it ___.
The food they eat is meat-based and ___.
___ form the biggest part of a honey badger's diet.
Honey badgers find the creatures they eat by their ___.
___ are often used to catch honey badgers which attack beehives.
For one particular type of food, the honey badger has a ___ with another creature.
why: "One of its most aggressive". "Not big" = "small size". Ikki sifat orasida — sifat kerak.
"Even humans are not safe ... if it thinks the human will attack or harm it". Tuzoq: lions/buffalo — ular himoya uchun emas, umuman hujum qilinadigan hayvonlar.
"Instantly recognisable by grey and white stripes". "Make it + sifat": "recognise" (fe'l) emas.
"Meat-eating animals with an extremely varied diet". "Meat-based" = "meat-eating".
"They mainly eat a range of small creatures". "Mainly eat" = "form the biggest part". Ko'plik ot kerak ("form").
"Locate their prey mainly using their excellent sense of smell". "Sense of smell" — 3 so'z, chegaradan oshadi; "smell" yetarli va gapga mos.
"Bee-keepers will often set special traps for honey badgers". Ko'plik ("are"). "Traps" yoki "special traps" — ikkalasi ham to'g'ri.
"Its working relationship with a bird called the greater honeyguide". Food = brood, another creature = bird.
tasks.note: 6-savol eng muhim misol: matndagi to'liq ibora "sense of smell" 3 so'z. Javob — "smell". "Sense of smell" deb yozgan o'quvchi IELTSda 0 ball oladi.

find the creatures they eat [Q6]
another creature [Q8]

"Meat-eating animals".
"They mainly eat".
"The badgers locate their prey".
Oxirgi xatboshi.

readings.title: The octopus: a clever escape artist
text: In April 2016, staff at the National Aquarium of New Zealand arrived at work to find that one of their animals had disappeared. Inky, a male octopus, had pushed his way through a small gap at the top of his tank, travelled across the floor, and escaped down a drainpipe that led directly to the sea. The only evidence of his journey was a wet trail on the floor.

Stories like this are not unusual, because octopuses are among the most intelligent animals without a backbone. An octopus has around 500 million nerve cells, a number similar to that of a dog, but about two thirds of them are found not in its head but in its eight arms. As a result, each arm can taste, touch and even make simple decisions on its own.

The octopus is also a master of disguise. Special cells in its skin allow it to change colour in less than a second, so that it can hide against rocks or sand. Some species can even change the texture of their skin to look like coral. When this does not work, an octopus can release a cloud of dark ink, which confuses an attacker and gives the octopus time to swim away.
Its body is unusual in other ways too. An octopus has three hearts and blue blood, and because it has no bones, it can squeeze through any hole larger than its beak — the only hard part of its body.
Sadly, this remarkable life is short. Most species live for only one or two years, and a female usually dies soon after her eggs hatch, having stopped eating while she guarded them.

tasks.title: Complete the sentences
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS from the passage
tasks.instr: Gaplar matn tartibida. Javobni gapga qo'yib o'qing.
items: Inky left his tank through a small ___ at the top.
A ___ on the floor showed where Inky had gone.
Most of an octopus's nerve cells are in its ___.
An octopus can hide by changing its ___ very quickly.
If hiding fails, an octopus may use a cloud of ___ to escape.
The ___ is the only hard part of an octopus's body.
A female octopus stops eating while she is guarding her ___.
why: "Pushed his way through a small gap at the top of his tank".
"The only evidence of his journey was a wet trail on the floor". Evidence = showed. "Trail" yoki "wet trail" — ikkalasi ham to'g'ri.
"About two thirds of them are found ... in its eight arms". "Arms" yoki "eight arms" — ikkalasi ham 2 so'z ichida.
"Change colour in less than a second". Very quickly = less than a second.
"Release a cloud of dark ink". "Ink" yoki "dark ink" — ikkalasi ham to'g'ri.
"Its beak — the only hard part of its body". Artikl gapda bor.
"Having stopped eating while she guarded them" — them = eggs.

tasks.title: So'z chegarasi
items: 2-savol: "a wet trail"
3-savol: "its eight arms"
4-savol: "colours"
6-savol: "hard beak"
why: Gapda "A" allaqachon bor.
"its" gapda bor, 3 so'z bo'lib qoladi.
Matnda "colour" — birlikda.
Javob matndan aynan olinadi.

readings.title: How camels survive the desert
text: Many people believe that a camel stores water in its hump. In fact, the hump is made mostly of fat. When food is scarce, the camel's body breaks down this fat for energy, and the hump becomes smaller and may even fall to one side. A well-fed camel has a firm, upright hump.

The real secret of the camel's survival lies in how it uses water. A camel can lose up to a quarter of its body weight through water loss and still survive, while most mammals would die after losing half that amount. When it finally finds water, it can drink more than 100 litres in about ten minutes.
Its blood is also unusual. The red blood cells of a camel are oval rather than round, which allows them to keep flowing even when the blood becomes thick because the animal is short of water.

Camels also save water by not sweating very much. Their body temperature can rise by around six degrees during a hot day before they begin to sweat, and the heat stored in their body is released during the cold desert night.

Finally, a camel is well protected from sand. It has two rows of long eyelashes, and it can close its nostrils completely during a sandstorm. Wide, soft feet stop it from sinking into the sand, which is why camels are sometimes called "ships of the desert". For thousands of years, these features have made them the most reliable form of transport for people living in dry regions.

tasks.title: Complete the sentences
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the passage
items: A camel's hump contains mainly ___, not water.
A camel that has eaten well has a firm, ___ hump.
A camel can survive losing about ___ of its weight in water.
After a long time without water, a camel can drink over ___ very quickly.
Because they are ___, a camel's red blood cells can keep moving through thick blood.
Camels lose the heat from their bodies during the ___.
Camels can shut their ___ when there is a sandstorm.
why: "The hump is made mostly of fat". Mainly = mostly.
"A well-fed camel has a firm, upright hump". Eaten well = well-fed.
"Lose up to a quarter of its body weight".
"More than 100 litres in about ten minutes". Over = more than.
"Oval rather than round, which allows them to keep flowing". "Because they are + sifat" — tuzoq: "round" teskari.

"The heat stored in their body is released during the cold desert night". Released = lose. Javob: "night" yoki "desert night". "Cold night" matnda ketma-ket kelmaydi, "cold desert night" esa 3 so'z — chegaradan oshadi.
"It can close its nostrils completely during a sandstorm". Shut = close.

tasks.title: Farosat tekshiruvi
tasks.instr: Bo'sh joy turi va javob mosligini ayting.
items: 1-savol
3-savol
4-savol
5-savol
7-savol
why: "contains mainly + ot" — fat.
"about ___ of" — a quarter.
"over ___" — 100 litres.
"they are + sifat" — oval.
"their ___" — nostrils.

readings.title: The return of the wolves
text: By the 1920s, grey wolves had disappeared from Yellowstone, the oldest national park in the United States. Farmers and hunters had killed them to protect their animals, and for the next seventy years the park had no large predator at the top of its food chain.

Without wolves, the number of elk, a large kind of deer, grew quickly. The elk spent long periods feeding beside rivers, where they ate young willow and aspen trees before they could grow. Scientists noticed that very few new trees were appearing along the riverbanks.

In 1995 and 1996, thirty-one wolves were caught in Canada and released in the park. Their numbers rose steadily, and within ten years there were more than a hundred. The wolves hunted elk, but they also changed the way elk behaved: the deer began to avoid open river valleys where they could easily be attacked.
In several areas, willow trees started to recover. Beavers, which use willow for food and for building dams, returned in larger numbers, and their dams created pools where fish and birds could live.

However, researchers warn against telling this as a simple story. Hard winters, human hunting and the return of bears also reduced elk numbers, and in some places the trees have not come back at all. Most scientists now agree that the wolves played an important part in the changes, but not the only one — and that nature rarely has a single cause.

tasks.title: Complete the sentences
tasks.type: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER from the passage
items: Wolves were killed by farmers and ___.
Without wolves, the elk population ___.
Elk ate young trees beside the ___.
The wolves brought to the park in the 1990s came from ___.
Elk started to stay away from open ___.
Beavers use willow for food and for building ___.
Researchers say the changes did not have a ___.
why: "Farmers and hunters had killed them".
"The number of elk ... grew quickly".
"Feeding beside rivers". "Riverbanks" ham to'g'ri.
"Thirty-one wolves were caught in Canada".
"Avoid open river valleys". Stay away from = avoid.
"For food and for building dams".
"Nature rarely has a single cause".

tasks.title: Paraphrase daftari
tasks.instr: Har gapdagi paraphraseni matndagi juftiga yozing.
items: stay away from [Q5]
population [Q2]
came from [Q4]
why: 3-xatboshi.
2-xatboshi.
3-xatboshi.

homework_intro: Bugun bo'sh joyga matndan aynan mos so'zni topishni va so'z chegarasidan chiqmaslikni mashq qildik — uyda xuddi shu ishni yolg'iz o'zingiz bajarasiz.

Birinchi vazifa — "The return of the wolves" matni: soatga qarab 10 daqiqa qo'ying, 7 ta gapni shu vaqt ichida to'ldiring va har javobni gapga qo'yib qayta o'qing, grammatikasi buzilmasa javob to'g'ri.

Keyin so'z chegarasi daftariga bugungi to'rt matndan 6 ta javobni ko'chiring va har biriga bitta "noto'g'ri variant" yozing — uch so'zli, artikl qo'shilgan yoki shakli o'zgargan — hamda nega 0 ball olishini bir gapda tushuntiring; oxirida honey badger matnidan 8 ta paraphrase juftini yozasiz: chapga gapdagi so'z, o'ngga matndagi ibora. Ikkalasi birga 20 daqiqacha oladi.

Eng ko'p uchraydigan xato — matndagi to'liq iborani ko'chirib qo'yish: "sense of smell" uch so'z va 0 ball, kerakligi esa faqat "smell"; shuning uchun har javobni yozib bo'lgach so'zlarini sanab chiqing.

Uchala vazifani ham bitta daftarga bajaring va keyingi dars boshida daftar ochiq holda stolga qo'ying: javoblarni birga tekshiramiz va men har javob uchun "gapdagi qaysi so'z matndagi qaysi iboraga teng?" deb so'rayman.

homework.title: 4-matn: "The return of the wolves"

homework.title: So'z chegarasi daftari
homework.instr: Bugungi 4 matndan 6 ta javobni oling va har biri uchun "noto'g'ri variant" yozing (3 so'z, artikl bilan, shakli o'zgargan) — nega 0 ball ekanini tushuntiring.
homework.answers: Ustoz tekshiradi.

homework.title: Paraphrase juftlari
homework.instr: Honey badger matnidan 8 ta paraphrase juftini yozing: gapdagi so'z — matndagi ibora.
homework.answers: Reading bo'limidagi paraphrase jadvali bilan solishtiriladi.

kahoot.q: Instructions: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS. Which answer is too long?
kahoot.explain: "a sharp claw" — 3 so'z: artikl ham so'z hisoblanadi. Chegaradan oshgan javob to'g'ri bo'lsa ham 0 ball.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Owls hunt using their excellent sense of hearing.' Sentence: 'Owls find food mainly by their ___.' (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS)
kahoot.explain: "sense of hearing" — 3 so'z, "their hearing" da "their" takrorlanadi; gapga mos va chegarada — "hearing".

kahoot.q: In sentence completion, in what order do the answers usually appear in the text?
options: In the same order as the questions
Only in the first and last paragraphs
In random order across the passage
kahoot.explain: Sentence completion javoblari matn tartibida keladi: 3-javob 2-javobdan keyingi joyda turadi.

kahoot.q: Sentence: 'The desert fox is small but very ___.' What type of word is missing?
kahoot.explain: "is ... very" dan keyin sifat keladi: very fast, very clever.

kahoot.q: Sentence: '___ are the main food of this small lizard.' What must the answer be?
kahoot.explain: "are" ko'plik fe'li — bo'sh joyda ko'plik ot bo'ladi (insects, ants).

kahoot.q: Text: 'The frog's skin is highly poisonous.' Sentence: 'Its bright colour warns that the frog is ___.' Best answer?
kahoot.explain: "is + sifat" kerak: matndagi "poisonous" aynan ko'chiriladi; "poison" — ot, shakl o'zgargan.

kahoot.q: Can you change the form of a word from the text, e.g. 'protect' to 'protection'?
options: Yes, if the meaning is the same
kahoot.explain: Javob matndan aynan olinadi; so'z shakli o'zgarsa — javob noto'g'ri.

kahoot.q: The sentence already has 'the' before the gap. Should you write 'the' in your answer?
kahoot.explain: Artikl gapda bor — takrorlansa ortiqcha so'z bo'ladi va chegaradan oshishi mumkin.

kahoot.q: Which answer would get NO mark because of spelling?
kahoot.explain: "enviroment" da "n" tushib qolgan (to'g'risi: environment). Imlo xato — 0 ball.

kahoot.q: The sentence says 'find food'. Which phrase in the passage could be its paraphrase?
options: go back to their nest at night
kahoot.explain: "find food" = "look for something to eat": ma'no bir xil, so'zlar boshqa.

kahoot.q: ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER. Which answer is acceptable?
kahoot.explain: "15 kilometres" — raqam + 1 so'z, chegarada. Qolganlarida so'z ko'p: "about", "more than", "a distance of".

kahoot.q: You have written your answer. What should you do next?
options: Add a word to be on the safe side
kahoot.explain: Javobni gapga qo'yib qayta o'qing: grammatika (birlik/ko'plik, sifat/ot) va ma'no to'g'rimi?

kahoot.q: An animal that hunts and eats other animals is a…
kahoot.explain: predator — yirtqich; u ovlaydigan hayvon esa prey (o'lja).

kahoot.q: What does 'prey' mean?
options: a safe place where bees live
a hard shell on an animal
kahoot.explain: prey — o'lja: boshqa hayvon ovlab yeydigan jonivor.

kahoot.q: In the desert, water is 'scarce'. This means water is…
kahoot.explain: scarce — kam, topish qiyin.

kahoot.q: A 'vulnerable' animal is one that is…
kahoot.explain: vulnerable — himoyasiz, zaif: unga hujum qilish oson.

kahoot.q: Which verb means 'to stay alive in a very difficult situation'?
kahoot.explain: survive — omon qolmoq; escape — qochib ketmoq, protect — himoya qilmoq.

kahoot.q: Complete: 'Lions are at the top of the food ___.'
kahoot.explain: food chain — oziq zanjiri: kim kimni yeyishini ko'rsatadi.

kahoot.q: 'Reliable' is closest in meaning to…
kahoot.explain: reliable — ishonchli, unga tayanish mumkin.

kahoot.q: The fox has a 'reputation' for being clever. 'Reputation' means…
options: what people generally think of it
the place where it usually sleeps
kahoot.explain: reputation — obro', nom: odamlarning biror narsa haqidagi umumiy fikri.

lessons.title: Listening: Table Completion
lessons.grammar_topic: Table completion (listening) — jadvalni to'ldirish
lessons.book_ref: Jony Academy materiali — ustoz bergan audiolar (Track 27 Animal World, Track 12 Natural History day) va 3 ta mualliflik skripti.
objectives: Jadvalni to'ldirishda ustun sarlavhalaridan foydalanib "qanday so'z kerak" ekanini oldindan aniqlash.
Jadvalda savol raqamlari qanday joylashganini (qator yoki ustun bo'ylab) ko'rib, audioni raqamlar tartibida kuzatish.
To'liq bo'lgan kataklardan "langar" sifatida foydalanish: to'ldirilgan katak keyingi bo'sh katakni topishga yordam beradi.
So'z chegarasini saqlash va tuzatilgan (o'zgartirilgan) javobni yozish.
5 ta mashqda (2 ta ustoz audiosi + 3 ta skript) ishlash.
materials: Track 27 "Animal World — today's events" savol varag'i: to'rt ustunli jadval (name of event | location | type of event | time) va 1–7 bo'sh kataklari bilan — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa; transkript faqat ustozda, tekshirishdan keyin tarqatiladi.

Track 12 "Natural History day — morning events" savol varag'i: to'rt ustunli jadval (Name of event | Theme or topic | Type of event | Location) va 1–8 bo'sh kataklari bilan — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa.
Ikki audio — ielts5_16_animal_world.mp3 va ielts5_16_natural_history.mp3 — qo'ng'iroqdan oldin kolonkaga ulanib, ovozi sinab ko'rilsin va fayl boshiga qaytarilsin (har biri BIR MARTA qo'yiladi).

Uchta Jony Academy skripti ustoz qo'lida chop etilgan bo'lsin (Community centre — weekly classes, Museum floor guide, University open day — tour schedule): audiosi yo'q, ustoz oddiy tezlikda ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi; birinchi ikkitasining bo'sh jadvali o'quvchilarga ham nusxa qilinadi.

Doskaga dars boshlanishidan oldin ikki narsa yoziladi: ustun turlari qatori — location → joy nomi, time → soat, type of event → talk/film/workshop, theme → ot; va alohida ramkada tuzatish signallari — "no, sorry, correct that", "rather than", "in the ... , not ...". Yana: "Raqamlar qaysi tartibda?" mini-jadvali (Monday / Wednesday ustunlari, 1–6 raqamlari ustun bo'ylab) doskaning yopiq qismiga chiziladi.

Doskaning burchagiga yirik harflar bilan "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS OR A NUMBER"; uyga vazifa jadvali "University open day — tour schedule" (1–6) dars oxirida tarqatish uchun har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa, o'quvchilarda esa ustun turi daftari va qalam bo'lsin.
timeline: Salomlashish; 15-dars uyga vazifasi ("The return of the wolves" 1–7, so'z chegarasi daftari) tez tekshiriladi — har javob uchun "gapdagi qaysi so'z matndagi qaysi iboraga teng?" Sentence completion bo'yicha 3 ta tezkor savol: 1) TWO WORDS da "sense of smell" yozsa bo'ladimi? (Yo'q — 3 so'z.) 2) Matndagi so'z shaklini o'zgartirsa bo'ladimi? (Yo'q — aynan ko'chiriladi.) 3) Gaplar matn tartibida keladimi? (Ha.)
Ustoz doskada: ustun sarlavhalari, raqamlar tartibi (qator yoki ustun bo'ylab), langar kataklar, tuzatish signallari
"Qanday so'z kerak?" (ustun turi) va "Raqamlar qaysi tartibda?" mashqlari birga bajariladi, har javob izohlanadi
Track 27 jadvali: ustun turlari, langar kataklar (11 a.m., film, demonstration) va kutilgan paraphrase (location = "in the ...") belgilanadi
Animal World (1–7): BIR MARTA tinglanadi, keyin transkript bilan tekshiriladi va "Langar va paraphrase" tahlili
Natural History day (1–8): jadval o'qiladi, BIR MARTA tinglanadi, tekshiriladi; "Tuzatish tuzog'i" (4-savol) tahlili
Community centre (1–6) va Museum floor guide (1–6): ustoz oddiy tezlikda BIR MARTA o'qiydi, keyin tekshirish, chalg'ituvchi va ustun turi tahlili
Kahoot (20 savol: table completion qoidalari + tadbirlar lug'ati) ~10 daqiqa; qolgan 5 daqiqada xatolar daftari — har xato sababi bilan (ustun turi, tartib, tuzatish, so'z chegarasi)
"University open day" skripti uyga (10 daqiqa); ustun turi daftari va tuzatish tuzoqlari

intro: Table completion — jadval beriladi, ba'zi kataklar bo'sh. Har ustunning sarlavhasi (name, location, time, type) bo'sh katakka qanday so'z tushishini aytadi.

Audio savol RAQAMLARI tartibida boradi (1, 2, 3 …). Tinglashdan oldin raqamlar qanday joylashganini ko'ring: raqamlar qator bo'ylab ketsa — qatorma-qator, chapdan o'ngga tinglaysiz; ustun bo'ylab (yuqoridan pastga) ketsa — ustunma-ustun tinglaysiz.
To'ldirilgan kataklar — langar. Masalan, "The World of Ants ... 11 a.m." to'liq bo'lsa, siz ular orasidagi bo'sh kataklarni (location, type) shu voqea haqida gapirilganda tinglaysiz.
Ustun turi so'z turkumini beradi: "location" — joy nomi; "time" — soat; "type of event" — talk / film / workshop kabi ot.
Paraphrase: jadvalda "location", audioda "in the Science Hall" yoki "held in Room 14".
Tuzatish tuzog'i: "in the old gym, no, sorry, correct that — in the sports hall". Oxirgi javob yoziladi.
presentation: Qaysi tartibda tinglayman?
Savol raqamlari tartibida. Raqamlar qator bo'ylab ketsa — qatorma-qator, ustun bo'ylab ketsa — ustunma-ustun. Tinglashdan oldin raqamlar yo'lini qalam bilan belgilab chiqing.
Bir katakni o'tkazib yubordim.
To'liq kataklarga qarang — ular sizni keyingi bo'sh katakka olib boradi.
Ustun sarlavhasi nimaga kerak?
So'z turini aytadi: location → joy, time → soat, type → tadbir turi.
"Room 27" yoki "27"?
Ustun "location" bo'lsa "Room 27" (joy nomi); ko'rsatmani tekshiring.
Javob tuzatildi. Qaysi biri?
Oxirgi, tuzatilgan variant: "no, sorry, ...".
Katta harf muhimmi?
Yo'q, lekin nomlar (Science Hall, Studio B) katta harf bilan tabiiy ko'rinadi.
notes: Ikkala ustoz audiosi ham hayvonlar/tabiat mavzusida tadbirlar jadvali — bir xil format, o'quvchi ikkinchisida mustaqil ishlaydi.
Track 27 va Track 12 kalitlari Listening bo'limida; tekshirishda har javobni transkriptdagi iqtibos bilan ko'rsating.
Har javobdan keyin so'rang: "jadvaldagi qaysi ustun edi? audioda qaysi so'z bilan aytildi?"
Tuzatish tuzoqlari (Track 12: lecture room → main hall; Community centre: studio → computer room) mashq tekshirilgandan KEYIN doskada alohida ko'rsatiladi.
mistakes: Jadvalni har doim chapdan o'ngga o'qish
Audio savol raqamlari tartibida: qator yoki ustun bo'ylab

listenings.title: Track 27. Animal World — today's events
intro: Animal World markazidagi bugungi tadbirlar e'loni. Avval jadvalni o'rganing: har ustun (location, type of event, time) qanday so'z kerakligini aytadi. To'liq kataklar (11 a.m., film, demonstration) — langar. Keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS OR A NUMBER for each answer.
transcript: Hi there, everybody, and welcome to Animal World. Before you start your visit, I'd just like to tell you about a few special events happening here today. They're all free, and I'd really encourage you to go to as many of them as you can, as I think you'll learn a lot.

The first event is called The World of Ants, and it's happening this morning quite soon, in the Insect House, which is just a short walk from here. The well-known entomologist Dr David Crocker, who many of you will have seen on television, is giving a lecture all about ants – the different types of ants, how they organise themselves, what they eat, their behaviour and so on. It's actually a fascinating subject. So, The World of Ants, a lecture by Dr Crocker, in the Insect House, and it starts at 11 o'clock and lasts for 60 minutes.

At midday, that's 12 o'clock, there's a film which is just as fascinating and it's called The Great Migration. This is all about birds and how they migrate across continents and oceans using the Sun, the stars and the Earth's magnetic field. As I said, it's a film – an absolutely spectacular film – which all the family will enjoy, some fabulous photography, and it's on in Theatre C, which you can see just behind me – so bear that in mind for 12 o'clock.

The next event is a demonstration taking place in the Exhibition Room and given by Monica Chaddha. It's called Encouraging Garden Wildlife. Monica will be showing you ways of encouraging animals, birds and other wildlife to visit and live in your garden, how to place boxes for nests, what food to put out for them and all sorts of practical advice. That's at 2.30, so just after lunch.

The final free event for today is Birds of Prey. Tasha, their keeper, will be giving a display of some of our most magnificent birds and how they fly, and I thoroughly recommend this event. The display includes eagles, vultures and owls and will be starting at 3.45 on the lawn outside. It's an unforgettable experience, so remember, on the front lawn at 3.45 to see the birds flying.

listenings.title: Track 12. College Natural History day — morning events
intro: Kollej direktori talabalarga ertalabki tadbirlar haqida aytmoqda. Har talaba bittasini tanlashi kerak. Avval jadvalni o'qing, keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS OR A NUMBER for each answer.
transcript: Hello, everyone, and welcome to our college Natural History day. You've all got your programme for the day, but let me just give you a bit of information about your options for this morning's sessions, which begin at half past nine. Remember, you need to attend one of these three sessions.

All right, your first choice is called 'Dogs might fly', which will take place in Room 27. Professor Keenan, who you may remember ran a workshop last year on how dinosaurs became extinct, will be giving a lecture on the evolution of animals. In particular, she'll be looking at how they may evolve in the future, and this will be followed by a group discussion where you'll get a chance to ask her questions and offer your own thoughts and opinions on this. So, if the evolution of animals is something you're interested in, head for Room 27.

We all know that animals communicate with each other, but what about flowers? Your second choice is a video presentation called 'Flowers talk'. This considers the possibility that plants and flowers do actually communicate with each other. The video is presented by Patrick Bell, who has just written a book on how plants adapt to their natural environment, so it should be very interesting. That will take place in the lecture room, no, sorry, correct that, here in the main hall. We've had to move it because the lecture room is being renovated.

The third choice is ideal for those of you who want to get a bit of fresh air. We've called it 'A world in your garden', which we thought was appropriate as it looks at the sort of things you can find just by stepping out of your front door. Anyway, for those of you interested in getting away from the classroom, Doctor Watkins will be taking you on a nature walk through the local park, and she'll be telling you about some of the fascinating animals and plants that live and grow nearby. And it's a lovely day for a walk!

The final option, well, you might want to avoid this one if you're frightened of things like snakes, as this is a hands-on workshop where you'll actually get a chance to handle these exotic creatures. It won't just be snakes, however. I believe Tom Howard, our resident reptile expert, has brought some other reptiles along for you to meet, including his pet tortoise, Reggie, who is over 100 years old, and a pet lizard he calls Arthur. So, if you want to meet Reggie and his other reptile friends, head on over to the Biology lab at 9.30.

listenings.title: Community centre — weekly classes
intro: Jamoa markazi xodimi haftalik darslar jadvalini aytmoqda. Avval jadvalni o'qing, keyin bir marta tinglang.
transcript: Welcome to the Greenfield Community Centre. Let me run through our weekly classes so you can decide which suit you.
On Monday evenings we have a cookery class. It's held in the kitchen, of course, and it costs eight pounds a session. It's very popular, so please book ahead.
On Wednesdays there's a painting class in the art room. It runs from six to eight, and you should bring your own brushes, although we provide the paint.
Thursday is our busiest day. In the afternoon there's a yoga class in the main hall, which is free for members. And in the evening, the same hall is used for a dance class, which costs five pounds.

Finally, on Saturday mornings we run a photography class. This one meets in the computer room rather than a studio, because most of the work is editing pictures. It's suitable for beginners, and the teacher is a professional photographer.

listenings.title: Museum floor guide
intro: Muzey gidi qavatlarni tushuntirmoqda. Avval jadvalni o'qing, keyin bir marta tinglang.
transcript: Good morning and welcome to the City Museum. Let me explain what you'll find on each floor.

On the ground floor is the ticket desk and, next to it, the gift shop. The cloakroom used to be on this floor too, but it has moved to the basement. There's also a café here if you'd like a drink before you start.

The first floor is all about ancient history. The main attraction is a collection of Egyptian objects, including a very famous statue. Visitors often ask about mummies, but I'm afraid we don't have any. Photography is allowed, but without flash.
On the second floor you'll find the art gallery. This month there's a special exhibition of paintings by local artists, which is free with your ticket.
The third floor is our science area, which is especially popular with children because everything is hands-on. There's a new display about space that opened last week.
Finally, the top floor is a roof garden with a wonderful view over the city. It's closed in winter, and in spring it's often too windy, so it's open only in summer.

homework_intro: Bugun jadvalni ustun sarlavhasiga qarab to'ldirishni va tuzatilgan javobni ushlashni mashq qildik — uyda endi xuddi shu ishni yolg'iz o'zingiz bajarasiz.

Birinchi vazifa — "University open day — tour schedule" skripti: avval jadvalni o'qib chiqing, keyin bir marta tinglang yoki birovga bir marta o'qitib bering, to'xtatmang, 1–6 kataklarni to'ldiring va faqat shundan keyin transkriptni ochib tekshiring — hammasi 10 daqiqa vaqt oladi.

Ikkinchisi — "Ustun turi daftari": Track 27 va Track 12 jadvallaridan 8 ta bo'sh katak ko'chirib, har biriga ustun turini (location / time / type / theme) va qanday so'z kutilganini yozasiz; uchinchisi — "Tuzatish tuzoqlari": bugungi besh mashqdan tuzatilgan yoki rad etilgan 4 ta javobni signali bilan yozib (main hall, computer room rather than a studio kabi), oxirgi to'g'ri variantni belgilaysiz — ikkalasi birga 20 daqiqacha.

Eng ko'p qilinadigan xato — birinchi eshitilgan so'zni shosha-pisha yozib qo'yish: Track 12 dagi 4-savolni eslang — avval "lecture room", keyin tuzatilgan "main hall" aytildi; har doim bo'sh joy nimani so'rayotganini (joy, taom, vaqt) tekshiring. Tuzatish daftarida esa signali ko'rsatilmagan qator qabul qilinmaydi, u qator uchun ball yo'q.

Uchala vazifani ham keyingi dars boshida daftar ochiq holda stolga qo'yasiz, javoblarni birga tekshiramiz va men har javob uchun "bu jadvaldagi qaysi ustun edi, audioda qaysi so'z bilan aytildi?" deb so'rayman.

kahoot.q: Column heading: 'Location'. What kind of answer do you expect?
options: a time, e.g. quarter past ten
a type of event, e.g. a talk
a person's name, e.g. Dr Hill

kahoot.q: Column heading: 'Type of event'. Which answer fits?

kahoot.q: In which order does the audio give the answers in a table?
options: Always row by row, left to right
Always column by column, top down
In any order the speaker likes

kahoot.q: Gaps (1)–(3) go down the first column and (4)–(6) down the second. What will you hear?

kahoot.q: Speaker: 'The talk is in Room 5 — no, sorry, correct that — in Room 9.' What do you write?
kahoot.explain: "no, sorry, correct that" dan keyingi — oxirgi variant yoziladi: Room 9.

kahoot.q: Speaker: 'This year we meet in the canteen rather than the old gym.' Where do they meet?

kahoot.q: NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS OR A NUMBER. Which answer is too long?

kahoot.q: You missed answer 3 and the speaker is already talking about the next event. What should you do?
options: Go on and listen for answer 4
Stop and wait for it to be repeated
Leave the rest of the table empty
Go back and read the whole table
kahoot.explain: Audio qaytarilmaydi: keyingi javobni kuting, 3-katakka oxirida mantiqiy taxmin yozing.

kahoot.q: Why are the cells that are already filled in useful?
options: They help you keep your place
They show the word limit for each gap
They are never mentioned in the audio
kahoot.explain: To'liq kataklar — langar: ular aytilganda qaysi qatordaligingizni bilasiz.

kahoot.q: Heading: 'Price'. Speaker: 'It's twelve pounds, but members pay half.' What is the price for non-members?
kahoot.explain: A'zo bo'lmaganlar uchun narx to'g'ridan-to'g'ri aytilgan: twelve pounds = £12. Hisoblash shart emas.

kahoot.q: What does 'correct that' tell you in a talk?
options: The first answer is the right one
kahoot.explain: "correct that" — tuzatish signali: undan keyingi ma'lumot to'g'ri javob.

kahoot.q: Do capital letters matter in IELTS Listening answers?
kahoot.explain: Katta-kichik harf hisobga olinmaydi, lekin imlo xato bo'lsa — 0 ball.

kahoot.q: An 'exhibition' is…
options: a public show of art or objects
a long talk by a university professor
a short walk around a park
a class where you cook food
kahoot.explain: exhibition — ko'rgazma: san'at asarlari yoki buyumlar namoyishi.

kahoot.q: Which phrase means 'to happen' (for a planned event)?
kahoot.explain: take place — bo'lib o'tmoq; take part in — qatnashmoq.

kahoot.q: 'The class is popular, so please book ahead.' This means…
options: bring a book with you to the class
pay when you arrive at the door
kahoot.explain: book ahead — oldindan joy band qilmoq.

kahoot.q: In a 'hands-on' workshop, you…
kahoot.explain: hands-on — amaliy: ishni o'zingiz qo'lingiz bilan bajarasiz.

kahoot.q: 'The old theatre is being renovated.' This means it is…
kahoot.explain: renovate — ta'mirlamoq, yangilamoq.

kahoot.q: 'Student accommodation' means…
kahoot.explain: accommodation — turar joy.

kahoot.q: A class that is 'suitable for beginners' is…
kahoot.explain: suitable — mos: yangi boshlovchilar uchun to'g'ri keladi.

kahoot.explain: guided tour — gid hamrohligidagi ekskursiya.

lessons.title: Listening: Map / Plan Labelling
lessons.grammar_topic: Map labelling — xarita yoki reja bo'yicha joyni harf bilan belgilash
lessons.book_ref: Jony Academy materiali — ustoz bergan audiolar (Track 28 zoo map; Track 13 college plan — eng qiyin, oxirida) va 3 ta mualliflik skripti. Xaritalar kitobdagi joylashuv bo'yicha qayta chizilgan.
objectives: Yo'l ko'rsatish so'zlari va joylashuv predloglarini tinglab tanish: turn left/right, go past, cross, opposite, next to, between, at the corner.
Tinglashdan oldin xaritada "You are here" nuqtasini, yo'llarni va belgilangan joylarni topish.
So'zlovchi bilan birga xarita bo'ylab "yurish" — har yo'nalishdan keyin qayerda ekanini kuzatish.
"Chap / o'ng" ni so'zlovchi qaysi tomonga qarab yurganiga qarab aniqlash (xaritaga qarab emas).
5 ta mashqda (2 ta ustoz audiosi + 3 ta skript) ishlash; eng qiyini — oxirida.
materials: Doskaga dars boshlanishidan oldin strelkalar bilan 14 ta yo'nalish so'zini yozib qo'ying: turn left / turn right, go straight ahead, go past, cross, opposite, next to, between, at the corner of, T-junction, Y-junction, crossroads, roundabout, traffic lights, zebra crossing. Birinchi sinf mashqi ("Yo'nalish so'zlari") shular bo'yicha ketadi va so'zlar dars oxirigacha o'chirilmaydi.
Zoo xaritasi (ielts5_17_zoo_map.png) - har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa; A-G harflari aniq ko'rinsin, o'quvchi javobni xaritaning ustiga yozadi.

Riverside Park (ielts5_17_park.png) va Westgate Shopping Centre (ielts5_17_shopping.png) xaritalari - har o'quvchiga bittadan. Bu ikki mashqda audio YO'Q, skriptni ustoz o'zi ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi, shuning uchun ikkala skript matnini ustoz uchun alohida chop etib oling.

Track 13 kollej rejasi (ielts5_17_college_plan.png) - har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa, A4 to'liq o'lchamda: A-K harflari ko'p, kichraytirib chop etilsa xonalar bir-biridan farqlanmaydi. Rejada "Main hall" yozuvi va eshiklar yo'q: nusxa ko'paytirishdan oldin asl nusxada Reception qarshisidagi nomsiz katta xonaga "Main hall" deb yozing va H xonasining eshigi markaziy yo'lakka ochilishini (ko'ndalang yo'lakka emas) kichik strelka bilan ko'rsating. Reja ekranda ko'rsatilsa, bu ikki belgini tinglashdan oldin og'zaki ayting.

Audio dars boshlanishidan oldin ochilgan va ovozi tekshirilgan bo'lsin: ielts5_17_zoo.mp3 (Track 28) va ielts5_17_college.mp3 (Track 13). Ikkalasi ham BIR MARTA qo'yiladi, shuning uchun kolonka ishlayotganiga oldindan ishonch hosil qiling.

Har o'quvchida oddiy qalam va o'chirg'ich bo'lsin - 4-bosqichda yo'l xarita ustida qalam bilan chizib boriladi; uyga beriladigan "Getting around the town centre" xaritasi (ielts5_17_town.png) ham har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa qilib tayyorlansin.
timeline: Salomlashish; 16-dars uyga vazifasi ("University open day" skripti, Ustun turi daftari, Tuzatish tuzoqlari) tez tekshiriladi. Table completion bo'yicha 3 ta tezkor savol: 1) Bo'sh katakka qanday so'z kerakligini nima ko'rsatadi? (Ustun sarlavhasi: joy, vaqt, narx.) 2) Raqamlar ustun bo'ylab ketsa, audio qaysi tartibda boradi? (Savol raqamlari tartibida, ustunma-ustun.) 3) "No, sorry, it's been moved to..." nima signal? (Tuzatish: oxirgi aytilgani javob.)
Ustoz doskada: map labelling qoidasi, 6 bosqich, "on your left" — yuruvchining chap-o'ngi, tipik xatolar

BIR MARTA tinglanadi (1–3), kalit why bilan tekshiriladi; "Yo'nalish zanjiri": har javobga qaysi so'zlar olib bordi

Kahoot (20 savol): map labelling qoidalari va yo'l/joy lug'ati; har xato javobdan keyin izoh o'qiladi
Eng qiyin mashq, oxirida: nusxada "Main hall" va H eshigi belgilangani tekshiriladi, Reception, Sports Hall va A–K topiladi; BIR MARTA tinglanadi (1–5), tekshirish va "Nisbiy joylashuv zanjiri"
Xatolar daftari: har xato sababi bilan — xaritaning chap-o'ngi olingan / langar yo'qotilgan / chegara joy javob deb olingan / opposite va next to aralashgan
Uyga vazifa: "Getting around the town centre" skripti (ielts5_17_town.png xaritasi bilan), Yo'nalish lug'ati (doskadagi 14 so'z), O'z xaritangiz; xatolar daftari to'ldiriladi

intro: Map labelling — xarita yoki bino rejasi beriladi, joylar harflar (A–G) bilan belgilangan. Siz har nom (gift shop, café) qaysi harfga to'g'ri kelishini yozasiz.
BIRINCHI qadam: "You are here" yoki "entrance" ni toping. So'zlovchi har doim shu nuqtadan boshlaydi.
So'zlovchi xarita bo'ylab tartib bilan "yuradi". Savollar ham odatda (USUALLY) shu tartibda keladi. Qalam bilan yo'lni kuzating.
ENG MUHIM: "on your left / on your right" — yurayotgan odamning chap-o'ngi. Agar u xaritada pastga qarab yursa, uning o'ngi sizning chapingiz bo'ladi. Xaritani aylantirib qarash ham mumkin.
Yo'nalish so'zlari: turn left / turn right, go straight ahead, go past, cross, take the first right, at the crossroads / junction / roundabout.
Joylashuv so'zlari: opposite (qarshisida), next to (yonida), between (orasida), at the corner of (burchagida), just beyond / just over (sal narida), at the end of (oxirida).
Tuzoq: bir necha joy tilga olinadi, lekin faqat savoldagisi javob. "Don't go too far, or you'll come to the aquarium" — akvarium savolda yo'q, u faqat chegara.
presentation: "On your left" — xaritaning chapimi?
Yo'q! Yurayotgan odamning chapi. Pastga yursa — teskari bo'ladi.
Yo'lni yo'qotib qo'ydim.
Keyingi langarni kuting (lake, reception, crossroad) va o'sha joydan davom eting.
Bir harf ikki marta ishlatiladimi?
Odatda yo'q. Ba'zi harflar umuman ishlatilmaydi.
"Opposite" nima degani?
Yo'lning qarama-qarshi tomonida, to'g'ri qarshisida.
Savollar tartibdami?
Odatda ha — so'zlovchi yurgan tartibda.
Harfni emas, nomni yozsam-chi?
Ko'rsatmada "letter" deyilgan — faqat harf yozing.
notes: Darsni yo'nalish so'zlari bilan boshlang: doskada strelkalar chizib, turn left / turn right, go straight ahead, go past, cross, opposite, next to, between, at the corner of, T-junction, Y-junction, crossroads, roundabout, traffic lights, zebra crossing so'zlarini ko'rsating.
Track 28 (hayvonot bog'i) — oson: bitta yo'l, aniq langarlar (lake, penguins). Track 13 (kollej rejasi) — eng qiyin: ko'p xona, eshiklar va koridorlar. Shuning uchun u darsning OXIRIDA.
Kalitlar: Track 28 — 1 F, 2 E, 3 A (skript va xarita bo'yicha asoslangan; 3-savolda "at the end of the path" A ni ko'rsatadi, B — tuzoq); Track 13 — 1 D, 2 E, 3 K, 4 C, 5 B.
Xaritalar asl kitob rasmidagi joylashuv bo'yicha Jony Academy tomonidan qayta chizilgan.
mistakes: Tilga olingan har joyni javob deb o'ylash

listenings.title: Track 28. Zoo — directions from the main building
intro: Hayvonot bog'ida xodim tashrif buyuruvchilarga yo'l ko'rsatmoqda. Avval xaritada "You are here" va "main building" ni toping. Yo'l qayerda ikkiga ayriladi? Lake va penguins qayerda? Keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Write the correct letter, A–G, next to questions 1–3.
transcript: Now, I'll just give you a few directions before you leave, especially for those of you who are feeling a bit hungry. When you leave the main building, you come to an area where the path divides. If you take the right-hand path, you'll see the lake on your right, and exactly opposite the lake on your left is the gift shop. Apart from selling gifts, it sells snacks, sandwiches and light drinks. If you walk on past the lake, on your right you'll also see the penguins. Go past the penguins and you'll come to the restaurant, also on your right. Don't go too far, or you'll come to the aquarium. The aquarium is on your right at the crossroad, and just over the crossroad, also on your right, is the lion enclosure.

If you're thinking of having a picnic, the best place to go is the picnic area, and for this you need to turn left at the crossroad and walk along a few metres. At the end of the path, you'll find the picnic area on your left.
Now, if you have any questions, I'd be happy to answer them and, once again, I really hope you enjoy your visit. Thank you.

tasks.title: Questions 1–3: Write the correct letter, A–G
tasks.instr: So'zlovchi bilan xarita bo'ylab yuring. Chap/o'ng — yuruvchiniki.
items: 1 gift shop
2 restaurant
3 picnic area
why: "The path divides ... take the right-hand path ... the lake on your right, and exactly opposite the lake on your left is the gift shop". O'ng yo'lda yuqoriga yursangiz, ko'l o'ngda, uning qarshisida chapda — F.

"Walk on past the lake ... on your right ... the penguins. Go past the penguins and you'll come to the restaurant, also on your right". Penguinsdan keyingi o'ngdagi joy — E. Tuzoq: D — akvarium ("on your right at the crossroad"), C — sher qo'rasi ("just over the crossroad").

"Turn left at the crossroad and walk along a few metres. At the end of the path ... on your left". Chapga burilgach (g'arbga), chap tomon — janub; yo'l oxirida — A. Tuzoq: B — yo'l boshida, oxirida emas.
tasks.note: Kalit: 1 F · 2 E · 3 A (skript va xarita bo'yicha asoslangan). 3-savolda hal qiluvchi ibora — "at the end of the path": chapga burilgach yo'lning OXIRIGACHA yuriladi, u yerda chapda A turadi. B yo'lning boshida — "walk along a few metres" ni eshitib B ni tanlaganlar oxirgi iborani o'tkazib yuborgan.

intro: Park xodimi darvoza oldida tashrif buyuruvchilarga yo'l ko'rsatmoqda. Avval "main gate" ni toping. Skriptni ustoz bir marta o'qiydi.
transcript: Welcome to Riverside Park. You're standing at the main gate, so let me tell you where everything is.
As soon as you come in, you'll see the café straight away on your right. It's a good place for a hot drink on a cold day. The toilets are just opposite, on your left.

If you walk straight up the main path, just before you reach the crossroads, you'll see the pond on your right. That's where you can hire a boat — the boat hire hut is right next to the pond, on your right.
For those of you with children, the playground is a little further. When you get to the crossroads, turn left, and at the end of that path, on your right, you'll find the playground.

listenings.title: Westgate Shopping Centre — ground floor
intro: Savdo markazi ma'lumot xodimi (Part 2). Avval "West entrance" va koridorni toping. Skriptni bir marta tinglang.
transcript: Good morning and welcome to Westgate Shopping Centre. If you've come in through the west entrance, you're at the start of our main corridor.
The first shop on your left is a sports shop, and the second shop on your left is the bookshop, which has a small café inside.
Directly opposite the bookshop, on your right, is the bank, where you'll also find cash machines.
If you're here to see a film, the cinema is at the very end of the corridor, on your right, next to the bank.
The pharmacy, by the way, is the first shop on your right as you come in.

tasks.title: Write the correct letter, A–F
tasks.instr: Sharqqa qarab yuring: chap — shimol (A B C), o'ng — janub (D E F).
items: 1 bookshop
2 bank
3 cinema
why: "The second shop on your left". Birinchisi A (sports shop), ikkinchisi — B.
"Directly opposite the bookshop, on your right". B ning qarshisi — E.
"At the very end of the corridor, on your right, next to the bank". Tuzoq: D — dorixona ("first shop on your right").

tasks.title: Tartib so'zlari
tasks.instr: first / second / at the very end.
items: first on your left
second on your left
first on your right
why: Savolda yo'q.
Bookshop.
Oxirida aytilgan — tartibni buzadi.

listenings.title: Getting around the town centre
intro: Turistik ma'lumot xodimi vokzaldan chiqqanlarga yo'l ko'rsatmoqda. Uyda bir marta tinglang.
transcript: Welcome to Kingsford. When you leave the station, walk straight ahead up the main road.
The first building you'll pass on your left is the post office, and opposite it, on your right, is a small supermarket.
At the top of the road there's a T-junction. The building directly opposite you is the town museum, which is free to enter.
To get to the hotel, turn right at the junction and it's the first building on your left, just past the museum.
If you need the bus station, it's also on this road, but on your right, across from the hotel.

tasks.title: Write the correct letter, A–F
items: 1 post office
2 museum
3 hotel
why: "The first building you'll pass on your left". Tuzoq: B — "opposite it, on your right" — supermarket.
"At the T-junction ... directly opposite you". Junction qarshisi — D.

"Turn right at the junction ... the first building on your left, just past the museum". Sharqqa yursangiz, chap — shimol; D dan keyin — E. Tuzoq: F — avtobus bekati ("on your right, across from the hotel").

tasks.title: Yo'nalish zanjiri
tasks.instr: Har javobga qaysi so'zlar olib bordi?
items: walk straight ahead + first on your left
T-junction + directly opposite
turn right + first on your left, just past
why: Post office.
Museum.
Hotel.

listenings.title: Track 13. College plan — for visiting students
listenings.qtype: Plan labelling (1–5) — eng qiyin, oxirgi mashq
intro: Kollejga kelgan talabalarga bino rejasi tushuntirilmoqda. Bu eng qiyin mashq: ko'p xona, koridorlar va eshiklar. Avval rejada "College entrance", "Reception", "Sports Hall" va "Parking area for bicycles" ni toping. Rejada "Main hall" yozuvi yo'q: bu — kirish yo'lagining chap tomonidagi, Reception ning to'g'ri qarshisidagi nomsiz katta xona (nusxada belgilanmagan bo'lsa, o'quvchilar uni "Main hall" deb yozib qo'yadi). Rejaga eshiklar chizilmagan, shuning uchun bitta qoidani ham aytib qo'ying: H xonasining eshigi markaziy (Sports Hall tomonga boradigan) yo'lakka ochiladi, ko'ndalang yo'lakka eshigi yo'q. Keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Write the correct letter, A–K, next to questions 1–5.
transcript: OK, now, we've got some students here from Bardwell College who have joined us for today's events. Hello to you all, and welcome.

Now, before our day begins, you'll need to get a guest badge, which you'll have to wear while you're on the college premises. You can get these from the administration office. To get there from the main hall, leave the hall by the door opposite reception, turn left, and just follow the corridor to the end. The administration office is on your right. Don't go any further, or you'll be in the sports hall. If you show your guest badge in the café, by the way, you'll get a 20% discount on drinks and sandwiches.

To get there from the main hall, walk along the corridor between the main hall and reception and turn right. The café is through the first door on your left. Directly opposite the café, on the same corridor, is the student common room, where you can go to relax and perhaps meet some of our own students.

If you have any valuables that you don't want to carry around with you, I suggest you put these in a locker. These are next to the sports hall, opposite the administration office. You can get a key for a locker when you get your guest badge from the administration office.

And if you want to use our library, leave the main hall by the door opposite the one you came in – that's the door by the bicycle parking area – and walk to the end of the corridor. The library is through the door straight ahead of you.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5: Write the correct letter, A–K
tasks.instr: Eng qiyin mashq: har yo'nalishdan keyin qayerdaligingizni qalam bilan belgilang.
items: 1 Administration office
2 Café
3 Student common room
4 Lockers
5 Library
why: "Leave the hall by the door opposite reception, turn left, and just follow the corridor to the end. The administration office is on your right. Don't go any further, or you'll be in the sports hall". Koridor oxirida, sport zali oldida o'ngda — D.

"Walk along the corridor between the main hall and reception and turn right. The café is through the first door on your left". O'ngga burilgach, chap tomondagi birinchi eshik — E (H ning eshigi bu yo'lakka emas, markaziy yo'lakka ochiladi, shuning uchun H tuzoq).
"Directly opposite the café, on the same corridor". E ning qarshisi — K.
"Next to the sports hall, opposite the administration office". D ning qarshisi, sport zali yonida — C.
"Leave the main hall by the door ... by the bicycle parking area – and walk to the end of the corridor. The library is through the door straight ahead of you". Koridor oxirida to'g'ri oldinda — B.
tasks.note: Ustoz kaliti: 1 D · 2 E · 3 K · 4 C · 5 B. Bu mashq qiyin, chunki 3 va 4-savol boshqa joyga NISBATAN beriladi (opposite the café, opposite the administration office) — oldingi javob xato bo'lsa, keyingisi ham xato bo'ladi.

tasks.title: Nisbiy joylashuv zanjiri
items: 3 (common room)
4 (lockers)
Chegara so'zi
answers: "Don't go any further, or you'll be in the sports hall"
why: "Directly opposite the café" — E qarshisi K.
"Opposite the administration office" — D qarshisi C.
D ni tasdiqlaydi.

homework_intro: Bugun biz xarita bo'ylab so'zlovchi bilan birga yurdik - uyga vazifa ham xuddi shu ish, faqat endi men yoningizda bo'lmayman, o'zingiz yolg'iz bajarasiz.

Birinchi vazifa - "Getting around the town centre" skripti: xaritani oldingizga qo'ying, BIR MARTA tinglang yoki o'qitib eshiting, 3 ta harfni yozing, keyin transkript bilan tekshiring; bunga 10 daqiqa yetadi.

Eng ko'p qilinadigan xato - chap va o'ngni xaritaga qarab olish: "on your left" yurayotgan odamning chapi, u burilgandan keyin sizning chapingiz o'zgaradi, shuning uchun har yo'nalishdan keyin qalam bilan qayerda turganingizni belgilab boring.
Ikkinchi vazifa - Yo'nalish lug'ati: doskadagi 14 ta so'zni o'zbekcha tarjimasi va bittadan gap bilan ko'chiring, taxminan 15 daqiqa ketadi.

Uchinchi vazifa - O'z xaritangiz: uyingizdan maktabgacha A-F harfli oddiy xarita chizing va 5 gaplik yo'l ko'rsatish matnini yozing; keyingi dars boshida daftarlarni yig'aman, xaritangizni esa sherigingiz tinglab harflarni topadi.

homework.title: 4-skript: "Getting around the town centre"
homework.instr: Uyda bir marta tinglang (yoki o'qitib eshiting), xaritada harflarni yozing, keyin transkript bilan tekshiring.
homework.answers: Javoblar Listening bo'limida.

homework.title: Yo'nalish lug'ati
homework.instr: Doskadagi 14 ta yo'nalish/joylashuv so'zini (turn left / turn right, go straight ahead, go past, cross, opposite, next to, between, at the corner of, T-junction, Y-junction, crossroads, roundabout, traffic lights, zebra crossing) o'zbekcha tarjimasi va bittadan gap bilan yozing.
homework.answers: 14 qator, gap bilan.

homework.title: O'z xaritangiz
homework.instr: Uyingizdan maktabgacha oddiy xarita chizing (A–F harflar bilan) va 5 gaplik yo'l ko'rsatish matnini yozing. Keyingi darsda sherigingiz tinglab harflarni topadi.
homework.answers: Ustoz yo'nalish so'zlari to'g'ri ishlatilganini tekshiradi.

kahoot.q: In a map labelling task, what should you find first, before the recording starts?
options: The starting point, e.g. 'You are here'
The letter that is used most often on the map
The longest name in the list of questions
The place that is furthest from the exit
kahoot.explain: So'zlovchi har doim boshlanish nuqtasidan ("You are here", entrance) yuradi, shuning uchun avval o'shani topasiz.

kahoot.q: You follow a route DOWN the map, towards the bottom of the page. The speaker says: 'The bank is on your right.' Where is the bank on the page?
options: To the left of the path
To the right of the path
kahoot.explain: Pastga yurayotgan odamning o'ngi xaritaga qaraganingizda sizning chapingiz bo'ladi.

kahoot.q: The instructions say: 'Write the correct letter, A–G.' What do you write in the answer box?
kahoot.explain: Ko'rsatmada "letter" deyilgan — faqat harf yoziladi, joy nomi yozilmaydi.

kahoot.q: The speaker says: 'Don't go too far, or you'll come to the car park.' The car park is not in your questions. Why is it mentioned?
options: It tells you where to stop
It is a place you must label
It is a mistake in the recording
kahoot.explain: Savolda yo'q joy — chegara (langar): shu yerdan o'tib ketmang degan belgi, javob emas.

kahoot.q: Do map labelling questions usually follow the order of the speaker's route?
options: Only if the map has a compass
Only in Part 4 of the test
kahoot.explain: Odatda (USUALLY) savollar so'zlovchi yurgan tartibda keladi.

kahoot.q: You lose your place on the map while listening. What is the best thing to do?
options: Wait for the next landmark, then continue
Stop and read all the questions again
Write the same letter for every question
Go back to the first question and restart
kahoot.explain: Keyingi langar (lake, reception, crossroads) tilga olinganda yana yo'lga qo'shilasiz.

kahoot.q: 'The chemist's is directly opposite the café.' Where is the chemist's?
options: Across the street, facing the café
Beside the café, on the same side
Behind the café, a bit further on
Inside the same building as the café
kahoot.explain: Opposite — ko'chaning narigi tomonida, to'g'ri qarshisida; next to esa yonida degani.

kahoot.q: 'Go past the bakery, and the gym is the next building.' Which building is the gym?
options: The one across from the bakery
kahoot.explain: Go past — yonidan o'tib keting: javob undan KEYINGI bino.

kahoot.q: On a building plan, why can one wrong answer lead to a second wrong answer?
options: Some rooms are given relative to other rooms
The questions are printed twice on the page
Every room on the plan has two letters
The speaker changes the plan halfway
kahoot.explain: "Opposite the library" kabi joylar boshqa xonaga nisbatan beriladi — o'sha xona xato topilsa, bu javob ham xato bo'ladi.

kahoot.q: What is the best way to use your pencil while you listen to directions?
options: Trace the speaker's route on the map
Write down every word the speaker says
Circle every letter before you listen
Draw a new map of your own town
kahoot.explain: Qalam bilan yo'lni chizib borsangiz, qayerda turganingizni yo'qotmaysiz.

kahoot.q: The speaker says: 'Turn left at the junction, and it's on your right.' Whose right is this?
options: The right of the map's author
kahoot.explain: Burilgandan keyin yuruvchining chap-o'ngi o'zgaradi: har doim hozirgi yurish yo'nalishi bo'yicha oling.

kahoot.q: Can one letter be the answer to two different questions in the same map task?
options: Usually not; some letters are not used
Yes, every letter is used twice
Yes, if the places have similar names
Yes, the first letter is always used twice
kahoot.explain: Odatda har harf bir marta ishlatiladi, ba'zi harflar esa umuman javob bo'lmaydi.

kahoot.q: Which word means 'a place where two roads cross each other'?
kahoot.explain: Crossroads — ikki yo'l kesishgan joy (chorraha); roundabout — aylanma halqa yo'l.

kahoot.q: Choose the word: 'The bank is ___ the hotel, on the other side of the street.'
kahoot.explain: "On the other side of the street" — ko'chaning narigi tomonida, ya'ni qarshisida: opposite.

kahoot.q: What is a 'T-junction'?
options: Where one road ends at another road
A road that goes round in a circle
A place where people cross the road
A road that is closed to all traffic
kahoot.explain: T-junction — bir yo'l boshqa yo'lga borib tutashadigan va shu yerda tugaydigan joy (T shaklida).

kahoot.q: At a zoo, what is an 'enclosure'?
options: A fenced area where animals are kept
A shop that sells food to visitors
A path that leads visitors to the exit
A building where tickets are sold
kahoot.explain: Enclosure — hayvonlar saqlanadigan o'ralgan joy (qo'ra).

kahoot.q: 'Please leave your valuables in a locker.' What are 'valuables'?
options: Things that are worth a lot of money
Things that you need for your lessons
Things that are too heavy to carry
Things that belong to the college
kahoot.explain: Valuables — qimmatbaho buyumlar (telefon, pul, taqinchoq).

kahoot.q: In 'Wear your badge while you are on the college premises', what does 'premises' mean?
kahoot.explain: Premises — bino va unga tegishli hudud.

kahoot.q: What does 'just beyond the bridge' mean?
options: A little further than the bridge
Just before you get to the bridge
On the top of the bridge itself
kahoot.explain: Just beyond — ...dan sal narida, undan o'tgach darrov.

kahoot.q: What is a 'common room' in a college?
options: A room where students can relax
A room where exams are usually held
A room where the head teacher works
A room where old books are stored
kahoot.explain: Common room — talabalar dam oladigan, suhbatlashadigan umumiy xona.

lessons.title: Reading: Pick from a List (Choose TWO)
lessons.grammar_topic: Pick from a list — ro'yxatdan ikki (yoki uch) javob tanlash
lessons.book_ref: Jony Academy materiali — ustoz matnlari (#21, #22) va mualliflik matnlari.
objectives: "Choose TWO letters" savolida ikkala javobni ham matndan isbotlash.
Savol qaysi mavzuni so'rayotganini aniqlab, matnning tegishli qismini tez topish.
Har bir variantni alohida tekshirish: matnda bormi? savolga javobmi? aynan shundaymi?
Tuzoqlarni ajratish: matnda bor, lekin boshqa narsa haqida; qisman to'g'ri; teskari.
5 ta matnda ishlash: ustozning 2 matni + 3 ta Jony Academy matni.
materials: Reading #21 "Humpback whale breaks migration record" matni va 1–14 savollari (7 juft "Choose TWO") — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa, javobsiz; javob kaliti va rad etish izohlari faqat ustozda qoladi.

Reading #22 "On the trail of the honey badger" matni 1–10 savollari (5 ta "Choose TWO" jufti) bilan, shuningdek "Why birds fly in a V" va "The dance of the honeybee" matnlari savollari bilan — har o'quvchiga bittadan nusxa (chop etiladi yoki ekranda).
Uyga beriladigan "How animals sleep" matni 1–6 savollari bilan — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa, javobsiz; dars oxirida tarqatiladi.

Doskada dars boshlanishidan oldin tayyor tursin: 4 ta belgi — "bor / savolga emas / teskari / aytilmagan" (butun dars davomida ishlatiladi) va sinf mashqining birinchi juftligi yonma-yon: gap "Adult crows often help each other to find food." — variant "Adult crows help their young to find food."; Humpback whale 9–10-savoli tahlili uchun doskaning o'ng chetida bo'sh joy qoldiring (u yerga tekshiruv paytida yoziladi: janub — hostile, hard to get to → shimol — friendlier, easier to reach).
Har o'quvchida "Tuzoq jadvali" uchun 4 ustunli sahifa (savol | rad etilgan variant | turi | sabab) — Humpback whale matnining 7 savoli uchun 7 qator; uyga vazifa ham shu jadvalda davom ettiriladi.

Taymer yoki sekundomer va 2 ta rangli marker: har "Choose TWO" juftiga 2–3 daqiqa, honey badger matni IELTS tezligida bajariladi; marker bilan variantdagi kalit so'z va matndagi paraphrase belgilanadi.
timeline: Salomlashish; 17-dars uyga vazifasi: "Getting around the town centre" javoblari (1 A, 2 D, 3 E) tez tekshiriladi; "O'z xaritangiz" — juftlikda sherik 5 gaplik yo'l matnini o'qiydi, ikkinchisi harflarni topadi (2 daqiqa), daftarlar yig'iladi. Map labelling bo'yicha 3 ta tezkor savol: 1) Xaritada birinchi nimani topasiz? (You are here / kirish.) 2) Xaritada pastga yurayotgan odamning "on your right" i qayerda? (Sizning chapingizda.) 3) Savolda yo'q joy tilga olinsa-chi? (Chegara, javob emas.)
Ustoz doskada: Choose TWO qoidasi (har harf 1 ball, tartib muhim emas, bo'sh qoldirmang), 6 bosqich, 4 belgi: bor / savolga emas / teskari / aytilmagan
"Bormi? Savolga javobmi?" (5 daqiqa, og'zaki); keyin Reading #21 "Humpback whale" tarqatiladi va 1–6 birga yechiladi: har variantga belgi qo'yiladi
O'quvchilar 7–14 ni mustaqil yechadi, har "Choose TWO" juftiga 2–3 daqiqa; har variant yoniga belgi
Javoblar why bilan tekshiriladi; 9–10 doskada tahlil (janub noqulay → shimol qulayroq); "Find the paraphrases"; Tuzoq jadvalining birinchi 2 qatori birga to'ldiriladi
1–10 (5 ta "Choose TWO" jufti) — 10 daqiqa vaqt bilan (IELTS tezligi), keyin tekshirish va "Tuzoq turlari"
"Why birds fly in a V" va "The dance of the honeybee" (har biri 1–6): har matnga 7 daqiqa, keyin tekshirish va honeybee "Tuzoq turlari"; vaqt yetmasa honeybee — zaxira (kuchli guruh yoki vaqt qolsa)

Kahoot (20 savol: Pick from a list qoidalari + hayvonlar lug'ati) ~10 daqiqa; qolgan 5 daqiqada xatolar daftari — har xato sababi bilan (savolga emas / teskari / aytilmagan / juftdan bitta harf yozilgan)
"How animals sleep" uyga tarqatiladi (12 daqiqa), Tuzoq jadvali va Paraphrase juftlari tushuntiriladi; xatolar daftari to'ldiriladi

intro: Pick from a list — savol va 5 ta variant (A–E) beriladi, ulardan IKKITASI to'g'ri; ko'rsatmada "Choose TWO letters, A–E" yoziladi. Ba'zan "Choose THREE letters" bo'ladi — unda variantlar odatda 7 ta (A–G).
Ikkala javob ham alohida ball oladi: 1–2-savol = 2 ball. Birini topsangiz ham 1 ball olasiz, shuning uchun bo'sh qoldirmang.
Javoblarni istalgan tartibda yozish mumkin: "B, C" yoki "C, B" — ikkalasi ham to'g'ri.
Bu savollar ko'pincha matnning BIR xatboshisiga tegishli. Savoldagi kalit so'zni (whale near Brazil, male badgers) matndan toping va o'sha qismni diqqat bilan o'qing.
Har variant uchun uchta savol: 1) matnda bormi? 2) savolda so'ralgan narsa haqidami? 3) aynan shundaymi yoki kuchliroq/teskari?

Asosiy tuzoq: variant matnda bor, lekin boshqa odam, boshqa vaqt yoki boshqa guruh haqida. Masalan: matnda "young seals play WITH EACH OTHER for hours" deyilsa, "young seals play with their mothers" varianti boshqa guruh haqida — bunday deyilmagan.
Variantlar matnda boshqa so'zlar bilan aytiladi: "keeps away from people" = "avoids humans"; "move in large groups" = "travel in herds".
presentation: Faqat bitta javobni aniq bilsam-chi?
Uni yozing va ikkinchisiga eng ehtimollisini tanlang — har biri alohida ball.
Javoblar tartibi muhimmi?
Yo'q. "B, C" va "C, B" bir xil.
Uchta variant to'g'ridek tuyulsa?
Uchinchisini qayta tekshiring: u savolga javobmi yoki matnda boshqa narsa haqida aytilganmi?
Variantdagi so'z matnda yo'q.
Paraphrase qidiring: "go without food" = "do not eat".
Savollar matn tartibidami?
Odatda ha, lekin bitta savol bir nechta xatboshini qamrashi mumkin.
Ikki javob qanday yoziladi?
Javob varag'ida ikki qator — har biriga bitta harf.
notes: Ustoz har variant uchun "bor / savolga emas / teskari / aytilmagan" belgisini qo'ydiradi — bu darsning asosiy ishi. "Savolga emas" ning ikki turi bor: boshqa guruh (boshqa odam, vaqt yoki guruh haqida) va boshqa narsa haqida — "Tuzoq turlari" mashqlari va uyga "Tuzoq jadvali" shu ikki nomni ishlatadi.
Humpback whale matnidagi 9–10-savolni doskada tahlil qiling: matn janub haqida gapiradi ("hostile", "hard to get to"), javob esa shimol haqida — teskari fikrlash kerak.
Honey badger matnida 5–6-savolning E varianti eng yaxshi tuzoq misoli (boshqa guruh).
mistakes: So'z bor, lekin boshqa narsa haqida
Guruhni aralashtirish (with each other ≠ with their mothers)
Teskari fikrlashni unutish (janub qiyin → shimol oson)

core: Some birds fly thousands of kilometres during their autumn migration.
Ba'zi qushlar kuzgi ko'chish paytida minglab kilometr uchadi.
This quiet bay is an important breeding ground for sea turtles.
Bu sokin ko'rfaz dengiz toshbaqalari uchun muhim ko'payish joyi.
The desert is a hostile environment for anyone without water.
Cho'l suvi yo'q har qanday odam uchun xavfli muhit.
Cutting down forests destroys the natural habitat of many animals.
O'rmonlarni kesish ko'plab hayvonlarning tabiiy yashash muhitini buzadi.
Thanks to satellite tracking, scientists can follow a turtle across the ocean.
Sun'iy yo'ldosh orqali kuzatish tufayli olimlar toshbaqani okean bo'ylab kuzatib bora oladi.
Young monkeys are curious and touch everything they find.
Yosh maymunlar qiziquvchan bo'ladi va topgan hamma narsasini ushlab ko'radi.
Wild animals can be unpredictable, so never feed them by hand.
Yovvoyi hayvonlar nima qilishini oldindan bilib bo'lmaydi, shuning uchun ularni hech qachon qo'lda boqmang.
The guide was reluctant to take us close to the bears.
Gid bizni ayiqlarga yaqin olib borishni istamadi.
A male tiger marks its territory to keep other tigers away.
Erkak yo'lbars boshqa yo'lbarslarni uzoqlashtirish uchun o'z hududini belgilaydi.
Some dogs become aggressive when a stranger comes near their food.
Ba'zi itlar begona odam ovqatiga yaqinlashsa, tajovuzkor bo'lib qoladi.
After a few days, the birds became accustomed to the cameras.
Bir necha kundan keyin qushlar kameralarga ko'nikib qoldi.
Zebras live in large groups to protect themselves from predators.
Zebralar yirtqichlardan himoyalanish uchun katta to'dalarda yashaydi.
Meerkats take turns to stay alert while the rest of the group eats.
Surikatlar navbatma-navbat hushyor turadi, qolgan to'da esa ovqatlanadi.
The geese flew south in a perfect V formation.
G'ozlar janubga mukammal V shaklidagi safda uchib ketdi.
Bats use sound to avoid collisions in the dark.
Ko'rshapalaklar qorong'ida to'qnashib ketmaslik uchun tovushdan foydalanadi.

class_ex.title: Bormi? Savolga javobmi?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz bir gap va bir variant o'qiydi; o'quvchi doskadagi 4 belgidan birini aytadi: bor / savolga emas / teskari / aytilmagan.
items: Gap: "Adult crows often help each other to find food." Variant: Adult crows help their young to find food.
Gap: "Wolves are usually shy around people." Variant: Wolves like to come close to humans.
Gap: "The team fixed small cameras to the turtles' shells." Variant: The researchers attached cameras to the animals.
Gap: "The team fixed small cameras to the turtles' shells." Variant: The cameras stayed on the turtles for a whole year.
Gap: "Sharks seldom attack swimmers in these waters." Variant: Shark attacks on swimmers are common here.
why: Gap kattalarning O'ZARO yordami haqida (each other); bolalariga yordam berishi aytilmagan — variant boshqa guruh haqida.

readings.title: Reading #21. Humpback whale breaks migration record
text: A whale surprises researchers with her journey.
A lone humpback whale travelled more than 9,800 kilometres from breeding areas in Brazil to those in Madagascar, setting a record for the longest mammal migration ever documented.

Humpback whales (Megaptera novaeangliae) are known to have some of the longest migration distances of all mammals, and this huge journey is about 400 kilometres _farther_ than the previous humpback record. The finding was made by Peter Stevick, a biologist at the College of the Atlantic in Bar Harbor, Maine.

The whale's journey was unusual not only for its _length_, but also because it travelled across almost 90 degrees of longitude _from west to east_. Typically, humpbacks move in a north-south direction between _cold feeding areas_ and _warm breeding grounds_ - and the longest journeys which have been recorded until now have been between breeding and feeding sites.

The whale, a female, was first spotted off the coast of Brazil, where researchers _photographed_ its tail fluke and _took skin samples_ for chromosome testing to determine the animal's sex. Two years later, a tourist on a whale-watching boat snapped a photo of the humpback near Madagascar.

To match the two sightings, Stevick's team used an extensive international catalogue of photographs of the undersides of tail flukes, which have distinctive markings. Researchers routinely _compare the markings_ in each new photograph to those in the archive.

The scientists then estimated the animal's shortest possible route: an arc _skirting the southern tip of South Africa_ and heading north-east towards Madagascar. The minimum distance is 9,800 kilometres, says Stevick, but this is likely to be an underestimate, because the whale probably took a detour to feed on krill in the Southern Ocean _near Antarctica_ before reaching its destination.

Most humpback-whale researchers focus their efforts on the Northern Hemisphere because the Southern Ocean near the Antarctic is _a hostile environment_ and it is _hard to get to_, explains Rochelle Constantine, who studies the ecology of humpback whales at the University of Auckland in New Zealand. But, for whales, oceans in the Southern Hemisphere are wider and easier to travel across, says Constantine. Scientists will probably observe more long-distance migrations in the Southern Hemisphere as _satellite tracking_ becomes increasingly common, she adds.

Daniel Palacios, an oceanographer at the University of Hawaii at Manoa, says that the record-breaking journey could indicate that migration patterns are shifting as populations begin to recover from near-extinction and the population increases. But the reasons why the whale did not follow the usual migration routes remain a mystery. She could have been _exploring new habitats_, or simply have _lost her way_. 'We generally think of humpback whales as very well studied, but then they surprise us with things like this,' Palacios says. 'Undoubtedly there are a lot of things we still don't know about whale migration.'

readings.title: Reading #22. On the trail of the honey badger
readings.qtype: Pick from a list (1–10) — qo'shimcha mashq
text: Researchers learn more about this fearless African predator

On a recent field trip to the Kalahari Desert, a team of researchers learnt a lot more about honey badgers. They were rewarded with a detailed insight into how these fascinating creatures live and hunt.

The team employed a local wildlife expert, Kitso Khama, to help them locate and follow the badgers across the desert. Their main aim was _to study the badgers' movements and behaviour_ as discreetly as possible, without frightening them away or causing them to change their natural behaviour. They also planned _to trap a few and study them close up before releasing them_. In view of the animal's reputation, this was something that even Khama was reluctant to do.

'The problem with honey badgers is they are naturally _curious_ animals, especially when they see _something new_,' he says. 'That, combined with their _unpredictable_ nature, can be a dangerous mixture. If they sense you have food, for example, they won't be shy about coming right up to you for something to eat. They're actually quite sociable creatures around humans, but as soon as they feel they might be in danger, they can become extremely vicious. Fortunately this is _rare_, but it does happen.'

The research confirmed many things that were already known. As expected, honey badgers ate any creatures they could catch and kill. Even poisonous snakes, feared and avoided by most other animals, were not safe from them. The researchers were surprised, however, by the animal's fondness for local _melons_, probably because of their _high water content_. Previously researchers thought that the animal got all of its liquid requirements from its prey. The team also learnt that, contrary to previous research findings, the badgers occasionally formed _loose family groups_. They were also able to confirm certain results from previous research, including the fact that female badgers never socialised _with each other_.

Following some of the male badgers was a challenge, since they can cover large distances in a short space of time. Some hunting territories cover _more than 500 square kilometres_. Although they seem happy to share these territories with other males, there are _occasional fights_ over an important food source, and male badgers can be as aggressive towards each other as they are towards other species.

As the badgers became accustomed to the presence of people, it gave the team the chance to get up close to them _without being the subject of the animals' curiosity_ - or their sudden aggression. The badgers' eating patterns, which had been disrupted, returned to normal. It also allowed the team to observe more closely some of the other creatures that form working associations with the honey badger, as these seemed to _adopt the badgers' relaxed attitude_ when near humans.

readings.title: Why birds fly in a V
text: Anyone who has watched geese crossing an autumn sky has noticed their V-shaped formation. For a long time, scientists suspected that the shape helped birds save energy, but it was very difficult to prove, because it is hard to measure what a bird is doing in the air.

In 2014, a team from the Royal Veterinary College in London found a solution. They attached tiny data recorders to a group of northern bald ibises, rare birds that had been trained to follow a light aircraft on their migration. The recorders measured the position of each bird and every beat of its wings.

The results were surprising. Each bird flew in exactly the place where the air pushed up by the wings of the bird in front could help lift it. The birds also timed their wing beats to match the bird ahead, so that they always met rising air rather than falling air. Earlier research on pelicans had shown that birds flying in formation have lower heart rates than those flying alone.

Flying at the front is the hardest job, and no single bird does it all the time. The ibises regularly changed places, and each bird spent roughly as long leading as it did following — a kind of fair sharing that researchers had not expected.

Energy is not the only reason for the shape. A V also allows every bird to see the others clearly, which helps the group stay together and avoid collisions. Young birds on their first migration can follow experienced adults who know the route.

readings.title: The dance of the honeybee
text: When a honeybee discovers a good source of food, it returns to the hive and performs a dance. For centuries, beekeepers noticed this strange movement, but it was the Austrian scientist Karl von Frisch who first explained what it meant. His work on bee communication won him a share of the Nobel Prize in 1973.

Von Frisch found that bees use two main dances. If the flowers are close to the hive, a bee performs a "round dance", running in small circles. This tells the other bees that food is nearby, but not the exact direction. For food further away, the bee performs a "waggle dance": it runs forward in a straight line while shaking its body from side to side, then circles back and repeats the movement.

The waggle dance contains surprisingly precise information. The angle of the straight run compared with a vertical line on the honeycomb shows the direction of the food compared with the position of the sun. The length of time the bee spends waggling shows how far away the food is: the longer the waggle, the greater the distance.

The dancer also shares other clues. Other bees touch it with their antennae and learn the smell of the flowers it has visited, and they may taste samples of nectar it brings back. Because the sun moves across the sky during the day, bees also adjust the angle of their dance as time passes.
Not every scientist accepted von Frisch's ideas at first. Some believed that bees found food only by smell, and it took several decades of experiments before the dance language was widely accepted.
