readings.title: The long story of the umbrella
text: A. The first umbrellas were not made to keep people dry. Four thousand years ago, in Egypt, China and Assyria, they were used as protection from the sun, and only kings, nobles and priests were allowed to stand under them. The word "umbrella" itself comes from the Latin word umbra, meaning shade.

B. It was the Chinese who first made umbrellas waterproof, covering paper shades with wax and oil. From China the idea spread slowly westwards, but for centuries in Europe umbrellas were seen as objects for women only. A man carrying one risked being laughed at in the street.

C. That changed in London in the 1750s thanks to a traveller called Jonas Hanway. Having seen umbrellas used in Persia, he carried one through the rainy streets of London for about thirty years. At first people shouted at him, and coach drivers, who earned money from people escaping the rain, even tried to run him down. By the time he died, however, the umbrella had become an ordinary item for men as well.

D. Early European umbrellas were heavy, with frames made of wood or whalebone, and they became difficult to open when wet. In 1852, Samuel Fox, an Englishman, designed a frame with light steel ribs. His design was so successful that the basic shape of the umbrella has hardly changed since then.

E. Today, around a billion umbrellas are sold around the world every year, and most of them are cheap enough to be lost without much worry. Lost-property offices in large cities report that umbrellas are the item most often left behind on buses and trains.

readings.title: Why we forget
text: A. In 1885, the German psychologist Hermann Ebbinghaus published one of the first scientific studies of memory. Using himself as the only subject, he learnt long lists of nonsense syllables such as "WID" and "ZOF", and then tested how many he could remember after different periods of time.

B. His results produced what is now called the "forgetting curve". Most forgetting happened very quickly: within an hour he had lost more than half of a new list, and after a day around two thirds. After that, the rate of forgetting slowed down, and what remained was kept for a long time.

C. Ebbinghaus also discovered a way to fight the curve. Each time he reviewed a list, he forgot it more slowly than before. Reviewing at increasing intervals — after one day, then three days, then a week — was far more effective than studying the same list many times in one evening. Today this method, known as spaced repetition, is used by many language-learning apps.

D. Later researchers found that forgetting is not always a failure. The brain receives far more information than it can store, and forgetting unimportant details makes it easier to find the information that matters. People who remember everything, a rare condition, often say that their memories make it hard to think clearly.

E. Sleep also plays a part. Studies show that people who sleep after learning remember more than those who stay awake for the same period, because the brain seems to strengthen new memories during the night. For students, this means that staying up all night before an exam may be the worst possible strategy.

readings.title: How the bicycle was invented
text: A. The first machine that looked like a bicycle was built in 1817 by Karl Drais, a German inventor. It had two wheels and a seat, but no pedals: riders sat on it and pushed themselves along the ground with their feet. Drais hoped it would replace horses, which were expensive to feed after a series of poor harvests.

B. Pedals arrived in the 1860s in France, where they were attached directly to the front wheel. These machines, called velocipedes, were faster, but they had iron wheels and wooden frames, and riding one on the stony roads of the time was so uncomfortable that the English nicknamed them "boneshakers".

C. To go faster, makers of the 1870s simply made the front wheel bigger, sometimes up to one and a half metres high. This design, later known as the "penny-farthing", was popular with young men, but it was dangerous: a small stone could throw the rider over the handlebars, head first.

D. The solution came in 1885, when John Kemp Starley in England built the "safety bicycle". Its two wheels were the same size, and a chain connected the pedals to the back wheel. Three years later, John Dunlop added air-filled rubber tyres, and cycling suddenly became comfortable.

E. The safety bicycle changed society. It was cheap enough for working people, and it gave women a new freedom to travel alone. The American campaigner Susan B. Anthony said in 1896 that the bicycle had done more to free women than anything else in the world.

kahoot.q: What does 'NB You may use any letter more than once' mean?
options: One paragraph can answer two questions

kahoot.q: Matching information questions usually ask you to find…
options: the main idea of a paragraph
kahoot.explain: Information — xatboshi ichidagi bitta detal (raqam, sabab, misol); asosiy g'oya esa headings savolida so'raladi.

kahoot.q: A question begins 'a definition of…'. Which sentence should you look for?
options: One that explains what a term means
One that gives an exact date or number
kahoot.explain: "A definition" — ta'rif, ya'ni "X is … / X means …" shaklidagi gap qidiriladi.

kahoot.q: A question asks for 'the reason why…'. Which words often signal the answer?
kahoot.explain: Sabab so'ralganda because, since, due to, as a result of kabi bog'lovchilar atrofini o'qing.

kahoot.q: When is it usually best to answer the matching information questions?
options: After the other questions on the passage
Before you read the instructions or the questions
Only if there is time at the end
Before you look at the passage
kahoot.explain: Boshqa savollardan keyin ishlasangiz, matn allaqachon tanish bo'ladi va detalni tezroq topasiz.

kahoot.q: Question: 'an example of a successful study method'. Which sentence answers it?
options: Students who test themselves remember more.
Many students say that studying is boring.
Study methods have changed over the years.
Some students prefer to study late at night.
kahoot.explain: O'zini test qilish — natija beradigan usulning misoli; qolgan gaplarda "study" so'zi bor, lekin muvaffaqiyatli usul yo'q.

kahoot.q: Text: 'Unless children read for pleasure, their vocabulary grows slowly.' What type of information is this?
options: a definition of a technical term
kahoot.explain: "Unless" — shart (agar … bo'lmasa), "grows slowly" — natija.

kahoot.q: A key word from the question appears in three paragraphs. What should you do?
options: Check which one has the right type of information
Choose the first paragraph where the word appears
Choose the paragraph that repeats the word most often
Skip the question and never come back to it
kahoot.explain: So'z mosligi — tuzoq: savol so'rayotgan ma'lumot TURI (sabab, raqam, misol) qaysi xatboshida borligini tekshiring.

kahoot.q: Why is it useful to write a 3–4 word note next to each paragraph?
options: It helps you find information faster
It helps you count the words
It lets you copy answers quickly
It shows the teacher that you have read it
kahoot.explain: Qisqa izohlar matn xaritasi bo'ladi — tartibsiz savollarda kerakli xatboshini tez topasiz.

kahoot.q: There are eight paragraphs (A–H) but only six questions. What is true?
options: Some paragraphs will not be used
Every paragraph must be used once
Two questions must share a letter
The last paragraph is never an answer
kahoot.explain: Xatboshilar savollardan ko'p bo'lsa, ba'zilari javob bo'lmaydi — bu normal holat.

kahoot.q: A table says 'NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS'. Which answer breaks the rule?
kahoot.explain: "the public library" — 3 so'z, chunki artikl ham so'z hisoblanadi.

kahoot.q: To 'skim' a text means to…
options: read it quickly for the main idea
read every single word slowly and carefully
learn the whole text by heart
kahoot.explain: Skim — asosiy g'oyani bilish uchun matnga tez ko'z yugurtirib o'qish.

kahoot.q: Which phrase is closest in meaning to 'irrelevant'?
kahoot.explain: Irrelevant — mavzuga aloqasi yo'q, keraksiz (ir- — inkor old qo'shimchasi + relevant).

kahoot.q: Complete: 'Try to ___ the key facts from a long report.'
kahoot.explain: Extract the key facts from — kerakli faktlarni ajratib olmoq.

kahoot.q: 'Comprehend' is closest in meaning to…
kahoot.explain: Comprehend — tushunmoq, anglab yetmoq (comprehension — tushunish).

kahoot.q: Complete: 'Only the top ten runners will ___ for the final.'
kahoot.explain: Qualify for — saralashdan o'tib, keyingi bosqichga huquq qozonmoq.

kahoot.q: What does 'literacy' mean?
options: the ability to read and write
the number of books you own
kahoot.explain: Literacy — savodxonlik, ya'ni o'qish va yozish qobiliyati.

kahoot.q: Which is the correct plural of 'phenomenon'?
kahoot.explain: Phenomenon (birlik) — phenomena (ko'plik), yunoncha so'z.

kahoot.q: If a teacher 'motivates' her students, she…
options: makes them want to work harder
gives them lower marks than before
kahoot.explain: Motivate — rag'batlantirmoq, ishlashga ishtiyoq uyg'otmoq.

intro: Matching people (matching features) — ro'yxatda odamlar (A–D) beriladi, har gap (statement) ulardan biri aytgan fikrga mos keladi.
Savollar matn tartibida KELMAYDI (NEVER guruhi). Lekin odamlar matnda odatda bir-bir marta chiqadi, shuning uchun ismlar joyini oldindan belgilab olish vaqtni tejaydi.

Tuzoq: bir odamning gapi ichida boshqa odam haqida gap bo'lishi mumkin. Jorgensen gapida Hillary Clinton tilga olinadi, lekin fikr — Jorgensenniki.

readings.title: Reading #29. Here today, gone tomorrow
text: The Arctic and Antarctica are now within reach of the modern tourist, with many going to see these icy wildernesses before it's too late. Christian Amodeo reports on the growth of polar tourism.

Travel at the North and South Poles has become an expensive leisure activity, suitable for tourists of all ages. The poles may be inhospitable places, but they are seeing increasing numbers of visitors.

Annual figures for the Arctic, where tourism has existed _since the 19th century_, have increased from about a million in the early 1990s to _more than 1.5 million_ today. This is partly because of the _lengthening summer season_ brought about by climate change.

Most visitors arrive by ship. In 2007, 370,000 cruise passengers visited Norway, twice the number that arrived in 2000. Iceland, a country where tourism is the second-largest industry, has enjoyed an annual growth rate of nine percent since 1990. Meanwhile, Alaska received some 1,029,800 passengers, a rise of 7.3 percent from 2006. _Greenland has seen the most rapid growth_ in marine tourism, with a sharp increase in cruise-ship arrivals of 250 percent since 2004.

The global economic downturn may have affected the annual 20.6 percent rate of increase in visitors to the Antarctic - last season saw _a drop of 17 percent_ to 38,200 - but there has been a 760 percent rise in land-based tourism there since 1997. More people than ever are landing at fragile sites, with _light aircraft, helicopters_ and all-terrain vehicles increasingly used for greater access, while in the past two seasons, 'fly-sail' operations have begun. These deliver tourists by air to ships, so far more groups can enjoy a cruise in a season; large cruise ships capable of carrying _up to 800 passengers_ are not uncommon.

In addition, it seems that a high number of visitors return to the poles. 'Looking at six years' worth of data, of the people who have been to the polar regions, _roughly 25 percent go for a second time_,' says Louisa Richardson, a senior marketing executive at tour operator Exodus.

In the same period that tourism has exploded, the 'health' of the poles has 'deteriorated'. 'The biggest changes taking place in the Antarctic are related to climate change,' says Rod Downie, Environmental Manager with the British Antarctic Survey (BAS). Large numbers of visitors increase these problems.

Although polar tourism is widely accepted, there have been few regulations up until recently. At the meeting of the Antarctic Treaty in Baltimore, the 28 member-nations adopted proposals for limits to tourist numbers. These included safety codes for tourist vessels in Antarctic waters, and improved environmental protection for the continent. They agreed to prevent ships with more than 500 passengers from landing in Antarctica, as well as limit the number of passengers going ashore to a maximum of 100 at any one time, with a minimum of one guide for every 20 tourists. _'Tourism in Antarctica is not without its risks,'_ says Downie. 'After all, Antarctica doesn't have a coastguard rescue service.'

_'So far, no surveys confirm that people are going quickly to see polar regions before they change,'_ says Frigg Jorgensen, General Secretary of the Association of Arctic Expedition Cruise Operators (AECO). 'However, _Hillary Clinton and many other big names have been to Svalbard_ in the northernmost part of Norway _to see the effects of climate change_. The associated media coverage could influence others to do the same.'

These days, rarely a week passes without a negative headline in the newspapers. The suffering polar bear has become a symbol of a warming world, its plight a warning that the clock is ticking. It would seem that this ticking clock is a small but growing factor for some tourists. _'There's an element of "do it now",'_ acknowledges Prisca Campbell, Marketing director of Quark Expeditions, which takes 7,000 people to the poles annually. Leaving the trip until later, it seems, may mean leaving it too late.

readings.title: Reading #30. Holidays with a difference
readings.qtype: Summary completion (1–8) + Matching people (9–13) — qo'shimcha mashq
text: Tribal tourism is becoming more popular. But at what cost to the locals?

Tribal tourism is a relatively new type of tourism. It involves travellers going to _remote destinations_, staying with local people and _learning about their culture and way of life_. They stay in local accommodation, share facilities with local people, and join in with meals and celebrations. At the moment, _less than one percent_ of holidays are tribal tourism holidays, but this is set to change.

Tribal tourism is often compared with foreign exchange visits. However, a foreign exchange involves staying with people who often _share the same values_. Tribal tourism takes visitors to places where the _lifestyle_ is very different from that in their home location. Those who have been on a tribal holiday explain that experiencing this lifestyle is _the main attraction_. They say that it offers them the chance to live in a way they never have before.

Not everyone is convinced that tribal tourism is a good thing, and opinions are divided. The argument is about whether or not it helps _the local population_, or whether it exploits them. The main problem is that, because tribal tourism is relatively new, the long-term effects on local populations have not been studied in much detail. _Where studies have been carried out, the effects have been found to be negative._

Travel writer Ian Coleman recalls a recent trip to Guatemala, where he saw an example of this. 'There is a village with a statue of a man called Maximon, who has a special spiritual meaning for the local tribe,' he explains. 'The statue is kept indoors, and once a year the locals bring him out and carry him around the village. However, _visitors now pay money for them to bring the statue out_ and carry it around, while they take photographs. As a result, Maximon has lost his original meaning, and is now just another tourist attraction.'

So, is it possible to experience an exotic culture without harming it in some way? 'With a bit of thought, we can maximise the positive impacts and minimise the negative,' says travel company director Hilary Waterhouse. 'Remember that you are there not only to experience a different culture, but to help it in some way. _Tourists bring money to the community, which the community can invest in local projects._ However, _this does not mean you can act the way you might do back home._ The most important thing is to show respect, learn about, and be aware of, local customs and traditions. Always remember you're a guest.'

Dawn Baker, manager of travel company Footprints, runs tours to tribal areas in Peru. 'Good companies specialising in tribal tours are very careful about who they allow on their tours,' she says. 'They won't take anyone they feel is unsuitable.' Baker offers reading recommendations so that visitors can read about the country and its cultures. _'The rewards of a trip to this country are priceless, and the more you know in advance, the more priceless they are.'_

Tribal tourism travellers are often surprised at how basic their facilities are when they get there. _'It's not for everyone,_ but for me it was all part of the experience,' says Jamie White, who has recently returned from a trip to Borneo. 'We stayed in the same huts that everyone was living in, with no running water and no electricity. It was basic, but it was an ethical way to travel. Being comfortable means you use more local resources and so have more of an environmental impact.'
paraphrases: whether or not it helps / exploits
where studies have been carried out
not act the way you might do back home
bring money ... invest in local projects
visitors pay money for them to bring the statue out
the more you know in advance

readings.title: Working from home: four views
text: Since 2020, millions of office workers around the world have spent at least part of the week working from home. Four people who have tried it describe their experience.

Aziza, a graphic designer, says she will never go back to full-time office work. "I used to spend nearly two hours a day travelling. Now I use that time to exercise and cook proper meals. My work hasn't suffered either — I finish projects faster because nobody interrupts me."

Tom, who manages a sales team of twelve, has mixed feelings. "My team is just as productive at home, and the numbers prove it. But I've noticed that new staff learn much more slowly. In the office, they could hear how experienced colleagues spoke to customers. At home, they only learn what we remember to tell them."

Dilnoza, a researcher, found the first months difficult. "My flat is small, and I was working at the kitchen table. By evening I couldn't separate work from rest. What helped was a simple rule: at six o'clock I close the laptop and put it in a cupboard, so I can't see it."

Mark, a secondary school teacher, taught online for a year. "Some quiet students actually participated more, because they could type questions in the chat instead of speaking in front of the class. But the practical subjects were almost impossible. You can't do a science experiment through a screen."
paraphrases: keep work and free time apart

readings.title: Should children get homework?
text: Few school topics cause as much argument between parents and teachers as homework. We asked four people with different experiences for their opinions.

Gulnora has taught mathematics for twenty years. "I give short tasks, never more than twenty minutes. Maths is like sport: if you only practise in the lesson, you forget the technique by the next week. What I don't do is give homework on something we haven't covered in class — that only makes children feel stupid."

James is the father of three primary-school children. "In our house, homework often ends in tears, and usually mine. I think younger children learn more by playing outside or helping to cook dinner than by filling in worksheets. Secondary school is different; by then, homework prepares them for exams."

Professor Rana Malik studies education. "The research is clearer than people think. For teenagers, a moderate amount of homework is linked to better results. For children under about eleven, the effect is very small. The problem is that schools often give the same amount to every age."

Otabek, aged sixteen, has his final exams next year. "Homework itself isn't the problem. The problem is when five teachers all give a big task on the same night. If teachers talked to each other and planned it together, we could do all of it properly."
paraphrases: helps them get ready for tests
not too much and not too little

why: "For teenagers ... linked to better results. For children under about eleven, the effect is very small". B tuzoq: James ham yosh bolalar haqida gapiradi, lekin tadqiqotga emas, o'z oilasiga tayanadi.

readings.title: Living in a big city
text: More than half of the world's population now lives in cities, and the number is still rising. Four people who moved to a large city in the last few years talk about what surprised them.

Bekzod moved to the capital from a small town to study. "What surprised me most was how lonely you can feel with millions of people around you. At home everybody knew me. Here I can go a whole week without a proper conversation, unless I make the effort to join a club."

Sofia, a nurse, came for a better salary. "The salary is higher, yes, but half of it goes on rent. I share a flat with two other nurses. On the other hand, I've learnt more in two years at a big hospital than I would have learnt in ten years back home."

Rustam runs a small café. "The competition is enormous — there are five cafés on my street alone. But there are also far more customers, and people here are willing to try new things. My most popular dish is one I would never have dared to sell in my home town."

Laura, a retired teacher, moved to be near her grandchildren. "People think big cities are for the young, but I have never been busier. There are free concerts, lectures and museums. The only thing I really miss is silence. It is never completely quiet here, even at three in the morning."
paraphrases: feel sad because something is not there

homework_intro: Bugun darsda matching people savollarini ismlar xaritasi bilan yechdik; uyda xuddi shu usulni endi yolg'iz o'zingiz qo'llab ko'rasiz.
Uchta ish bor: "Living in a big city" matnidan 1–6 savollar, "Holidays with a difference" uchun ismlar xaritasi va Polar tourism summarysidagi 7 ta paraphrase juftligi.

Avval "Living in a big city"ni soatga qarab 10 daqiqada bajaring — to'rt ismni doira ichiga olib, har biri yoniga 2–3 so'z yozgandan keyingina savollarni o'qing; ismlar xaritasi bilan summary daftari yana 15–20 daqiqa oladi.

Eng ko'p xato shu yerda bo'ladi: harf takrorlanmaydi deb o'ylash. "Living in a big city"da NB bor — ikki odam ikki martadan javob bo'ladi, shuning uchun birinchi topgan harfingizni "band" deb hisoblamang.

Uchala ishni ham bitta daftarga yozing va keyingi dars boshida topshiring; har javob yoniga o'sha odam aytgan inglizcha gapni ham ko'chiring, chunki men "buni kim aytgan?" deb so'rayman — isbotsiz javob hisobga olinmaydi.

objectives: Part 3 formatiga ko'nikish: talaba va o'qituvchi (tutor) akademik ish haqida gaplashadi.
Matchingda bir harfni bir necha marta ishlatish (NB You may use any letter more than once) va o'qituvchining FIKRINI ajratish.
Flow chart (jarayon sxemasi) bosqichlarini tartib bilan kuzatish: collection → treatment → removal → result → use.
Talaba fikri va o'qituvchi fikrini farqlash: savol "What comment does the TUTOR make..." bo'lsa, faqat o'qituvchi gapi hisoblanadi.
Sinfda 4 ta audio (Fahad: CD2 Track 21–22; Jo: essay va cloud seeding) va 2 ta Jony skripti bilan ishlash; 3-skript (solar energy) — uyga.
materials: Audio: ielts5_27_presentation.mp3 (CD2 Track 21), ielts5_27_desalination.mp3 (CD2 Track 22), ielts5_27_essay.mp3 (Jo — essay, boshqa diskdagi Track 20) va ielts5_27_cloud_seeding.mp3 (Jo — cloud seeding, boshqa diskdagi Track 21; CD2 Track 21 bilan adashtirmang) — dars boshlanishidan oldin telefon yoki kolonkaga yuklab, orqa partadan eshitiladigan qilib sinab qo'ying; har biri faqat BIR MARTA qo'yiladi.

Savol varaqasi: 1-varaq — Fahad taqdimoti 1–5 matching (A It needs to be shorter; B The ideas are difficult to follow; C Some information should be added) va desalination 6–10 flow charti strelkalari bilan; 2-varaq — Jo inshosi 1–5 matching (A not well organised; B may not be correct; C not relevant) va cloud seeding 6–10 flow charti. Har o'quvchiga bittadan, 1-varaq audio qo'yilishidan OLDIN, 2-varaq qo'shimcha mashq bosqichida tarqatiladi.

3 ta Jony Academy skripti ("Research project — tutor feedback", "How recycled paper is made", "Group presentation on solar energy") — bularning audiosi yo'q, ustoz ovoz chiqarib o'qiydi: skriptni chop etib DR GRANT/LOLA, JAMSHID/TUTOR va ANNA/RUSTAM repliklarini ikki xil belgilab chiqing; uchinchisi uyga vazifa varaqasi sifatida dars oxirida tarqatiladi.

[class] "Kimning fikri?" uchun sinf mashqidagi 5 ta gap (audiodan olinmagan) alohida qog'ozchalarga yozib, kesib qo'yiladi (o'quvchi kartochkani tortib oladi, "talaba" yoki "o'qituvchi" deydi va A/B/C harfini qo'yadi).

Doskada qo'ng'iroqqacha: ikki ustun TALABA | O'QITUVCHI; yonida yirik harflar bilan "NB You may use any letter more than once" va "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS"; pastda zanjir: collection → treatment → salt removal → result → use.

Fahad audiolari (CD2 Track 21 va 22) transkript nusxalari — har juftlikka bitta, faqat tekshirish bosqichida tarqatiladi; o'quvchilarda xatolar daftari va ikki rangli qalam bo'lsin (o'qituvchi gapi bir rang, talaba gapi boshqa rang).
timeline: Salomlashish, o'tgan darsdagi savol turini 3 savolda eslatish
Ustoz doskada: qoida, bosqichlar, tipik xatolar
Savol turiga oid mashq birga bajariladi, har javob izohlanadi

Paraphrase va so'z chegarasi: sinf mashqi va grammar dagi audiodan olinmagan misollar ("hard to follow" = difficult to follow; "bad news for the birds" → can harm; rainwater = 1 so'z) va Kahoot'dagi skill savollari; audiolardagi paraphrase jadvallari javob joyini ochadi — ularni faqat tinglashdan KEYIN ishlating

"Research project" (Lola, 1–4 matching) va "How recycled paper is made" (Jamshid, 1–5 flow chart) — ustoz ikki ovozda o'qiydi, keyin javoblar tekshiriladi

intro: Part 3 — 2–3 kishining akademik suhbati: talaba loyihasi, taqdimot, tadqiqot. Til 1–2 sectionlardan qiyinroq, fikrlar tez almashadi.

Matching (Fahad, CD2 Track 21): taqdimotning 5 qismi va 3 ta izoh (A shorter, B difficult to follow, C information should be added). Harflar TAKRORLANADI — "NB You may use any letter more than once". Shuning uchun "bu harf ishlatildi" deb o'chirmang.

Kimning fikri? Talaba o'z fikrini aytadi ("I was planning to use lots of photos"), lekin savol o'qituvchi izohini so'raydi ("Good, but you need to say where they come from" → C: information should be added). Talaba taklifi ko'pincha chalg'ituvchi.
Flow chart (Fahad, CD2 Track 22): jarayon bosqichlari strelka bilan ketma-ket. Audio ham shu tartibda boradi. Har bosqich nomi (Collection, Treatment, Salt removal) — langar.

Flow chartda javob ko'pincha bosqich haqidagi eng muhim detal: "Sorting: a very ___ stage" → slow ("Collecting the paper is hard work, but sorting it is really slow"). Bo'sh joy qaysi bosqichni tasvirlashini tekshiring: "hard" — boshqa bosqich (collecting) haqida.
So'z chegarasi: "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS" — "rainwater" (qo'shma so'z — bitta so'z) va "storage tank" (ikki so'z) mos keladi; "the big storage tank" (to'rt so'z) — chegaradan oshadi.
presentation: Bitta harfni ikki marta yozsam bo'ladimi?
Ha, agar "NB You may use any letter more than once" yozilgan bo'lsa. 5 savol va 3 harf bo'lsa, kamida bitta harf albatta takrorlanadi.
Talaba bir narsa dedi, o'qituvchi boshqasini.
Savolga qarang: "What comment does the TUTOR make" — o'qituvchi gapi.
Flow chart bosqichini yo'qotdim.
Keyingi bosqich nomini kuting (Treatment, Salt removal) — u sizni qaytaradi.
"Rain water" yoki "rainwater"?
Odatda ikkalasi ham qabul qilinadi (kalitda "rainwater / rain water" kabi beriladi). Muhimi — imlo to'g'ri bo'lsin.
Part 3 nima uchun qiyin?
Ikki kishi, akademik so'zlar, fikr tez o'zgaradi. Kim gapirayotganini kuzating.
Javob audioda aynan aytilmadi.
Paraphrase: "It's bad news for the birds that nest there" → "can harm birds". Flow chartdagi so'z audioda ko'pincha sinonim bilan keladi.
notes: CD2 Track 21 va 22 — bitta talaba (Fahad) va o'qituvchi (Dr Tyler) suhbati: avval taqdimotning umumiy tuzilishi, keyin jarayon qismi. O'quvchilar ikkinchisida suhbatni taniydi. Jo audiolari (Track 20 va 21) boshqa diskdan — fayl nomi bo'yicha qo'ying.

Kalit (Fahad, CD2 Track 21–22): 1 C · 2 B · 3 A · 4 B · 5 C; 6 seabird / sea(-)bird · 7 plant · 8 expensive · 9 fish / marine life · 10 farmland / farm(-)land. Kalitni o'quvchilarga faqat tinglashdan KEYIN ko'rsating.
Fahad audiosi (CD2 Track 22) transkripti oxirigacha berilgan: 9–10-javoblar suhbatning oxirgi qismida keladi, shuning uchun audioni oxirigacha qo'ying.
Har matching javobidan keyin so'rang: "talaba nima dedi? o'qituvchi nima dedi? savol kimni so'raydi?"
mistakes: Bo'sh joy aynan qaysi bosqichni tasvirlashini tekshirish
"Sorting: a very ___ stage": "collecting is hard work, but sorting is really slow" → slow

how: CORE — shu darsdagi audio va skriptlardan olingan 14 ta so'z va ibora. Ularni tinglashdan KEYIN ko'rib chiqing: har o'quvchi o'z taqdimoti yoki loyihasi haqida 2 ta so'z bilan gap tuzadi.
core: Send me a rough outline of your talk before Friday.
Juma kunigacha menga ma'ruzangizning taxminiy rejasini yuboring.
Let's go over your notes before you write the final version.
Yakuniy variantni yozishdan oldin qaydlaringizni birga ko'rib chiqaylik.
Only include examples that are relevant to the topic.
Your ideas are good, but you need to reorganise them into a clearer order.
Fikrlaringiz yaxshi, lekin ularni aniqroq tartibda qayta joylashtirishingiz kerak.
The talk was too technical for a general audience.
Ma'ruza oddiy tinglovchilar uchun juda texnik edi.
I need to sort out my notes before the exam.
Imtihondan oldin qaydlarimni tartibga keltirishim kerak.
We discussed the pros and cons of building a new water plant.
Yangi suv zavodini qurishning afzallik va kamchiliklarini muhokama qildik.
At the end, summarise your three main points in one minute.
Oxirida uchta asosiy fikringizni bir daqiqada qisqacha xulosalang.
Homework for young children is a controversial topic.
Kichik bolalarga uy vazifasi berish — munozarali mavzu.
Could you elaborate on your second point with an example?
Ikkinchi fikringizni misol bilan batafsilroq tushuntirib bera olasizmi?
Your essay is good, but there is still room for improvement.
Inshoingiz yaxshi, lekin uni hali yaxshilash mumkin.
Some dry countries get most of their drinking water from desalination.
Ba'zi qurg'oqchil mamlakatlar ichimlik suvining ko'p qismini tuzsizlantirish orqali oladi.
Most of the river's water is used for irrigation.
Daryo suvining katta qismi sug'orish uchun ishlatiladi.
We sent a questionnaire to two hundred students about their study habits.
O'qish odatlari haqida ikki yuz nafar o'quvchiga so'rovnoma yubordik.

class_ex.title: Kimning fikri?
class_ex.instr: Ustoz gapni o'qiydi; o'quvchi "talaba" yoki "o'qituvchi" deydi va o'qituvchi izohini A/B/C bilan belgilaydi (A It needs to be shorter · B The ideas are difficult to follow · C Some information should be added).
items: "I thought I'd keep the results section very short."
"Your data is fine, but the method section is hard to follow."
"Your list of references is twice the size it should be — reduce it to ten sources."
"The charts look good, but you should add a short example from your own school."
"The ending is clear, but please mention what you would do differently next time."
why: Talabaning o'z rejasi — savol o'qituvchi izohini so'raydi, shuning uchun javob emas.
"fine" — maqtov; "but" dan keyingi qism muhim: hard to follow = difficult to follow.
"twice the size it should be" va "reduce it" = needs to be shorter (paraphrase — "long" so'zi aytilmaydi).
"look good" — maqtov (tuzoq); "but ... add" = information should be added.
"clear" — maqtov; "but please mention ..." = ma'lumot qo'shish kerak. C ikkinchi marta — NB qoidasi.
class_ex.note: Doskada ikki ustun: TALABA | O'QITUVCHI. Faqat o'ng ustun javob beradi. Gaplar audiodan olinmagan, shuning uchun tinglashdan oldin o'ynash xavfsiz; audiodagi iqtiboslarni faqat tekshiruvdan keyin ko'rsating.

listenings.title: Audio 1 — ielts5_27_presentation.mp3 (CD2 Track 21). Fahad's presentation — tutor feedback
intro: Talaba Fahad o'qituvchisi Dr Tyler bilan tuzsizlantirish (desalination) haqidagi taqdimoti rejasini muhokama qiladi. Savol: What comment does the tutor make about each part? Avval 5 qism va 3 izohni o'qing. Keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Write the correct letter, A–C, next to Questions 1–5. NB You may use any letter more than once.
transcript: TUTOR: So, Fahad, let's talk about your presentation. Um, you've done a rough outline, so, er, let's go over it and then you can go away and write it all up.
FAHAD: Sure.
TUTOR: I asked you to choose a topic related to water, and you've chosen desalination – removing salt from seawater. Now, why did you choose that?
FAHAD: Well, I come from the United Arab Emirates, and we have the world's largest desalination plant.
TUTOR: Right, that's very relevant, and I think you should include that – you know, your personal, er, reasons – at the start.
FAHAD: Say why I decided on this topic?
TUTOR: Yes – just give a sentence or two, that'll do.
FAHAD: OK – I mean, I thought I should keep the introduction brief ...
TUTOR: Yes, but you can say why you like the topic ... it's a good choice of topic – very interesting – and then I can follow the introduction easily.
FAHAD: OK.
TUTOR: Now, let's go on to the historical background.
FAHAD: Mm, I want to make it clear that seawater purification isn't a new idea.
TUTOR: No – indeed, that's a good point to make.
FAHAD: So I'm going to describe some of the 'older' methods from the past.
TUTOR: Mmm. I got a bit lost reading your notes here.
FAHAD: Ah-ha. Is it too long?
TUTOR: Well, I think the real problem is that the information isn't in any logical order.
FAHAD: I see ... well, it is just notes.
TUTOR: Well, you start in the 18th century, then move to the present day, then go back to the 20th century.
FAHAD: So it needs reorganising.
TUTOR: Yes, that would help.
FAHAD: OK – I'll make it clearer. What about the description of the process?
TUTOR: Ah, yes, that looks pretty good to me, but we'll go over it in more detail in a moment.
FAHAD: OK. I may need to cut it down.
TUTOR: Yes, definitely – it goes on for a long time and gets a bit technical.
FAHAD: Sure, er ... OK. After the process, I want to talk about the pros and cons of desalination, because that seems to be the big debate.
TUTOR: I totally agree. But you need to sort this section out.
FAHAD: Yes, it is a bit confusing.
TUTOR: I think you should present the main points one at a time.
FAHAD: OK – what, er, the advantages and disadvantages?
TUTOR: Yes, and talk about each one individually.
FAHAD: OK – rather than presenting them all together?
TUTOR: Mmm – it's hard for your listeners to take in like that. It's all a bit unclear at the moment.
FAHAD: I see.
TUTOR: So, lastly, you conclude that we need to look for alternative ways to remove salt from sea water.
FAHAD: Well, yes. Do you think that's the wrong conclusion?
TUTOR: No, no – not at all. However, you should tell your audience exactly why you think this.
FAHAD: I will in the previous section.
TUTOR: Mmm, but you need to summarise the reasons again in the final part of your presentation.
FAHAD: Oh, I see. Right ... I'll mention them briefly, then.
TUTOR: Just a list will do. That'll make the conclusion a better length as well.
FAHAD: OK – thanks very much, Dr Tyler.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5: What comment does the tutor make about each part of the presentation?
tasks.instr: NB You may use any letter more than once. Faqat o'qituvchi izohi.
items: 1 the introduction
2 the background
3 the description of the process
4 the advantages/disadvantages
5 the conclusion
why: "I think you should include that – your personal reasons – at the start ... you can say why you like the topic". Tuzoq: A — talaba "keep the introduction brief" deydi, o'qituvchi esa QO'SHISHni aytadi.
"I got a bit lost reading your notes ... the information isn't in any logical order". Tuzoq: A — talaba "Is it too long?" so'raydi, o'qituvchi "the real problem is..." deb boshqa muammoni aytadi.
"It goes on for a long time and gets a bit technical" — "cut it down". Needs to be shorter.
"It's hard for your listeners to take in ... It's all a bit unclear at the moment". Unclear = difficult to follow.
"You need to summarise the reasons again in the final part ... Just a list will do". Add information (reasons).
tasks.note: Ustoz kaliti: 1 C · 2 B · 3 A · 4 B · 5 C. B va C ikki martadan ishlatilgan — NB qoidasi. 1 va 2-savollarda talaba taklifi (brief, too long) — chalg'ituvchi.
box: A It needs to be shorter.
B The ideas are difficult to follow.
C Some information should be added.

tasks.instr: Talaba nima dedi — o'qituvchi nima dedi?

answers: talaba: "keep it brief" / o'qituvchi: "include your reasons"

talaba: "cut it down" / o'qituvchi: "definitely ... too long, technical"

A (ikkalasi rozi).

listenings.title: Audio 2 — ielts5_27_desalination.mp3 (CD2 Track 22). The desalination process
intro: Fahad va Dr Tyler endi jarayon qismini batafsil ko'rib chiqadi. Avval flow chartni o'qing: har bosqich nomi (Collection, Treatment, Salt removal) — langar. Keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
transcript: TUTOR: OK, so let's have a closer look at the section on the process of desalination.
FAHAD: Well, I just need to outline the principle of the process, don't I?
TUTOR: Uh-huh. Yes, yes. You need to explain first what desalination means.
FAHAD: Well, I want to start by referring to a natural form of desalination ... Um, and to say that a sea bird filters salt out of sea water in its throat.
TUTOR: OK, that's interesting ... so they just spit the salt out, do they?
FAHAD: Yes.
TUTOR: Right, that's a good introduction. Then you can go on to describe the mechanical process.

FAHAD: Yes – well, the first stage is the collection ... um ... it involves a large plant that collects the water – actually, it goes through a canal and that passes the water into the plant, which treats it, you know ...
TUTOR: Removes all the rubbish.
FAHAD: Yes.
TUTOR: So the treatment's the second stage. What happens next?
FAHAD: Well, the next stage is that it goes through a lot of pipes until it reaches the point where the salt is removed.
TUTOR: OK – so that's the next point on your chart ...
FAHAD: Yes – I can talk about this quite a lot ... the salt's separated from fresh water.
TUTOR: Right ... the water passes through a membrane ...
FAHAD: Mmm – not exactly. That's the whole thing. The sea water has to be forced ... er, pumped ... and a lot of pressure is involved.
TUTOR: Mmm – you need to make that point – explain that the water doesn't go freely.
FAHAD: No, because the salt is heavy. This is the really expensive part of the process.
TUTOR: OK ... so after that, what happens?
FAHAD: Well, there's some more treatment after the high-pressure filtering process, but eventually the system produces fresh water.
TUTOR: OK – it might be good to mention what's left over.
FAHAD: Salt, and that's a really big problem ...
TUTOR: Where does it go?
FAHAD: After the desalination process, the substance that remains – it's called brine – it's a very salty substance and it goes back – usually into the sea.
TUTOR: Mmm.
FAHAD: It's not good for fish, though. It damages marine life.
TUTOR: Well, you can discuss that in the next section of your presentation.
FAHAD: Yeah. So, anyway, a lot of the fresh water that's produced is used for human consumption.
TUTOR: Mm, yes, and it's also used for irrigation?
FAHAD: For watering farmland.
TUTOR: Great. Well, you've mentioned some of the disadvantages ...

tasks.title: Questions 6–10: The desalination process — complete the flow chart
why: "A sea bird filters salt out of sea water in its throat". Introductory point — tabiiy tuzsizlantirish.
"A canal ... passes the water into the plant". Tuzoq: "canal" — formada bor.
"This is the really expensive part of the process". Tuzoq: "heavy" — tuz haqida, jarayon emas.
"It's not good for fish, though. It damages marine life". Can harm = not good for / damages.
"Irrigation? — For watering farmland". Irrigating = watering.
tasks.note: Ustoz kaliti: 6 seabird / sea(-)bird · 7 plant · 8 expensive · 9 fish / marine life · 10 farmland / farm(-)land. 8-savol eng yaxshi tuzoq: "heavy" ham, "high pressure" ham eshitiladi — lekin "a very ___ process" ga "expensive" mos.
rows: Introductory point: a (6) can desalinate sea water using its throat.
Collection: sea water passes through a canal into the (7).
Salt removal: sea water passes through a membrane under high pressure; a very (8) process.
Produces fresh water and salty brine – can harm (9).

listenings.title: Audio 3 — ielts5_27_essay.mp3 (boshqa disk, Track 20). Jo's essay on weather control — tutor feedback
listenings.audios: Ustoz bergan audio: ielts5_27_essay.mp3 (boshqa disk, Track 20)
intro: O'qituvchi talaba Jo bilan ob-havoni boshqarish haqidagi inshosini muhokama qiladi. Savol: What comment does the tutor make about each part of the essay? Harflar takrorlanadi. Avval variantlarni o'qing, keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Write the correct letter, A–C, next to Questions 1–5. NB You may use any letter more than once.
transcript: TUTOR: Hello, Jo. Come in and take a seat. I wanted to talk to you about your essay on weather control.
STUDENT: Right. What did you think?
TUTOR: Well, let's start by looking at your introduction. You say that global warming is causing extreme weather conditions around the world.
STUDENT: That's right, isn't it?

TUTOR: Well, you need to be careful here. Yes, there is a lot of evidence that this is the case, but the issue is still controversial. You need to specify that many experts believe this is the case, rather than saying, 'This is how it is.'
STUDENT: OK.
TUTOR: Then you look at the issues surrounding extreme weather, er, and how it has a negative effect in some countries.
STUDENT: I was worried that that section was a bit disorganised.
TUTOR: No, not at all. It's very good, but I was slightly surprised when, in the same paragraph, you mentioned an advantage of extreme weather.
STUDENT: Not the right place for it?

TUTOR: Not really, no. In fact, I would question the need to put it there at all. At one point you're talking about droughts, hurricanes, floods, etc., and then suddenly you're talking about people being able to sunbathe on the beach in January.
STUDENT: Ah, I see what you mean. I think I was going to elaborate on that, add more information, but I guess I forgot to do so.
TUTOR: OK, then there's the section on weather-control programmes. This made interesting reading, but your ideas didn't really lead on from each other. Did you write a plan before you did this?
STUDENT: Er, no.

TUTOR: Well, you really ought to. Here's an example. You talk about experiments to control hurricanes, then you write about rain-making experiments, and then for no apparent reason, you go back to talking about hurricane control.
STUDENT: So, a bit messy?

TUTOR: A bit, yes. Next, you go on to talk about something called 'cloud seeding'. Great, you gave a good, clear explanation about what cloud seeding is, that it's a way of using science and chemistry to make clouds produce rain, and you give some examples of where it's been used.
STUDENT: So, that section's all right?
TUTOR: Ah, well, listen to this. 'The chemical silver nitrate is introduced into clouds to encourage them to produce rain.' Silver nitrate?
STUDENT: Oh, that was careless. I meant silver iodide.
TUTOR: Exactly. I would hate to think what might happen if you started firing silver nitrate into clouds. OK, finally, the conclusion.
STUDENT: I always have problems with the conclusion. I never really know what to say.

TUTOR: Well, you summarise your main points and give a few opinions, which is great, but you then start talking about environmental systems. This was not only in the wrong place, but I couldn't see where it fitted in with the rest of the essay generally.
STUDENT: Right. So, there's a bit of room for improvement, then.

tasks.title: Questions 1–5: What comment does the tutor make about each part of the student's essay?
tasks.instr: NB You may use any letter more than once. Faqat o'qituvchi izohi.
items: 1 the introduction
2 the description of problems caused by the weather
3 the section on weather-control programmes
4 the description of cloud seeding
5 the conclusion
why: "The issue is still controversial. You need to specify that many experts believe this is the case, rather than saying 'This is how it is'". May not be correct.

"I would question the need to put it there at all ... suddenly you're talking about people being able to sunbathe". Not relevant. Tuzoq: A — talaba "a bit disorganised" deydi, o'qituvchi "No, not at all".
"Your ideas didn't really lead on from each other ... for no apparent reason, you go back". Not well organised.
"Silver nitrate? — I meant silver iodide". Noto'g'ri ma'lumot. Tuzoq: "good, clear explanation" — boshida maqtov.
"Talking about environmental systems ... I couldn't see where it fitted in with the rest of the essay". Not relevant.
tasks.note: Ustoz kaliti: 1 B · 2 C · 3 A · 4 B · 5 C. 2-savol eng yaxshi tuzoq: talaba o'zi "disorganised" (A) deydi, o'qituvchi rad etadi va boshqa muammoni (C) aytadi.
box: A It is not well organised.
B It contains information that is not, or may not be, correct.
C It contains information that is not relevant.

tasks.title: Talaba yoki o'qituvchi?
tasks.instr: Talaba nima dedi — o'qituvchi nima dedi?

intro: Jo va o'qituvchi inshodagi bulut ekish (cloud seeding) jarayonini bosqichma-bosqich ko'rib chiqadi. Avval flow chartni o'qing, keyin BIR MARTA tinglang.
Ko'rsatma: Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS for each answer.
transcript: TUTOR: All right, let's go back to the section in your essay on cloud seeding. Apart from your silver nitrate / silver iodide mistake, you've missed a few bits out.
STUDENT: Have I?
TUTOR: I'm afraid so. What I'd like you to do is talk me through the process of cloud seeding, what it involves and so on, and I'll stop you if you've forgotten something. OK?
STUDENT: Fine. Well, first of all silver nitr-, er, iodide is fired into the cloud from the ground using a rocket.
TUTOR: Good, and you could mention that sometimes it's dropped from above by aircraft.
STUDENT: Right, and this is the first stage, the primary stage, which is called static seeding. The silver iodide causes a chemical reaction with the tiny water drops in the cloud, and they freeze.
TUTOR: OK, so you've got millions of tiny ice particles because the water droplets in the cloud freeze. What happens next?
STUDENT: Next, er, there's a process called riming, R-I-M-I-N-G. That's when the ice particles, well, they join up to form bigger pieces of ice, and when they're heavy enough, they fall from the sky.
TUTOR: Good, and then?
STUDENT: Well, as they fall, they turn to rain or snow. And, er, well, that's it, isn't it?
TUTOR: Well, usually, yes, but you've mentioned that there's a first stage, a primary stage, so surely you should have mentioned ...?
STUDENT: Oh, the secondary stage.
TUTOR: Which is known as?
STUDENT: Dynamic seeding, of course, how could I have left that bit out? Let me think. OK, so the water droplets turn to ice, and, er ...
TUTOR: What happens when water freezes? When anything freezes, for that matter. Something that may seem surprising.
STUDENT: Oh, of course, it releases heat.
TUTOR: Exactly, it releases heat. And what can happen to a cloud when freezing water inside it does this?
STUDENT: The cloud gets bigger, and contains even more moisture.
TUTOR: Exactly, and not only do they become bigger, but they also ...?
STUDENT: They, er, produce storms. No, hang on, that's not right. They last longer, that's it.
TUTOR: Right. They last longer, which means they can be seeded again to produce even more rain.

why: "Sometimes it's dropped from above by aircraft". Tuzoq: "rocket" — formada bor.
"A chemical reaction with the tiny water drops in the cloud, and they freeze". "To ___" — fe'l.
"The ice particles ... join up to form bigger pieces of ice". Tuzoq: "particles" — "pieces of ___" dan keyin modda nomi.
"When anything freezes ... it releases heat". Ikki so'z.
"They, er, produce storms. No, hang on, that's not right. They last longer". Tuzatish tuzog'i: "produce storms" — rad etilgan.
tasks.note: Ustoz kaliti: 6 aircraft · 7 freeze · 8 ice · 9 releases heat · 10 last longer. 10-savol — tuzatish tuzog'i ("No, hang on, that's not right").
rows: The chemical silver iodide is introduced into a cloud by a rocket or by (6).
This causes tiny water drops in the cloud to (7), in a process called static seeding.
Lots of very small pieces of (8) join together in a process called riming.
These fall from the sky, turning to rain or snow.
A secondary effect, known as dynamic seeding, occurs when water that freezes (9).
Sometimes this can cause the clouds to grow larger and (10).

intro: Talaba (Jamshid) seminar uchun qog'ozni qayta ishlash jarayonini tushuntirmoqda. Avval flow chartni o'qing, keyin bir marta tinglang.
transcript: JAMSHID: So the process starts when paper is collected from homes and offices and taken to a recycling centre.
TUTOR: Is it all used?
JAMSHID: No — first it's sorted by type, because newspaper and office paper are treated differently.
TUTOR: And then?
JAMSHID: Then it's mixed with water and chemicals in a huge machine called a pulper, which turns it into a soft mixture called pulp.
TUTOR: What about the ink?
JAMSHID: The ink is removed by adding soap and air, which make the ink float to the top, where it's skimmed off.
TUTOR: And finally?
JAMSHID: The clean pulp is spread onto large rollers and dried with heat. The result is new paper, which is mostly used for packaging.

homework_intro: Bugun Part 3 da ikki ishni qildik: o'qituvchining izohini talaba gapidan ajratdik va flow chartni bosqichma-bosqich to'ldirdik — uyda xuddi shu ikkisini yolg'iz o'zingiz bajarasiz.

Birinchi vazifa — 3-Jony skripti "Group presentation on solar energy": avval 1–4 matching va 5–8 flow chartni o'qib chiqing, keyin BIR MARTA tinglang (yoki uydagi birov ovoz chiqarib o'qib bersin) va to'xtatmasdan to'ldiring; 10 daqiqa yetadi, keyin transkript bilan tekshirasiz.

Ikkinchisi — "Talaba — o'qituvchi jadvali": Fahad audiosining (CD2 Track 21) 5 qismi uchun ikki ustun chizasiz, chapga talaba nima dedi, o'ngga o'qituvchi nima dedi, harfni esa faqat o'ng ustunga qarab qo'yasiz; uchinchisi — "O'z flow chartingiz": bitta jarayonni 5 bosqichga bo'lib chizasiz va first, then, after that, finally bilan 5 gap yozasiz; ikkalasi birga 20 daqiqacha.

Eng ko'p uchraydigan xato — talabaning o'z taklifini javob deb olish ("keep the introduction brief" → A) yoki flow chartga formada allaqachon turgan so'zni ("canal", "rocket") yozib qo'yish: javob o'qituvchining bahosidan olinadi va ikki so'zdan oshmaydi.

Uchala vazifani ham keyingi dars boshida daftar ochiq holda stolga qo'yasiz, javoblarni birga tekshiramiz va men har matching javobi uchun "talaba nima dedi, o'qituvchi nima dedi, savol kimni so'raydi?" deb so'rayman.

kahoot.q: Matching instructions say 'NB You may use any letter more than once'. What does this mean?
options: A letter can answer more than one question
Each letter is used for exactly one question
You must write two letters for each question
Letters that are not heard are never used
kahoot.explain: NB qoidasi: bitta harf bir necha savolga javob bo'lishi mumkin, shuning uchun ishlatilgan harfni o'chirmang.

kahoot.q: There are five questions but only three options (A–C). What must be true?
options: At least one letter is used twice
Every letter is used only once
Two of the questions have no answer
Option C is always the last answer
kahoot.explain: 5 savol va 3 harf bo'lsa, kamida bitta harf albatta takrorlanadi.

kahoot.q: The question asks: 'What comment does the TUTOR make?' Whose words give the answer?
kahoot.explain: Savol o'qituvchi izohini so'raydi — talabaning o'z fikri ko'pincha chalg'ituvchi.

kahoot.q: Student: 'I thought the results section was fine.' Tutor: 'Actually, it's far too long.' What is the tutor's comment?
options: It is fine as it is
kahoot.explain: Talabaning fikri emas, o'qituvchi bahosi javob bo'ladi: far too long = needs to be shorter.

kahoot.q: Tutor: 'Your charts are great, but I couldn't follow the order of your points.' Which comment fits?
options: The ideas are hard to follow
The charts need to be improved
kahoot.explain: "but" dan keyingi qism muhim: maqtovdan keyin o'qituvchining haqiqiy izohi keladi.

kahoot.q: Tutor: 'Your method section is fine, but say where your data came from.' Which comment fits?
options: It is not relevant at all
The points are in the wrong order
kahoot.explain: "say where your data came from" — yangi ma'lumot qo'shish kerak, ya'ni C turidagi izoh.

kahoot.q: A speaker says: 'The report is about 20 pages — no, sorry, 25.' What do you write?
kahoot.explain: Tuzatish tuzog'i: "no, sorry" dan keyingi ma'lumot yakuniy javob bo'ladi.

kahoot.q: A flow chart says: 'The mixture is then ______.' What kind of word is most likely needed?
kahoot.explain: "is then ___" — passiv (be + V3): heated, filtered. Grammatika bo'sh joyni bashorat qilishga yordam beradi.

kahoot.q: Instructions: 'Write NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS.' Which answer is NOT acceptable?
kahoot.explain: "the big tank" — uch so'z, chegaradan oshadi; qo'shma so'z (rainwater) bitta so'z hisoblanadi.

kahoot.q: How do the stages in a flow chart usually relate to the recording?
options: They come in the same order
Only the last stage is heard
kahoot.explain: Flow chart bosqichlari audio tartibida keladi — bosqich nomlari langar vazifasini bajaradi.

kahoot.q: A flow chart reads: 'passes through a filter into a ___'. You hear: '...through a filter and into a tank'. What do you write?
kahoot.explain: Formada turgan so'zni (filter) qayta yozmang — bo'sh joyga yangi ma'lumot kerak.

kahoot.q: Which phrase usually tells you that the speaker is moving to the next stage of a process?
kahoot.explain: After that, next, then, finally — bosqich signallari; ular flow chartda qayerdaligingizni ko'rsatadi.

kahoot.q: Your tutor asks you to 'go over' your notes. What should you do?
kahoot.explain: go over — ko'rib chiqmoq, qayta tekshirmoq.

kahoot.q: Your presentation needs to be 'reorganised'. What is the problem?
kahoot.explain: reorganise — qayta tartiblamoq: muammo fikrlarning tartibida.

kahoot.q: Which word is closest in meaning to 'relevant'?
kahoot.explain: relevant — mavzuga tegishli, bog'liq (related).

kahoot.q: What does 'pros and cons' mean?
kahoot.explain: pros and cons — afzallik va kamchiliklar (advantages and disadvantages).

kahoot.q: 'Desalination' is the process of removing ___ from seawater.
kahoot.explain: de- (olib tashlash) + salt (tuz): dengiz suvidan tuzni ajratish.

kahoot.q: A 'controversial' idea is one that ...
kahoot.explain: controversial — munozarali: odamlar bu haqda turlicha fikrda va bahslashadi.

kahoot.q: If you 'summarise' an article, you ...
kahoot.explain: summarise — asosiy fikrlarni qisqacha takrorlamoq.

kahoot.q: Your tutor says your talk is 'too technical'. What does this mean?
kahoot.explain: technical — maxsus atamalarga (jargon) boy, oddiy tinglovchiga tushunish qiyin.

lessons.title: Reading: Passage 2 (Combination)
lessons.grammar_topic: Passage 2 — aralash savollar: Matching headings + Sentence completion + Pick from a list
lessons.book_ref: Jony Academy materiali — ustoz matnlari (#31 The burden of thirst, #32 The rain makers) va mualliflik matnlari.
objectives: Bitta matnda 3 xil savol turini ketma-ket ishlash va vaqtni to'g'ri taqsimlash (Passage 2 — 20 daqiqa).
Qaysi savol turini birinchi ishlashni tanlash: headings — xarita beradi; tartibli turlar — keyin.
Oldingi darslardagi strategiyalarni birlashtirish: headings (10-dars), sentence completion (15-dars), pick from a list (18-dars).
So'z chegarasini har bo'limda qayta o'qish: "ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER" — "TWO WORDS" emas.
Sinfda 4 ta matn (ustozning #31 va #32 matnlari + 2 ta Jony Academy matni: tram, farms), uyda 1 ta ("The Great Green Wall").
materials: Reading #31 "The burden of thirst" matni A–F xatboshilari va 1–13 savollari bilan — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa, javobsiz; i–viii sarlavhalar ro'yxati matn bilan bir varaqda bo'lsin, javob kaliti va tuzoq izohlari faqat ustozda qoladi.

Reading #32 "The rain makers" matni 1–14 savollari bilan (i–ix sarlavhalar, 7–12 sentence completion, 13–14 "Choose TWO") — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa; bu matn IELTS tezligida, vaqt bilan bajariladi, shuning uchun stolda taymer yoki sekundomer tursin.

"The return of the tram" va "Farms without fields" matnlari savollari bilan — har o'quvchiga bittadan nusxa: bu darsda audio yo'q, shuning uchun timeline'dagi 15 daqiqalik bosqich shu ikki matn bilan o'tadi (vaqt yetmasa "Farms without fields" — zaxira, kuchli guruh yoki uyga).

"The Great Green Wall" uy vazifasi varaqasi — har o'quvchiga bitta nusxa, javobsiz; dars oxirida tarqatiladi, orqa tomonida "headings / sentence completion / TFNG uchun necha daqiqa ketdi" deb yoziladigan uchta bo'sh qator qoldiring.

Doskada qo'ng'iroqqacha tayyor tursin: sinf mashqining besh qatorli jadvali — savol turi | qoida | tartib (ALWAYS / USUALLY / NEVER) | eng katta tuzoq (headings, sentence completion, pick from a list, summary, Yes / No / Not Given); yonida Passage 2 vaqt rejasi: headings 7 + sentence completion 8 + pick from a list 3 + tekshirish 2 = 20 daqiqa. Bu ikki ro'yxat dars oxirigacha o'chirilmaydi.

Qirqib tayyorlanadigan kartochkalar: #31 matnining i–viii sarlavhalari alohida tasmalarga qirqilgan — har juftlikka bitta to'plam (A–F xatboshilariga qo'yib ko'riladi, ikkita tasma ortiqcha qoladi); har o'quvchida xatolar daftari, qalam va ikki rangli marker — biri savoldagi kalit so'z, ikkinchisi matndagi paraphrase uchun.
timeline: Salomlashish, o'tgan darsdagi savol turini 3 savolda eslatish
Ustoz doskada: qoida, bosqichlar, tipik xatolar
Savol turiga oid mashq birga bajariladi, har javob izohlanadi

Lug'at so'zlari bilan paraphrase juftlari (scarce — limited, abundant — plentiful, fetch — go and bring back); o'quvchilar ovoz chiqarib topadi. #31 dagi "Find the paraphrases" jadvali javob joyini ochadi — uni faqat #31 tekshiruvidan KEYIN ishlating
1–13: headings → sentence completion → pick from a list, mustaqil; keyin javoblar isbot gap bilan tekshiriladi
"The return of the tram" va "Farms without fields" — mustaqil yoki juftlikda, keyin javoblar isbot bilan tekshiriladi (bu darsda audio yo'q; vaqt yetmasa farms — zaxira)
IELTS tezligida 1–14: headings 7 + sentence completion 8 + pick from a list 3 + tekshirish 2 daqiqa
Xatolar daftari: har xato javob sababi bilan yoziladi
"The Great Green Wall" uyga; xatolar daftari to'ldiriladi

intro: IELTS Reading Passage 2 odatda 13–14 savoldan iborat va 2–3 xil savol turini aralashtiradi. Har tur o'z qoidasi bilan ishlanadi — ularni aralashtirmang.

Tavsiya etilgan tartib: 1) Matching headings — har xatboshini qisqa o'qib sarlavha berasiz, shu bilan butun matnning "xaritasi" paydo bo'ladi. 2) Sentence completion — tartibli (ALWAYS), xaritadan foydalanib tez topiladi. 3) Pick from a list — odatda bitta xatboshiga tegishli.
Headings bo'yicha eslatma: sarlavha — xatboshining ASOSIY g'oyasi. Birinchi va oxirgi gaplarga alohida e'tibor bering. Ro'yxatda ortiqcha sarlavhalar bor.

Sentence completion: ko'rsatmani QAYTA o'qing. Bu darsdagi ikkala ustoz matnida "NO MORE THAN ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER" — ya'ni bitta so'z yoki raqam. "4.7 million" kabi yozuv — bitta raqam, ruxsat etiladi.

Pick from a list: ikkala harf ham matndan isbotlanishi kerak. Savol kimni so'rayotganini (masalan, qishloq aholisi yoki tashkilot) va nima haqida ekanini tekshiring: bajaruvchisi aytilmagan yoki savoldagidan boshqa odamlar qilgan ish — tuzoq.
Vaqt: headings — 7 daqiqa, sentence completion — 8 daqiqa, pick from a list — 3 daqiqa, tekshirish — 2 daqiqa.
presentation: Qaysi turni birinchi ishlayman?
Odatda headings: u matn xaritasini beradi va boshqa savollarni tezlashtiradi.
Headings qiyin bo'lsa-chi?
Uni oxirga qoldiring va avval tartibli turlarni ishlang — matn tanish bo'lgach sarlavha osonlashadi.
"ONE WORD AND/OR A NUMBER" da "15 kilometres" yozsam bo'ladimi?
Ha: bitta raqam + bitta so'z.
Pick from a list ham tartibdami?
Odatda bitta joyga tegishli, lekin tartib kafolatlanmagan.
Bir xatboshiga ikki sarlavha mos kelsa?
Ikkalasini ham xatboshining birinchi va oxirgi gapi bilan solishtiring; asosiy g'oyani tanlang.
Vaqt yetmasa?
Har tur uchun vaqt chegarasi qo'ying; bitta savolga 2 daqiqadan ko'p vaqt sarflamang.
notes: Bu dars — takrorlash va birlashtirish darsi. Ustoz har bo'limdan oldin o'quvchilardan shu turning qoidasini so'raydi (10, 15, 18-darslar).
Kalitlar: #31 (1–13) va #32 (1–14) javoblari "why" ustunida matndan iqtibos bilan berilgan — tekshirishda o'quvchidan isbot gapni so'rang.

#31, 12–13: savol Konso qishloqlari aholisini umumiy so'raydi — yo'lni (A) Orbesho aholisi qurgan, beton va toshni (C) tog'ning narigi tomonidagi qishloqlar aholisi tayyorlagan. Suv omborini kim qurgani aytilmagan (B — tuzoq).
mistakes: Har bo'limda bir xil so'z chegarasi deb o'ylash
Savoldagidan boshqa odamlar qilgan yoki bajaruvchisi aytilmagan ish — tuzoq

how: CORE — shu darsdagi matnlardan olingan 14 ta so'z (birortasi ham javob so'zi emas). Paraphrase bosqichida o'qishdan OLDIN ma'no va sinonimini ayting; dars oxirida har o'quvchi o'z shahri yoki qishlog'idagi suv muammosi haqida 2 ta so'z bilan gap tuzadi.

readings.title: Reading #31. The burden of thirst
readings.qtype: Passage 2: Headings (1–6) + Sentence completion (7–11) + Pick from a list (12–13)
text: Millions of women carry water long distances. If they had a tap by their door, whole societies would be transformed.

A. Aylito Binayo's feet know the mountain. Even at four in the morning, she can run down the rocks to the river by starlight alone and climb the steep mountain back up to her village with a container of water on her back. _She has made this journey three times a day since she was a small child._ So has every other woman in her village of Foro, in the Konso district of south-western Ethiopia in Africa. Binayo left school when she was eight years old, in part because she had to help her mother fetch water from the Toiro River. The water is unsafe to drink; every year that the _drought_ continues, the river carries less water, and its flow is reduced. But it is the only water Foro has ever had.

B. In developed parts of the world, people turn on a tap and out pours abundant, clean water. Yet _nearly 900 million people_ in the world have no access to clean water. Furthermore, _2.5 billion people_ have no safe way to get rid of human waste. Polluted water and lack of proper hygiene cause disease and _kill 3.3 million people_ around the world annually, most of them children. In southern Ethiopia and in northern Kenya, a lack of rain over the past few years has made even dirty water hard to find. But soon, for the first time, things are going to change.

C. Bringing clean water close to villagers' homes is the key to the problem. _Communities where clean water becomes accessible and plentiful are transformed._ All the hours previously spent hauling water can be used to cultivate more _crops_, raise more animals or even start a business. Families spend less time sick or caring for family members who are unwell. Most important, not having to collect water means girls can go to school and get jobs. The need to fetch water for the family, or to take care of younger siblings while their mother goes, usually prevents them ever having this experience.

D. But the challenges of bringing water to remote villages like those in Konso are overwhelming. Locating water underground and then reaching it by means of deep _wells_ requires _geological expertise and expensive, heavy machines_. Abandoned wells and water projects litter the villages of Konso. In similar villages around the developing world, _the biggest problem with water schemes is that about half of them break down_ soon after the groups that built them move on. Sometimes technology is used that can't be repaired locally, or spare parts are available only in the capital.

E. Today, a UK-based international non-profit organisation called WaterAid is tackling the job of bringing water to the most remote villages of Konso. Their approach combines technologies proven to last - such as building a _sand_ dam to capture and filter rainwater that would otherwise drain away. But _the real innovation_ is that WaterAid believes technology is only part of the solution. Just as important is _involving the local community in designing, building and maintaining_ new water projects. Before beginning any project, WaterAid asks the community to create a WASH (water, sanitation, hygiene) committee of seven people. The committee works with WaterAid to plan projects and involve the village in construction. Then it maintains and runs the project.

F. The people of Konso, who grow their crops on terraces they have dug into the sides of mountains, are famous for hard work. In the village of Orbesho, _residents even constructed a road themselves_ so that drilling machinery could come in. Last summer, their pump, installed by the river, was being motorised to push its water to a newly built reservoir on top of a nearby mountain. From there, gravity will carry it down in pipes to villages on the other side of the mountain. Residents of those villages have each given some money to help fund the project. They have _made concrete and collected stones_ for the structures. Now they are digging trenches to lay pipes. _If all goes well_, Aylito Binayo will have a tap with safe water just a three-minute walk from her front door.

the real innovation ... involving the local community

readings.title: Reading #32. The rain makers
readings.qtype: Passage 2: Headings (1–6) + Sentence completion (7–12) + Pick from a list (13–14) — qo'shimcha mashq
text: Science and technology work with nature to bring rain when and where it is needed

A. Wheat farmer Gang Liu is a worried man. The annual rains have not arrived, and there is a danger that unless there is substantial rainfall soon, his annual wheat crop will fail. As he looks anxiously at the clouds which promise rain but are failing to deliver it, there is a sudden loud roar, and from fields for miles around, hundreds of small rockets are fired into the clouds. _Within twenty minutes, the farms around the eastern Chinese city of Luohe are experiencing their first rain for many weeks._ Gang Liu's valuable wheat has been saved, thanks to a technique known as 'cloud seeding', in which the chemical silver iodide (AgI) is introduced into clouds. This causes the tiny drops of moisture in the clouds to turn to ice. These tiny ice particles join until they become heavy enough to fall from the sky, turning into rain as they melt.

B. But did cloud seeding really cause the rain in Luohe to fall, or was it just a coincidence? Experts often question whether cloud seeding actually works. It is hard to tell how _effective_ cloud seeding actually is, they say, as it might have rained anyway, without human intervention. But this has not stopped many governments and organisations from trying. _There are currently 150 weather-modifying projects taking place in more than 40 countries._ Not all of them are aimed at creating rain. The Eastlund Scientific Enterprises Corporation in the USA, for example, is experimenting with firing microwaves into clouds to prevent the tornadoes which cause enormous damage to the country every year. In Russia, experiments have been carried out to make sure the sun shines during important national events.

C. However, it is rainmaking that dominates the research programmes. In many of these, researchers are using trials in which some clouds are 'seeded' while others are not, and both groups are monitored. Arlen Huggins of the Desert Research Institute is leading a research project in Australia. Weather-monitoring _technology_ is so good nowadays, he says, that we can measure clouds much more effectively, even from the inside. As a result, we now know much more about the effect humans can have on the weather. _What Huggins' team has discovered so far is promising._ They believe that cloud seeding does work, although there are still two _years_ of the six-year project left to go.

D. _In China, where the majority of cloud-seeding operations take place_, weather-modification authorities use _army rockets_ to fire silver-iodide particles into the clouds. 39,000 staff working for the China Meteorological Administration (CMA) are equipped with 7,113 army cannons which, in 2006, were used to fire a million silver-iodide rockets into the atmosphere. This costs over $100 million a year, although the CMA claims the results are worth the expense. Between 1999 and 2006, they say, cloud seeding produced 250 billion metric tonnes of rain and prevented thousands of _farmers_ from losing their crops.

E. "We want to understand what makes clouds rain," says Philip Brown of the UK Meteorological office, explaining why so much time, effort and money are being invested. "But there is a more powerful economic reason. A lot of countries around the world are at risk from drought, and governments will try anything to make sure that doesn't happen, even if the scientific evidence is weak. _The potential economic value is greater than the scientific value._ Making it rain might allow you to keep agriculture going where, without human intervention, it might fail."

F. Some people are concerned, however, that altering the weather can have negative consequences. Leonard Barrie, director of the research department at the World Meteorological Organisation in Geneva, explains why. "All areas of weather modification are still very controversial. Some people think that diverting water for irrigation benefits some people, but is a disadvantage to others. _Someone in one area will get more water, but as a result, someone somewhere else could get less._" His fears may be justified. Recently, the town of Zhoukou in China's Henan province accused neighbouring town Pingdingshang of 'stealing' rain from clouds that were due to pass over its own farms, prompting what may be the world's very first documented incident of 'rain rage'.
paraphrases: a period of drought comes to an end
what Huggins' team has discovered so far is promising
why so much time, effort and money are being invested
someone will get more water ... someone else could get less
the majority of operations take place
one area gets more, another gets less

readings.title: The return of the tram
readings.qtype: Passage 2: Headings (A–D) + Sentence completion + True / False / Not Given
text: A. A hundred years ago, almost every large city in Europe and North America had trams. By the 1960s, most of them had disappeared. Cars and buses were seen as modern and flexible, while trams were considered slow, noisy and old-fashioned, and their rails were taken up or simply covered with tarmac.

B. Since the 1980s, however, the tram has made a remarkable comeback. The French city of Nantes opened a new line in 1985, and Strasbourg followed in 1994 with a system that became a model for others. Today more than twenty French cities have trams again, and new lines have opened across Europe, Asia and Africa.

C. There are several reasons for this return. A modern tram line costs far less to build than an underground metro, yet it can carry many more passengers than a bus. Modern trams have low floors, so that people in wheelchairs or with pushchairs can get on easily. They also produce no exhaust fumes in the street, which matters in cities worried about air quality. City planners often use a new tram line to improve the whole street, adding trees, wider pavements and cycle paths.

D. Trams are not a perfect solution. Building a line can close streets for two or three years, which is hard on local shops. And critics point out that modern electric buses can offer many of the same benefits at a much lower cost, without the need for rails. The debate is likely to continue, but for now, in many cities, the sound of the tram bell has come back.

readings.title: Farms without fields
readings.qtype: Passage 2: Headings (A–D) + Sentence completion + Pick from a list
text: A. In a warehouse on the edge of a city, lettuce is growing in towers ten layers high. There is no soil and no sunlight. The plants' roots hang in water containing nutrients, and pink-purple LED lights shine on the leaves eighteen hours a day. This is vertical farming, and supporters believe it could change the way cities are fed.

B. The benefits are impressive. Because the water is recycled, vertical farms can use up to ninety-five percent less water than traditional fields. The plants are grown indoors, so no pesticides are needed, and harvests continue all year round regardless of the weather. Food can be grown close to the people who eat it, which reduces transport and keeps vegetables fresh.

C. The problem is energy. Sunlight is free; LED lights are not. Lighting, heating and cooling a building full of plants requires huge amounts of electricity, and when energy prices rose sharply in 2022, several well-known vertical-farming companies in Europe and the United States closed down.

D. For now, vertical farms grow mostly leafy vegetables and herbs, which grow quickly and sell for a good price. Crops such as wheat or rice would need far too much light to be profitable. Many experts therefore see vertical farming not as a replacement for traditional agriculture, but as one useful addition to it, especially in cities where land is expensive and water is scarce.

readings.title: The Great Green Wall
readings.qtype: Passage 2: Headings (A–D) + Sentence completion + True / False / Not Given
text: A. The Sahel is a long strip of dry land that crosses Africa just south of the Sahara Desert. For decades, its soil has been getting poorer, partly because of drought and partly because of overgrazing and the cutting of trees for fuel. As the land dries, millions of people who depend on farming lose their income.

B. In 2007, the African Union launched an ambitious plan to fight this process: the Great Green Wall. The original idea was a line of trees about 8,000 kilometres long, running from Senegal in the west to Djibouti in the east. The goal was to restore 100 million hectares of damaged land by 2030.

C. Progress has been slower than hoped. A report published in 2020 found that less than a fifth of the target had been reached. Many young trees died because they were planted in the wrong places or were not looked after. Money promised by international donors often arrived late, and conflict in parts of the region made work dangerous.

D. The project has also changed its shape. Instead of a single line of trees, it is now seen as a mosaic of different activities: planting, protecting trees that grow naturally, building small walls of stone to hold rainwater, and helping farmers manage their land. In Niger, farmers who simply protected young trees growing from old roots have brought back millions of hectares of green land — at very low cost.
paraphrases: bring back to a good condition

homework_intro: Bugun bitta matnda uch xil savol turini ketma-ket ishladik va har turga alohida vaqt ajratdik — uyda endi xuddi shu ishni yolg'iz o'zingiz bajarasiz.

Birinchi vazifa — "The Great Green Wall" matni: soatga qarab 15 daqiqa qo'ying, avval A–D xatboshilariga sarlavha tanlang, keyin sentence completionni, oxirida TRUE / FALSE / NOT GIVEN ni ishlang va har javob yoniga matndagi isbot gapni qisqa ko'chirib qo'ying.

Ikkinchisi — "Qoidalar kartasi": beshta savol turiga (headings, sentence completion, pick from a list, summary, Yes / No / Not Given) bittadan kartochka, har birida qoida, tartib va eng katta tuzoq yoziladi; uchinchisi — "Headings xaritasi": "The rain makers" matnining oltita xatboshisiga o'z sarlavhangizni 4–6 so'zda yozib, keyin ro'yxatdagi sarlavha bilan solishtirasiz — ikkalasi birga 20 daqiqacha oladi.

Eng ko'p qilinadigan xato — so'z chegarasini har bo'limda qayta o'qimaslik: bugungi ikkala ustoz matnida bitta so'z edi, "The Great Green Wall"da esa "NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS AND/OR A NUMBER" yozilgan, ya'ni ikki so'zli javob (masalan, "rainy season") ham to'g'ri — ishni boshlashdan oldin har ko'rsatmani boshidan o'qing.

Uchala vazifani ham keyingi dars boshida daftar ochiq holda stolga qo'yasiz: javoblarni birga tekshiramiz va men har bo'limga necha daqiqa ketganini so'rayman — vaqti yozilmagan ish to'liq hisoblanmaydi.
